 * CLOSED AS FIXED IF NEXT.
- `E4.S3`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  They got the message "Cannot invoke method toInteger( ) on null
   object"
   once dropping the ODR part on the pattern editor.
   It is an error only WCA which upgraded WCA from v1.1.1.0 GA code
   to v2.0.0.0 GA.
   When they use WCA 2.0 GA code with reset, this error does not
   occur.
   .
   Here is the steps taken during the migration from 1.1.1 GA.
   1. replace the firmware from v1.1.1.0 GA to v2.0.0.0 GA
   2. upload WAS HV 7.0.0.11 (RHEL) to WCA via
      CLI(cloudburst.virtualimage.create('local path of ova') )and
      Enabled IMP
   3. upload WAS HV 7.0.0.11(SLES) to WCA via CLI and Enabled IMP
   4. tried to create new pattern with ODR part, but failed with
      both RHEL and SLES ODR parts.
- `E4.S4`: LOCAL FIX
 *  reset the GA 2.0 firmware
- `E4.S5`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  Title
- `E4.S6`: The On-Demand Router part is not usable in user interface when a
   WebSphere Cloudburst Appliance is upgraded to 2.0.0.0 and the
   WebSphere Hypervisor Edition with Intelligent Management Pack
   image is imported
- `E4.S7`: Error description
   The problematic scenario is when:
   (1) WebSphere Cloudburst Appliance is upgraded to version
   2.0.0.0
   (2) Then the new WebSphere Hypervisor Edition with the
   Intelligent Management Pack virtual image is imported, the
   license is accepted, and the Intelligent Management pack support
   is enabled.
   (3) Then when you attempt to drag and drop a  On demand router
   part onto the pattern. The pattern no longer can be displayed
   and a "Cannot invoke method toInteger( ) on null object"
   message is displayed.
- `E4.S8`: Local fix
   There is no workaround for this issue.
- `E4.S9`: Problem summary
   ****************************************************************
- `E4.S10`: * USERS AFFECTED:
   Users upgrading a WebSphere CloudBurst Appliance from releases
   prior to 2.0.0.0 to 2.0.0.0, who then import a new WebSphere
   Hypervisor Edition virtual image.
   ****************************************************************
- `E4.S11`: * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:
   In previous releases of WebSphere CloudBurst appliance, the On
   Demand Router part is no included. This is actually two parts,
   an abstract conceptual part, and a specific concrete"part
   associated with a particular WebSphere Hypervisor Edition
   virtual image. The upgrade from WebSphere CloudBurst 2.0.0.0
   does not add the conceptual part to the WebSphere CloudBurst
   Appliance. WebSphere CloudBurst Appliance is unable to construct
   a consistent pattern model, and the message "Cannot invoke
   method toInteger( ) on null object"  is the result.
   ****************************************************************
- `E4.S12`: Problem conclusion
   The WebSphere CloudBurst Appliance 2.0.0.1 upgrade includes the
   addition of the On Demand Router conceptual part to the
   WebSphere Cloudburst appliance.
   If this upgrade is applied, the problem is resolved.
- `E4.S13`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION

- `E5.S1`: efeature; ci; cis; actual; authorized TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Updates to actual CI attributes not being updated in authorized space. Note we are using the Update Promotion eFeature.
- `E5.S3`: SYMPTOM
The original load of classification attributes for the authorized CIs
- `E5.S4`: had misspellings in the attribute names. These "bad" attributes have 
been removed and the correct ones added using the CI Space Loader tool. 
The problem is that the correct attributes are not being added to the 
CIs when they are promoted with the update and copy attributes options 
checked.
- `E5.S5`: Once the attribute names were fixed I tried to recreate the CIs from the Select Action menu. After the operation completed there was no change to the CI in the authorized space.
- `E5.S6`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The key problem is that the CI Space Loader tool is not compatible 
with the Update Promotion eFeature in certain scenarios. In particular, 
if you use the CI Space Loader tool to add CI Attributes to a CI Type 
after CI instances have been created with promotion, the Update 
Promotion eFeature will not work correctly. The problem is that the CI 
Space Loader tool does not use the MBO interface and thus it bypasses 
new logic that has updated the classification MBO with the eFeature. The
supported use case is to add an attribute in the classification 
application. This will go through all CI instances of that CI Type and 
add a blank attribute. You can even choose to copy the value for the 
actual CI attribute if you desire. However, there is a known performance
issue with this function that has been corrected in 7.2. If you have 
more than 5000 CIs of one CI Type, you may experience OOM exceptions. 
The work around is to increase the JVM Memory for this operation.
- `E5.S7`: There are 3 options to correct this:
- `E5.S8`: 1) Try the classification "add attribute" function and consider increasing JVM memory if needed. This is the officially supported way to handle your use case. Note, delete the attribute before trying to add it again.
- `E5.S9`: 2) Delete all of your authorized CIs and then promote again. Do not use 
the CI Space Loader tool to load new attributes and you will not have 
this issue again.
- `E5.S10`: 3) Use a custom written script to add a blank attribute to each CI 
instance. Then update promotion will bring the values over from the 
actual Side.

### techqa_DEV_Q021#row-0099

Question: How to refresh a DataPower WebService Proxy which WSDL got changed? I have made changes to a WSDL stored in DP local filesystem.

How can I make the WSP reflect this change since DataPower Gateway 7.1.0 WebService Proxy WebGUI doesn't offer the "Refresh" button anymore?

Is there a best practice to refresh the WSP if I modified my WSDL?

Reference / gold answer:
To refresh a DataPower Web Service Proxy (WSP) when the WSDL has changed in the local filesystem, you can follow these steps:

1. Disable the WSP service that uses the outdated WSDL.
2. Re-enable the WSP service, which will force DataPower to re-read the configuration and include the changes from the modified WSDL.

Since the WebGUI in DataPower Gateway 7.1.0 no longer offers a "Refresh" button for the WSP, disabling and re-enabling the service is the recommended practice to ensure that the changes in the WSDL are reflected in the WSP configuration.

By following these steps, you can effectively refresh a DataPower WSP when the underlying WSDL has been modified.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `1b`:  You created a Web Service Proxy (WS Proxy) based on a .wsdl file and want to refresh when there are changes in the .wsdl file.
- `1c`: The file is located on the DataPower appliance under the "local" directory.
- `1d`: You created a WSDL Cache Policy to specify the local .wsdl file for the URL Match expression, but the web service proxy state is not being refreshed when there are changes in the file. SYMPTOM
- `1e`: The WSDL Cache Policy is not refreshing from a WSDL in the local:/// directory.
- `1g`: In a WS Proxy, you can refresh WSDL from an URL using WSDL Cache policy.
- `1h`: However, if the WSDL is hosted on the DataPower appliance, such as in local:///, rather than on an external URL, the WSDL Cache Policy does not apply.
- `1i`: For instance, changes made to local:///test.wsdl are not picked up by WS Proxy although there is a WSDL Cache policy setting the URL Match expression to local:///test.wsdl.
- `1j`: This issue was reported to Quality Engineering but it was determined that the DataPower device is working as designed.
- `1k`: The device will not poll WSDL files on the local store.
- `1l`: The WSDL Cache policy works with WSDL files hosted on an external URL.
- `1m`: To refresh a WSDL in the local:/// directory, disable and re-enable the service.

- `E3.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
A WSDL can be retrieved from a Web Service Proxy by allowing the GET method in the HTTP or HTTPS front side handler and going to the URL of the service including "?wsdl" for the query string such as:
- `E3.S4`: http://service:port/uri?wsdl
- `E3.S5`: By default, the GET method is disabled within a Web Service Proxy. If the GET method is not enabled, you will not be able to retrieve the WSDL from the URL.

   WAS51 wsdl2java fails due to a name collision problem in the
   WSDL file.
   Specifically ,a name collision between the complex type name and
   the
   service name.  In this example where both names are "PNInfo":
- `E4.S6`: <xsd:complexType name="PNInfo"> and <wsdl:service name="PNInfo">

   were in conflict.

 *  A simple WORKAROUND, assuming you own the WSDL file,
   would be to change the Service name in the example from
   PNinfo to something else, such as PNInfoService.
   That is, change <wsdl:service name="PNInfo"> to
   <wsdl:service name="PNInfoService">
   and regenerate the web service,
   This workaround assumes you have control over the WSDL for this
   service
   and its is not already  used in production as is.
- `E4.S9`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  All users of WebSphere Application Server   *
   *                  Toolkit v6.1.1 and Rational Application     *
   *                  Developer v7.0                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: The webservice Proxy generation fails   *
   *                      with a NullPointerException due to the  *
   *                      service name and complex type name      *
   *                      being the same in the WSDL.             *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   If a WSDL contains a service that has the same name as a
   complex type then the JAX-RPC webservice proxy generation will
   fail with a NullPointerException.

Support units:
- `E1.S1`: datapower; wsdl cache refresh; wsdl; cache; refresh TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You created a Web Service Proxy (WS Proxy) based on a .wsdl file and want to refresh when there are changes in the .wsdl file. The file is located on the DataPower appliance under the "local" directory. You created a WSDL Cache Policy to specify the local .wsdl file for the URL Match expression, but the web service proxy state is not being refreshed when there are changes in the file.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
The WSDL Cache Policy is not refreshing from a WSDL in the local:/// directory.
- `E1.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In a WS Proxy, you can refresh WSDL from an URL using WSDL Cache policy. However, if the WSDL is hosted on the DataPower appliance, such as in local:///, rather than on an external URL, the WSDL Cache Policy does not apply.
- `E1.S5`: For instance, changes made to local:///test.wsdl are not picked up by WS Proxy although there is a WSDL Cache policy setting the URL Match expression to local:///test.wsdl.
- `E1.S6`: This issue was reported to Quality Engineering but it was determined that the DataPower device is working as designed. The device will not poll WSDL files on the local store.
- `E1.S7`: The WSDL Cache policy works with WSDL files hosted on an external URL.
- `E1.S8`: To refresh a WSDL in the local:/// directory, disable and re-enable the service.

- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You are looking to retrieve a WSDL from a Web Service Proxy service with the IBM WebSphere DataPower XS40 or XI50 appliance
- `E3.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
A WSDL can be retrieved from a Web Service Proxy by allowing the GET method in the HTTP or HTTPS front side handler and going to the URL of the service including "?wsdl" for the query string such as:
- `E3.S4`: http://service:port/uri?wsdl
- `E3.S5`: By default, the GET method is disabled within a Web Service Proxy. If the GET method is not enabled, you will not be able to retrieve the WSDL from the URL.
- `E3.S6`: NOTE: When a WSDL contains include or import references to other documents, the WSDL that is output from DataPower will also contain include or import references. If you are unable to access your complete WSDL or if you find that something is missing when using this method, contact IBM Support [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322] for assistance with troubleshooting the problem.

- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Due to variations in browser rendering capabilities unique to each environment, you might see a noticeable slowdown in browser performance when using the Web interface to view a WS-Proxy configuration containing multiple WSDLs.
- `E4.S3`: CAUSE
 This slowdown is due to the time required to render multiple WSDLs in certain browsers.
- `E4.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To minimize the impact of this issue, consider creating additional WS-Proxies to reduce the number of WSDLs per proxy.

 *  While using the Web Services wizard to create a WAS51 JAX-RPC
   web services client project from
   a WSDL file, the web services Generate Client wizard failed with
   IWAB0014E Unexpected exception occurred.
- `E5.S5`: The proxy for WASv5.1 web service was not able to generated.
   WAS51 wsdl2java fails due to a name collision problem in the
   WSDL file.
   Specifically ,a name collision between the complex type name and
   the
   service name.  In this example where both names are "PNInfo":
- `E5.S6`: <xsd:complexType name="PNInfo"> and <wsdl:service name="PNInfo">
- `E5.S7`: The two PNInfo.java
   (com.cnh.ebom. and com.cnh.ebom.icp.service.)
   were in conflict.
- `E5.S8`: LOCAL FIX
 *  A simple WORKAROUND, assuming you own the WSDL file,
   would be to change the Service name in the example from
   PNinfo to something else, such as PNInfoService.
   That is, change <wsdl:service name="PNInfo"> to
   <wsdl:service name="PNInfoService">
   and regenerate the web service,
   This workaround assumes you have control over the WSDL for this
   service
   and its is not already  used in production as is.
- `E5.S9`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  All users of WebSphere Application Server   *
   *                  Toolkit v6.1.1 and Rational Application     *
   *                  Developer v7.0                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: The webservice Proxy generation fails   *
   *                      with a NullPointerException due to the  *
   *                      service name and complex type name      *
   *                      being the same in the WSDL.             *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   If a WSDL contains a service that has the same name as a
   complex type then the JAX-RPC webservice proxy generation will
   fail with a NullPointerException.
- `E5.S10`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The error was happening because the complex type name and
   service name were being used directly from the WSDL when it
   should come from the JAX-RPC mapping file since the underlying
   WAS webservice emitter will change the names.

### techqa_DEV_Q022#row-0053

Question: where is the websphere application server 9.0.0.4 fix for developers I am using the was 9.0.0.0 in rad/rsa 9.6.1 for Windows. I cannot upgrade to the 9.0.0.4 fixpack, because there is no developer edition. On the downloadpage there are Base, Network Deployment, DMZ Secure Proxy Server and IBM Web Enablement for IBM i, but no Developers! See link text For was 8.5.5.10 there exists a developers edition. Where can I download the Websphere Application Server fix pack 9.0.0.4 Developers?

Reference / gold answer:
The WebSphere Application Server fix pack 9.0.0.4 Developers edition is not available for download. The fix pack provided in the context is specifically for the Edge Caching Proxy component of WebSphere Application Server and does not include a separate edition for developers. The available editions listed are Base, Network Deployment, DMZ Secure Proxy Server, and IBM Web Enablement for IBM i. If you are using RAD/RSA 9.6.1 with WAS 9.0.0.0, you may not be able to upgrade to the 9.0.0.4 fix pack specifically for developers.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `0b`:  The Edge Caching Proxy component of WebSphere Application Server may be vulnerable to an HTTP response splitting attack.
- `0c`: This is a separate install from WebSphere Application Server.
- `0d`: You only need to apply this if you use the Edge Caching Proxy. VULNERABILITY DETAILS
- `0k`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
- `0l`: IBM WebSphere Application Server Edge Caching Proxy Version 7.0, 8.0, 8.5, & 9.0 REMEDIATION/FIXES
- `0m`: The recommended solution is to apply the Fix Pack or PTF for each named product as soon as practical. Fix:
- `0n`: Apply an Interim Fix, Fix Pack or PTF containing APAR PI82587 if you use the Edge Caching Proxy component (separate install from WebSphere Application Server) as noted below: [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980]
- `0o`: For IBM WebSphere Application Server
- `0p`: For V9.0.0.0 through 9.0.0.4:
- `0q`:  * Upgrade to 9.0.0.3 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `0r`: -- OR  * Upgrade to 9.0.0.4 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `0s`: -- OR  * Apply Fix Pack 5 (9.0.0.5), or later.
- `0z`: For more details about WAS fixpack refer to link http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815] WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
- `0aa`: Mitigation is to apply relevant WAS fixpack.
- `0ab`: For more detail refer to link http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815]

- `E1.S1`: V7Rnotes PRODUCT DOCUMENTATION
- `E1.S2`: ABSTRACT
 This document describes how to download IBM WebSphere Application Server for Developers Version 7.0 for Windows installation images from the IBM Passport Advantage Online Web site.
- `E1.S3`: CONTENT
IBM WebSphere Application Server is the premier Java™ Platform, Enterprise Edition (Java EE) and Web services-based application server. WebSphere Application Server is built on open standards and helps you deploy and manage applications ranging from simple Web sites to powerful on-demand solutions.
- `E1.S4`: More information
To access a wide variety of technical resources for this product, see the Information Centers for WebSphere Application Server Version 7.0 [http://www14.software.ibm.com/webapp/wsbroker/redirect?version=compass&product=was-base-dist&].
- `E1.S5`: Space requirements
- `E1.S6`: * 800 MB of disk space to store the required downloadable parts plus 900 MB of disk space to unpack the parts. 
 * 1 GB (1000 MB) of disk space to install the product without profiles and 1.25 GB (1250 MB) for a cell installation. 
 * 30 MB of space in the tmp directory to run the installation program. 
 * For more detailed information, see the WebSphere Application Server detailed system requirements [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27006921] document.

- `E3.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Customers see different content in the Rational Application Developer (RAD) Websphere Application Server (WAS) download compared to prior RAD releases.
- `E3.S3`: During install of this new WAS ILAN version, customers now see explicit wording saying this a no cost, non-supported and non-warranted version of WebSphere Application Server traditional. While this has always been the case for this developer version, refer to evaluation software page & FAQ below, seeing these words during install may be a new information for some users.
- `E3.S4`: CAUSE
New WAS packaged in RAD:
- `E3.S5`: Rational Application Developer for WebSphere packages WebSphere Application Server for development and test purposes. WAS recently renamed WAS for Developers (WAS4D) to WAS ILAN (see here [https://developer.ibm.com/wasdev/downloads/#asset/WAS_traditional_for_Developers]). In response to this change, RAD 9.6 now packages WAS ILAN available in the RAD_WS_9.6_WASTE_9.0.zip file. It has the same capabilities and updates that RAD users expect.
- `E3.S6`: Support for this new WAS packaged in RAD:
New message during installation has worried users, however, users with an active support contract for their production WebSphere Application Server are entitled for support on the developer machine as long as an active support contract is in place for the production server.
- `E3.S7`: * Evaluation software page: https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/index.html [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/index.html] 
 * FAQ: https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/faq-wasdevelopers.html [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/faq-wasdevelopers.html]
- `E3.S8`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To change/upgrade RAD 9.6 WAS4D to WAS ILAN.
- `E3.S9`: Add the following repository to Installation Manager: https://www.ibm.com/software/repositorymanager/com.ibm.websphere.ILAN.v90/ [https://www.ibm.com/software/repositorymanager/com.ibm.websphere.ILAN.v90/]
- `E4.S1`: Description File name WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client in a stand-alone environment image_xs_client.8500.zip WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client for WebSphere Application Server Version 6 image_xs_client_was6.8500.zip WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client for WebSphere Application Server Version 7 image_xs_client_was7.8500.zip WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client for WebSphere Application Server Version 8 image_xs_client_was8.8500.zip 
     2. Install IBM Installation Manager [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24031300]. 
     3. Use Installation Manager to install the product from the product repositories that you downloaded in step 1.

- `E5.S1`: CVE-2017-1503; WAS security SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E5.S2`: SUMMARY
 The Edge Caching Proxy component of WebSphere Application Server may be vulnerable to an HTTP response splitting attack. This is a separate install from WebSphere Application Server. You only need to apply this if you use the Edge Caching Proxy.
- `E5.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2017-1503 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-1503]
DESCRIPTION: IBM WebSphere Application Server is vulnerable to HTTP response splitting attacks. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using specially-crafted URL to cause the server to return a split response, once the URL is clicked. This would allow the attacker to perform further attacks, such as Web cache poisoning, cross-site scripting, and possibly obtain sensitive information.
CVSS Base Score: 6.1
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/129578 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/129578] for the current score
- `E5.S4`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
IBM WebSphere Application Server Edge Caching Proxy Version 7.0, 8.0, 8.5, & 9.0
- `E5.S5`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
The recommended solution is to apply the Fix Pack or PTF for each named product as soon as practical.
- `E5.S6`: Fix: 
Apply an Interim Fix, Fix Pack or PTF containing APAR PI82587 if you use the Edge Caching Proxy component (separate install from WebSphere Application Server) as noted below: [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980]
- `E5.S7`: For IBM WebSphere Application Server 
For V9.0.0.0 through 9.0.0.4:
- `E5.S8`: * Upgrade to 9.0.0.3 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `E5.S9`: -- OR  * Upgrade to 9.0.0.4 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `E5.S10`: -- OR  * Apply Fix Pack 5 (9.0.0.5), or later.
- `E5.S11`: For V8.5.0.0 through 8.5.5.12:  * Upgrade to 8.5.5.11 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `E5.S12`: -- OR  * Upgrade to 8.5.5.12 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `E5.S13`: -- OR  * Apply Fix Pack 13 (8.5.5.13), or later (targeted availability 5 February 2018).
- `E5.S14`: For V8.0.0.0 through 8.0.0.1 3:  * Apply Fix Pack 14 (8.0.0.14), or later.
- `E5.S15`: For V7.0.0.0 through 7.0.0.43:  * Upgrade to a minimum of 7.0.0.41 fix pack level then apply Interim Fix [http://www-933.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/selectFixes?parent=ibm%2FWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/WebSphere+Application+Server&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=8.5.5-WS-EDGECP-FP00000071&includeSupersedes=0]PI82587 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24044131]
- `E5.S16`: -- OR  * Apply Fix Pack 45 (7.0.0.45), or later (targeted availability 2Q 2018).
- `E5.S17`: For more details about WAS fixpack refer to link http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815] WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
Mitigation is to apply relevant WAS fixpack. For more detail refer to link http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg22006815]

Visible answer:
In RAD 9.6, the developer version was renamed from WebSphere Application Server for Developers (WAS4D) to WAS ILAN. RAD 9.6 packages WAS ILAN in the RAD_WS_9.6_WASTE_9.0.zip file, with the same capabilities and updates expected by RAD users. [E3.S5]

To change or upgrade the RAD 9.6 WAS4D installation to WAS ILAN, add this repository to IBM Installation Manager: https://www.ibm.com/software/repositorymanager/com.ibm.websphere.ILAN.v90/ [E3.S8] [E3.S9]

For WebSphere Application Server 9.0.0.0 through 9.0.0.4, the documented options are to upgrade to 9.0.0.3 and apply Interim Fix PI82587, upgrade to 9.0.0.4 and apply that interim fix, or apply Fix Pack 5 (9.0.0.5) or later. [E5.S7] [E5.S8] [E5.S9] [E5.S10]

- `E1.S2`: ABSTRACT
 This document describes how to download IBM WebSphere Application Server for Developers Version 7.0 for Windows installation images from the IBM Passport Advantage Online Web site.
- `E1.S3`: CONTENT
IBM WebSphere Application Server is the premier Java™ Platform, Enterprise Edition (Java EE) and Web services-based application server. WebSphere Application Server is built on open standards and helps you deploy and manage applications ranging from simple Web sites to powerful on-demand solutions.
- `E1.S4`: More information
To access a wide variety of technical resources for this product, see the Information Centers for WebSphere Application Server Version 7.0 [http://www14.software.ibm.com/webapp/wsbroker/redirect?version=compass&product=was-base-dist&].
- `E1.S5`: Space requirements
- `E1.S6`: * 800 MB of disk space to store the required downloadable parts plus 900 MB of disk space to unpack the parts. 
 * 1 GB (1000 MB) of disk space to install the product without profiles and 1.25 GB (1250 MB) for a cell installation. 
 * 30 MB of space in the tmp directory to run the installation program. 
 * For more detailed information, see the WebSphere Application Server detailed system requirements [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27006921] document.
- `E1.S7`: Downloading and assembling the product  1. Navigate your browser to the Find Downloads and Media [http://www-112.ibm.com/software/howtobuy/passportadvantage/paocustomer/sdma/SDMA?PO=DOWNLOAD_FIND_BY_PART_NUMBER] Web page on the IBM Passport Advantage Online Web site. 
 2. Select the Find by part number search option under Download finder options. 
 3. Search for each downloadable image by part number. 
 4. Download all of the required parts. 
 5. Use a file extracting utility that supports large file extractions to unpack each of the parts into a single, temporary directory on your system. 
 6. Open the Quick Start Guide, which is located on the Quick Start CD. Follow step three through step nine of the Quick Start Guide to access the documentation to help with product installation.

- `E3.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Customers see different content in the Rational Application Developer (RAD) Websphere Application Server (WAS) download compared to prior RAD releases.
- `E3.S3`: During install of this new WAS ILAN version, customers now see explicit wording saying this a no cost, non-supported and non-warranted version of WebSphere Application Server traditional. While this has always been the case for this developer version, refer to evaluation software page & FAQ below, seeing these words during install may be a new information for some users.
- `E3.S4`: CAUSE
New WAS packaged in RAD:
- `E3.S5`: Rational Application Developer for WebSphere packages WebSphere Application Server for development and test purposes. WAS recently renamed WAS for Developers (WAS4D) to WAS ILAN (see here [https://developer.ibm.com/wasdev/downloads/#asset/WAS_traditional_for_Developers]). In response to this change, RAD 9.6 now packages WAS ILAN available in the RAD_WS_9.6_WASTE_9.0.zip file. It has the same capabilities and updates that RAD users expect.
- `E3.S6`: Support for this new WAS packaged in RAD:
New message during installation has worried users, however, users with an active support contract for their production WebSphere Application Server are entitled for support on the developer machine as long as an active support contract is in place for the production server.
- `E3.S7`: * Evaluation software page: https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/index.html [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/index.html] 
 * FAQ: https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/faq-wasdevelopers.html [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/downloads/ws/wasdevelopers/faq-wasdevelopers.html]
- `E3.S8`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To change/upgrade RAD 9.6 WAS4D to WAS ILAN.
- `E3.S9`: Add the following repository to Installation Manager: https://www.ibm.com/software/repositorymanager/com.ibm.websphere.ILAN.v90/ [https://www.ibm.com/software/repositorymanager/com.ibm.websphere.ILAN.v90/]
- `E4.S1`: CVE-2017-1503; WAS security SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E4.S2`: SUMMARY
 The Edge Caching Proxy component of WebSphere Application Server may be vulnerable to an HTTP response splitting attack. This is a separate install from WebSphere Application Server. You only need to apply this if you use the Edge Caching Proxy.
- `E4.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2017-1503 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2017-1503]
DESCRIPTION: IBM WebSphere Application Server is vulnerable to HTTP response splitting attacks. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using specially-crafted URL to cause the server to return a split response, once the URL is clicked. This would allow the attacker to perform further attacks, such as Web cache poisoning, cross-site scripting, and possibly obtain sensitive information.
CVSS Base Score: 6.1
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/129578 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/129578] for the current score
- `E4.S4`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
IBM WebSphere Application Server Edge Caching Proxy Version 7.0, 8.0, 8.5, & 9.0
- `E4.S5`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
The recommended solution is to apply the Fix Pack or PTF for each named product as soon as practical.
- `E4.S6`: Fix: 
Apply an Interim Fix, Fix Pack or PTF containing APAR PI82587 if you use the Edge Caching Proxy component (separate install from WebSphere Application Server) as noted below: [https://www-304.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980]

### techqa_DEV_Q030#row-0111

Question: For HP-UX how to write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout? A customer asked why no gc logs generated even if they use the -Xverbosegc option. So How can I write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout for HP-UX? 

Reference / gold answer:
To write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout for HP-UX, you would need to add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments:

-XX:+PrintGCDetails 
-XX:+PrintGCDateStamps 
-XX:+PrintHeapAtGC 
-Xverbosegc:file=/tmp/gc_pid$$.vgc 

Additionally, to enable log file rotation, you should include the following parameters:
-XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation
-XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10
-XX:GCLogFileSize=10M 

These settings will allow you to write verbose gc output to a log file other than native_stdout on HP-UX and generate gc logs as needed.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `1m`: Add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC -Xverbosegc:file= /tmp/gc_pid$$.vgc
- `1n`: To enable log file rotation: -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10 -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M

- `E2.S1`: analysis verbose gc output; MustGatherDocument TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Verbose GC data gives an insight into the actions that the Garbage Collector is taking, and is vital for performance tuning.
In addition it is one means of determining if the application is "leaking" Java objects, and what size leak has occurred which is useful when carrying out heapdump analysis.
- `E2.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Once the generation of Verbose GC output has been setup [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222436] and the output gathered, it is possible to carry out analysis of the data.
This can be carried out in one of two ways:
- `E2.S4`: * Using a Visualisation tool 
 * Manual Analysis by reading the XML log file
- `E2.S5`: Visulization Tools There are currently two publically available tools that are capable of analyzing the Verbose GC output:
- `E2.S6`: * Diagnostic Tool for Java Garbage Collector: http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/gcdiag [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/gcdiag] 
 * IBM Pattern Modeling and Analysis Tool for Java Garbage Collector (PMAT): http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/pmat [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/pmat]
- `E2.S7`: Manual Analysis The Verbose GC output that is received is dependent on which of the following three Garbage Collection strategies is in place:
- `E2.S8`: * -Xgcpolicy:optthruput Optimum Throughput [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222443] 
 * -Xgcpolicy:optavgpause Concurrent GC [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222459] 
 * -Xgcpolicy:gencon Generational and Concurrent [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222486]
- `E2.S9`: It is recommended that a visualization tool is used to develop an overview of the Garbage Collector activity and trends, and then carry out manual analysis for Garbage Collection cycles of particular interest. RELATED INFORMATION
 Optimum Through Put [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21222443]

Generational and Concurrent [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21222486]

PMAT [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/PMAT]

- `E3.S1`: mustgather; must gather; data collection; source control; rtc; scm; SCM Web UI; SCM Eclipse Client; SCM CLI; trace TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 How to collect the data necessary to diagnose and resolve IBM Rational Team Concert (RTC) source control issues.
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
This MustGather will assist you in collecting the data necessary to help you diagnose and resolve the issue. If you are unable to determine the root cause using the information collected, you should open a PMR with IBM Support [http://www.ibm.com/contact] for further investigation providing the data collected.
- `E3.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
You can use the IBM Support Assistant Lite (ISA Lite) Data Collector tool [https://jazz.net/help-dev/clm/index.jsp?re=1&topic=/com.ibm.team.concert.doc/topics/t_using_the_isal.html] to quickly collect diagnostic files, such as log files, configuration files or to run traces. This tool is bundled with RTC 4.x and above. ISA Lite collects information about your Jazz Team Server environment and stores the information in a .zip archive file. If you have a need to open a service request with IBM Support [http://www.ibm.com/contact] for further assistance, you can send the archive file with the data collection so that they can help diagnose and fix problems.

- `E4.S1`: wasrun; wasjdk; open; files; too; ProblemDeterminationDocument; JCC was appserver app server TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 This technote explains how to debug the "Too many open files" error message on Microsoft Windows, AIX, Linux and Solaris operating systems.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following messages could be displayed when the process has exhausted the file handle limit:
- `E4.S4`: java.io.IOException: Too many open files
- `E4.S5`: [3/14/15 9:26:53:589 EDT] 14142136 prefs W Could not lock User prefs. Unix error code 24.
- `E4.S6`: New sockets/file descriptors can not be opened after the limit has been reached.
- `E4.S7`: CAUSE
System configuration limitation.
- `E4.S8`: When the "Too Many Open Files" error message is written to the logs, it indicates that all available file handles for the process have been used (this includes sockets as well). In a majority of cases, this is the result of file handles being leaked by some part of the application. This technote explains how to collect output that identifies what file handles are in use at the time of the error condition.
- `E4.S9`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E4.S10`: Determine Ulimits
- `E4.S11`: On UNIX and Linux operating systems, the ulimit for the number of file handles can be configured, and it is usually set too low by default. Increasing this ulimit to 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime, but this depends on your applications and your file/socket usage. Additionally, file descriptor leaks can still occur even with a high value.
- `E4.S12`: Display the current soft limit:
ulimit -Sn
- `E4.S13`: Display the current hard limit:
ulimit -Hn
- `E4.S14`: Or capture a Javacore, the limit will be listed in that file under the name NOFILE:
kill -3 PID
- `E4.S15`: Please see the following document if you would like more information on where you can edit ulimits:
Guidelines for setting ulimits (WebSphere Application Server)
http://www.IBM.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21469413 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21469413]
- `E4.S16`: Operating Systems
- `E4.S17`: Windows By default, Windows does not ship with a tool to debug this type of problem. Instead Microsoft provides a tool that you can download called Process Explorer [http://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896653]. This tool identifies the open handles/files associated with the Java™ process (but usually not sockets opened by the Winsock component) and determines which handles are still opened. These handles result in the "Too many open files" error message.
- `E4.S18`: To display the handles, click on the Gear Icon [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&amp;aid=1] in the toolbar (or press CTRL+ H to toggle the handles view). The icon will change to the icon for DLL files (so you can toggle it back to the DLL view).
- `E4.S19`: It is important that you change the Refresh Rate. Select View > Update Speed, and change it to 5 seconds.
- `E4.S20`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&aid=2]
- `E4.S21`: There is also another Microsoft utility called Handle that you can download from the following URL: 
https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896655.aspx [https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896655.aspx]
- `E4.S22`: This tool is a command line version of Process Explorer. The URL above contains the usage instructions.
- `E4.S23`: AIX 
The commands lsof and procfiles are usually the best commands to determine what files and sockets are opened..
- `E4.S24`: lsof 
To determine if the number of open files is growing over a period of time, issue lsof to report the open files against a PID on a periodic basis.
- `E4.S25`: with the -r option to capture multiple intervals: 
lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E4.S26`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.
- `E4.S27`: HP-UX 
lsof 
lsof -p [ PID ] > lsof.out
- `E4.S28`: This will get one round of lsof output. If you want to determine if the number of open files is growing over time, you can issue the command with the -r option to capture multiple intervals: 
lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E4.S29`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
On HP-UX, verbose GC is not written to a log file by default; this must be configured. [E1.S3]

Add the following generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC -Xverbosegc:file=/tmp/gc_pid$$.vgc [E1.S14]

To enable log rotation, also add -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation, -XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10, and -XX:GCLogFileSize=10M. [E1.S15]

- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 How can I write verbose gc output to a log file other than the native_stdout?
- `E1.S3`: CAUSE
By default, Solaris and HP-UX do not write verbose GC to a log file. This must be configured.
- `E1.S4`: ANSWER
- `E1.S5`: WAS 8.5.0.2 (and higher), WAS 8.0.0.6 (and higher), WAS 7.0.0.27 (and higher):
- `E1.S6`: Solaris:
Add the following parameters to the generic JVM arguments:
- `E1.S7`: -XX:+PrintGCDetails 
-XX:+PrintGCDateStamps 
-XX:+PrintHeapAtGC 
-Xloggc:/tmp/gc.log
- `E1.S8`: To enable log file rotation:
-XX:+UseGCLogFileRotation
-XX:NumberOfGCLogFiles=10
-XX:GCLogFileSize=10M
- `E1.S9`: notes:

- `E1.S10`: * ex: -Xloggc:/tmp/gc.log
- `E1.S11`: -XX:+UseGCLogFileRotati o n  * Enabled GC log rotation, requires -Xloggc
- `E1.S12`: -XX:NumberOfGClogFiles= <num_of_files>  * Set the number of files to use when rotating logs, must be >= 1. The rotated log files will use the following naming scheme, <filename>.0, <filename>.1, ..., <filename>.n-1.
- `E1.S13`: -XX:GCLogFileSize=<number>K (or M)  * The size of the log file at which point the log will be rotated, must be >= 8K.

- `E2.S2`: QUESTION

- `E2.S3`: ANSWER
This document explains how to correlate data from the MustGather below which utilizes GlancePlus: [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=0&uid=swg21166017]
- `E2.S4`: * MustGather: Performance, Hang, or High CPU Issues on HP-UX [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21127574]
- `E2.S5`: The following files will be used to determine the thread that has high CPU:  * hpux_glance.out

- `E2.S9`: 1. The hpux_glance.sh script outputs 13 times every 25 seconds and tracks CPU usage. Each section is separated by a timestamp. CPU usage is indicated in the cpu% column. By default it displays only java processes/threads.
- `E2.S10`: 2. The pid column contains the process ID. If the PID is for an application server, the 
<SERVER_NAME>.pid contains the matching PID. You can find this file in the server logs directory. In the above example, the PID is 11671.
- `E2.S11`: 3. The ktid column identifies an individual thread. In this example, the thread 5551377 is utilizing 82% of the CPU.

- `E3.S1`: analysis verbose gc output; MustGatherDocument TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Verbose GC data gives an insight into the actions that the Garbage Collector is taking, and is vital for performance tuning.
In addition it is one means of determining if the application is "leaking" Java objects, and what size leak has occurred which is useful when carrying out heapdump analysis.
- `E3.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Once the generation of Verbose GC output has been setup [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222436] and the output gathered, it is possible to carry out analysis of the data.
This can be carried out in one of two ways:
- `E3.S4`: * Using a Visualisation tool 
 * Manual Analysis by reading the XML log file
- `E3.S5`: Visulization Tools There are currently two publically available tools that are capable of analyzing the Verbose GC output:
- `E3.S6`: * Diagnostic Tool for Java Garbage Collector: http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/gcdiag [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/gcdiag] 
 * IBM Pattern Modeling and Analysis Tool for Java Garbage Collector (PMAT): http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/pmat [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/pmat]
- `E3.S7`: Manual Analysis The Verbose GC output that is received is dependent on which of the following three Garbage Collection strategies is in place:
- `E3.S8`: * -Xgcpolicy:optthruput Optimum Throughput [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222443] 
 * -Xgcpolicy:optavgpause Concurrent GC [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222459] 
 * -Xgcpolicy:gencon Generational and Concurrent [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=727&uid=swg21222486]
- `E3.S9`: It is recommended that a visualization tool is used to develop an overview of the Garbage Collector activity and trends, and then carry out manual analysis for Garbage Collection cycles of particular interest. RELATED INFORMATION
 Optimum Through Put [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21222443]
Concurrent GC [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21222459]
Generational and Concurrent [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21222486]
Diagnostic Tool for Java Garbage Collector [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/gcdiag]
PMAT [http://www.alphaworks.ibm.com/tech/PMAT]
HeapDump Analysis [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21222458]
- `E4.S1`: java java mime adapter class jca turn on jni layer trace mustgather jni jni trace trace trace TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When using any of the WebSphere® Transformation Extender (WTX) Java™ based adapters, you can better troubleshoot problems by turning on the Java Native Interface layer (JNI) trace.
- `E4.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
The JNI layer trace can be turned on in the configuration file found in the WTX installation directory. The configuration file name differs by version.
- `E4.S4`: Version File Name 8.1, 8.2, 8.3 dtx.ini 
The configuration file contains a section named [JNI Layer Trace].
- `E4.S5`: [JNI Layer Trace]
;switch=off
;file=
- `E4.S6`: These instructions will assist you in changing the configuration file so that a trace file is created. 
 1. Find the [JNI Layer Trace] section in the configuration file. 
 2. Uncomment (delete the semicolon [ ; ] from the front of the line) the switch option. 
 3. Change the switch option from "off" to "on". 
 4. Uncomment the file option. 
 5. Add a complete path and file name to the file option.

On HP-UX, verbose GC is not written to a log file by default; configure it in the server’s generic JVM arguments. [E1.S3] [E1.S14]

Add these generic JVM arguments: -XX:+PrintGCDetails, -XX:+PrintGCDateStamps, -XX:+PrintHeapAtGC, and -Xverbosegc:file=/tmp/gc_pid$$.vgc. [E1.S14]

### techqa_DEV_Q052#row-0110

Question: Why do I still get "certificate expired" error after adding new certificate? 

The remote SSL vendor has provided us a new certificate to replace an expiring one. We have added the new certificate to the appropriate Datapower validation credential, however, connections are still failing with "certificate expired":

mpgw(Inbound_MPG): tid(51005)[request][10.20xx.xx] gtid(51345): certificate validation failed for '/C=US/O=People Services/OU=IT/CN=test.site.com' against 'My_ValCred': certificate has expired

Reference / gold answer:
The error message "certificate expired" suggests that the DataPower appliance is still using the old/expired certificate for validation instead of the new one you added. Here are some possible reasons why the new certificate might not be used even after adding it:

1. The new certificate was not properly loaded into the keystore: Double-check that the new certificate was correctly loaded into the appropriate keystore and that the keystore configuration has been updated to use the new certificate for validation.

2. Keystore reference: Ensure that the validation credential configuration in DataPower is correctly referencing the updated keystore that contains the new certificate. Sometimes, the appliance may still be configured to use the old keystore, leading to the validation failure.

3. Cache issue: DataPower might be caching the old certificate information. Try restarting the DataPower appliance to clear any cached references to the old certificate and force it to use the new one.

4. Insufficient permissions: Verify that the user running the DataPower appliance has the necessary permissions to read and use the new keystore and certificates. Insufficient permissions could prevent the appliance from accessing the new certificate data.

5. Configuration error: Review the DataPower configuration settings to ensure that all changes related to the new certificate are correctly made. It's possible that there could be a misconfiguration that is causing the appliance to continue using the expired certificate.

By addressing these potential issues and ensuring that the new certificate is correctly loaded, referenced, and accessible by the DataPower appliance, you should be able to resolve the "certificate expired" error.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `2a`: certificate validation expired TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING) PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
- `2b`:  DataPower firmware 3.8.1 and prior versions do not support certificate validation involving non-unique Distinguished Names. SYMPTOM
- `2c`: A Validation Credential object configured with multiple Certificate Authority certificates containing identical subject DNs but different key material may fail to validate incoming certificates that have been signed with one of the issuer certificates. CAUSE
- `2d`: DataPower searches the certificate list based on subject DN and attempts to validate against the first certificate that it finds with the given DN.
- `2e`: If the initial attempt fails, the certificate validation will fail. ENVIRONMENT
- `2i`: If there is more than one certificate with the same subject DN, this may be the issue.
- `2j`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM

- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 What is the procedure for replacing an expiring certificate that is in use on the DataPower appliance with a newly obtained certificate?
- `E2.S3`: CAUSE
Once you have obtained a new certificate from your certificate authority and are ready to replace the expiring one currently in use by your DataPower configuration with this new certificate, there is no single prescribed manner in which to perform the replacement operation. The following information presents some options for formulating an approach that best fits your environment.
- `E2.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
First, know your certificate material. It's not uncommon for newer certificates to be chained, so it is not a one for one replacement; the existing certificate on the DataPower appliance may need to be replaced by more than one certificate. Therefore, it is important to ensure you have the full certificate chain, as appropriate (i.e, the personal, intermediate and root certificates). Certificate authorities may send two certificates in the chain and expect the third one to be downloaded from their website.
- `E2.S5`: Here's a screenshot of a sample chain. Notice that you can check the 'Certification Path' tab if there are any remaining certificates in the chain. Also note the chain of "Issued To" and "Issued By" identities.
ExampleCertificateChain.jpg [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=2]ExampleCertificateChain.jpg [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=1]
- `E2.S6`: As for the certificate configuration on DataPower, the appliance will reference the actual key and certificate files stored in the cert: directory by file name. Navigation in the WebGUI to the SSL Proxy Profile -> Crypto Profile -> Crypto Key and Certificate objects will show the current files referenced by the configuration.
- `E2.S7`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=3] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=3]
- `E2.S8`: For example, your DataPower configuration may currently reference the existing files cert:///current-key.pem and cert:///current-cert.pem.
- `E2.S9`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=4] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=4]
- `E2.S10`: As long as the replacement file(s) are NOT named the same as these files (i.e. the new ones are named cert:///new-key.pemand cert:///new-cert.pem for example), it is safe to load the new file(s) into the cert: directory at any time ahead of the replacement operation. Your existing configuration will not use the new files, so long as the Crypto Key and Certificate Objects still refer to the files associated with the expiring certificate (i.e. cert:///current-key.pem and cert:///current-cert.pem).
- `E2.S11`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=5] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=5]
- `E2.S12`: Having both expiring and replacement files in the cert: directory at once allows for the capability to modify the configuration to point to the new files or revert it back to the expiring files relatively easily or to configure a new SSL Proxy Profile object that references the new files. The new SSL Proxy Profile could be used to test independently of the currently running configuration using a new test service such as an XML Firewall.
- `E2.S13`: You can navigate directly to the key and certificate objects using these paths: 
Objects → Crypto Configuration → Crypto Certificate.
Objects → Crypto Configuration → Crypto Key

- `E3.S22`: Procedures
- `E3.S23`: Installation procedure (using /opt/ibm as the install directory)
- `E3.S24`: 1. Download the new files that are attached at the end of this technote into a temporary directory ( /tmp) on the APM server.
- `E3.S25`: 2. Stop APM by issuing the following command:
- `E3.S26`: apm stop_all
- `E3.S27`: 3. Back up the existing shared keystore by issuing the following command:
- `E3.S28`: cp /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/key.jks
/opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/key.jks.BAK
- `E3.S29`: 4. Install the new keystore (replace the existing file) by issuing the following command:
- `E3.S30`: cp /tmp/updated.8.1.4.key.jks /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/key.jks
- `E3.S31`: 5. Back up the existing UI truststore by issuing the following command:
- `E3.S32`: cp /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/trust.jks /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/trust.jks.BAK
- `E3.S33`: 6. Install the new UI truststore (replace the existing file) by issuing the following command:
- `E3.S34`: cp /tmp/updated.8.1.4.trust.jks /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/trust.jks
- `E3.S35`: 7. Restart APM by issuing the following command:
- `E3.S36`: apm start_all
- `E3.S37`: Verification procedure - verifying the installation of the new keystore files
- `E3.S38`: 1. After APM is restarted, navigate to the APMUI at https://<APM_server_hostname>:9443 [https://apm_server_hostname:9443/]
- `E3.S39`: where <APM_server_hostname> is the hostname of your V8.1.4 APM server.
- `E3.S40`: 2. Verify that the APM Log in page appears and log in.
- `E3.S41`: 3. Verify that agent data is shown on the APM dashboard. 
Note: The passwords for the keystores and truststores are the same passwords as the upgraded 8.1.4 environment, therefore, you don't need to update the server.xml and serverVariables.xml files.

- `E4.S1`: certificate validation expired TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 DataPower firmware 3.8.1 and prior versions do not support certificate validation involving non-unique Distinguished Names.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
A Validation Credential object configured with multiple Certificate Authority certificates containing identical subject DNs but different key material may fail to validate incoming certificates that have been signed with one of the issuer certificates.
- `E4.S4`: CAUSE
DataPower searches the certificate list based on subject DN and attempts to validate against the first certificate that it finds with the given DN. If the initial attempt fails, the certificate validation will fail.
- `E4.S5`: ENVIRONMENT
A common scenario in which this issue arises is when a CA certificate is due to expire and the CA has issued a new certificate for the same subject.
- `E4.S6`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
If certificate validation fails (especially with "certificate signature failure"), check to make sure all of the configured certificates have unique subject DNs. If there is more than one certificate with the same subject DN, this may be the issue.
- `E4.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use a single certificate with a given subject DN per Validation Credential object or upgrade to a firmware version above 3.8.1 when it is available.

Use only one certificate for a given subject DN in the Validation Credential, or upgrade to firmware above 3.8.1.","support_ids":["E4.S2","E4.S4","E4.S5","E4.S7"]}]}}

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
If the replacement certificate uses the same filename as the expired certificate, disable and re-enable the certificate object to clear cached references to the expired certificate. [E2.S24]

If the Validation Credential contains both the old and new CA certificates with the same subject Distinguished Name, older DataPower firmware searches by subject DN and may select the first certificate—the expired one—causing validation to fail. Use only one certificate for a given subject DN in the Validation Credential, or upgrade to firmware above 3.8.1. [E4.S2] [E4.S4] [E4.S5] [E4.S7]

- `E1.S1`: certificate validation expired TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 DataPower firmware 3.8.1 and prior versions do not support certificate validation involving non-unique Distinguished Names.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
A Validation Credential object configured with multiple Certificate Authority certificates containing identical subject DNs but different key material may fail to validate incoming certificates that have been signed with one of the issuer certificates.
- `E1.S4`: CAUSE
DataPower searches the certificate list based on subject DN and attempts to validate against the first certificate that it finds with the given DN. If the initial attempt fails, the certificate validation will fail.
- `E1.S5`: ENVIRONMENT
A common scenario in which this issue arises is when a CA certificate is due to expire and the CA has issued a new certificate for the same subject.
- `E1.S6`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
If certificate validation fails (especially with "certificate signature failure"), check to make sure all of the configured certificates have unique subject DNs. If there is more than one certificate with the same subject DN, this may be the issue.
- `E1.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Use a single certificate with a given subject DN per Validation Credential object or upgrade to a firmware version above 3.8.1 when it is available.
- `E2.S1`: 720limitation; MQ; CERTLABL; 2539; 0x000009eb; MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E2.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After setting CERTLABL for an SSL channel on MQ Server, DataPower can no longer connect to that channel.
- `E2.S3`: SYMPTOM
When CERTLABL is configured on the channel that DataPower is using to connect to queue manager, the connection would fail and DataPower MQ Queue Manager object would be down.
- `E2.S4`: The following errors will be seen in the DataPower logs:
- `E2.S5`: * [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): test connection failed (2539) 
   [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): Queue Manager Error: 'mq-server.ibm.com:1111' ''. Reason code - 2539 
   The reason code is: 2539 0x000009eb MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR
- `E2.S6`: On MQ Server, there will be error logs explaining this connection failure:  * 
 * 
 *
- `E2.S7`: * 
 * The SSL or TLS channel 'SSL.SVRCONN.2' is configured to use certificate label 
   'SSL.SVRCONN.2'. However, the remote peer did not send the necessary 
   information to allow the local channel to use the correct certificate. The 
   remote host is 'datapower (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx)'.
- `E2.S8`: * This error occurs when the local channel definition has a certificate label and 
   the remote peer does not support selection of certificates. 
   The channel did not start.
- `E2.S9`: * 
 * Ensure that the remote peer supports certificate label configuration. Refer to 
   the Security section of the WebSphere MQ Information Center for details of 
   certificate label requirements. Alternatively, alter the local channel 
   definition so that it does not specify a certificate label.
- `E2.S10`: CAUSE
MQ version 8 and the later version provides a new parameter "CERTLABL" for administrators to specify a certificate to be used when making a SSL connection to a channel. This allows multiple certificates to be configured, one for each channel. All certificates are managed in the same queue manager on MQ Server. In order to utilize this function, both ends of the channel must be running MQ version 8 or the later version and must support Server Name Indication (SNI). 
Although DataPower version 7.2.0 runs MQ version 8 client and also supports SNI for the rest of the services, it does not support SNI for MQ Queue Manager object.
- `E2.S11`: ENVIRONMENT
MQ Server version 8, DataPower version 7.2.0
- `E2.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In order for DataPower to connect to the queue manager, the CERTLABL must be removed from the channel, which means you must not configure the CERTLABL on the MQ Server. After removing the CERTLABL from the channel, the channel would use the default certificate as configured in queue manager's properties.
- `E2.S13`: RELATED INFORMATION
 IBM MQ V8 Features and Enhancements [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redbooks/pdfs/sg248218.pdf]
- `E3.S1`: SSL HTTPS TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 What is the procedure for replacing an expiring certificate that is in use on the DataPower appliance with a newly obtained certificate?
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
Once you have obtained a new certificate from your certificate authority and are ready to replace the expiring one currently in use by your DataPower configuration with this new certificate, there is no single prescribed manner in which to perform the replacement operation. The following information presents some options for formulating an approach that best fits your environment.
- `E3.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
First, know your certificate material. It's not uncommon for newer certificates to be chained, so it is not a one for one replacement; the existing certificate on the DataPower appliance may need to be replaced by more than one certificate. Therefore, it is important to ensure you have the full certificate chain, as appropriate (i.e, the personal, intermediate and root certificates). Certificate authorities may send two certificates in the chain and expect the third one to be downloaded from their website.
- `E3.S5`: Here's a screenshot of a sample chain. Notice that you can check the 'Certification Path' tab if there are any remaining certificates in the chain. Also note the chain of "Issued To" and "Issued By" identities.
ExampleCertificateChain.jpg [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=2]ExampleCertificateChain.jpg [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=1]
- `E3.S6`: As for the certificate configuration on DataPower, the appliance will reference the actual key and certificate files stored in the cert: directory by file name. Navigation in the WebGUI to the SSL Proxy Profile -> Crypto Profile -> Crypto Key and Certificate objects will show the current files referenced by the configuration.
- `E3.S7`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=3] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=3]
- `E3.S8`: For example, your DataPower configuration may currently reference the existing files cert:///current-key.pem and cert:///current-cert.pem.
- `E3.S9`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=4] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=4]
- `E3.S10`: As long as the replacement file(s) are NOT named the same as these files (i.e. the new ones are named cert:///new-key.pemand cert:///new-cert.pem for example), it is safe to load the new file(s) into the cert: directory at any time ahead of the replacement operation. Your existing configuration will not use the new files, so long as the Crypto Key and Certificate Objects still refer to the files associated with the expiring certificate (i.e. cert:///current-key.pem and cert:///current-cert.pem).
- `E3.S11`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=5] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21500046&aid=5]
- `E3.S12`: Having both expiring and replacement files in the cert: directory at once allows for the capability to modify the configuration to point to the new files or revert it back to the expiring files relatively easily or to configure a new SSL Proxy Profile object that references the new files. The new SSL Proxy Profile could be used to test independently of the currently running configuration using a new test service such as an XML Firewall.
- `E3.S13`: You can navigate directly to the key and certificate objects using these paths: 
Objects → Crypto Configuration → Crypto Certificate.
Objects → Crypto Configuration → Crypto Key

- `E3.S18`: → Crypto Certificate.

- `E3.S21`: Either way, note how the configuration ultimately references the files in the cert: directory and plan ahead for how you prefer to reference the new files.
- `E3.S22`: They may be swapped out within the existing Crypto Configuration objects (i.e. update the objects to reference the new file(s) or to revert to the expiring ones as needed).
- `E3.S23`: Alternatively, a new separate set of Crypto Configuration objects that reference the new files may be created and replacement performed at the Crypto object level by updating the configuration to reference the new replacement Crypto Configuration objects.

Navigate to the Administrator's Guide, under "Managing the Appliance" - "Working with keys and certificates" from the WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654].

- `E4.S23`: Installation procedure (using /opt/ibm as the install directory)
- `E4.S24`: 1. Download the new files that are attached at the end of this technote into a temporary directory ( /tmp) on the APM server.
- `E4.S25`: 2. Stop APM by issuing the following command:
- `E4.S26`: apm stop_all
- `E4.S27`: 3. Back up the existing shared keystore by issuing the following command:
- `E4.S28`: cp /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/key.jks
/opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/key.jks.BAK
- `E4.S29`: 4. Install the new keystore (replace the existing file) by issuing the following command:
- `E4.S30`: cp /tmp/updated.8.1.4.key.jks /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/key.jks
- `E4.S31`: 5. Back up the existing UI truststore by issuing the following command:
- `E4.S32`: cp /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/trust.jks /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/trust.jks.BAK
- `E4.S33`: 6. Install the new UI truststore (replace the existing file) by issuing the following command:
- `E4.S34`: cp /tmp/updated.8.1.4.trust.jks /opt/ibm/wlp/usr/shared/resources/security/trust.jks
- `E4.S35`: 7. Restart APM by issuing the following command:
- `E4.S36`: apm start_all
- `E4.S37`: Verification procedure - verifying the installation of the new keystore files
- `E4.S38`: 1. After APM is restarted, navigate to the APMUI at https://<APM_server_hostname>:9443 [https://apm_server_hostname:9443/]
- `E4.S39`: where <APM_server_hostname> is the hostname of your V8.1.4 APM server.
- `E4.S40`: 2. Verify that the APM Log in page appears and log in.
- `E4.S41`: 3. Verify that agent data is shown on the APM dashboard. 
Note: The passwords for the keystores and truststores are the same passwords as the upgraded 8.1.4 environment, therefore, you don't need to update the server.xml and serverVariables.xml files.

### techqa_DEV_Q061#row-0044

Question: Why does my JVMSERVER remain in a "BEING DISABLED"  state? When I try to disable a JVMSERVER it becomes hung and remains in a "BEING DISABLED" state. This also occurs when I shut down the CICS region. The CICS region ultimately has to be cancelled. 

Reference / gold answer:
Based on the provided context, the issue with the JVMSERVER remaining in a "BEING DISABLED" state could be due to the zFS files not being properly propagated to the target environments after applying preventative maintenance to CICS Transaction Server for z/OS. When the updated zFS files are not rolled out to the target environments, it can impact the functioning of the JVM Servers.

To resolve this issue, ensure that the updated zFS files are properly propagated to all target environments when maintenance is applied to CICS. This should allow the JVMSERVER to be disabled successfully without getting stuck in a "BEING DISABLED" state.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `4b`:  You install preventative maintenance to CICS Transaction Server for z/OS (CICS TS).
- `4c`: Now when you install a JVMServer you receive DFHSJ0214 and DFHSJ0914 error messages. SYMPTOM
- `4g`: zFS files not propagated to target environment(s)
- `4i`: When you applied the maintenance, the zFS files were updated.
- `4j`: However, due to a procedural error, these updated files were not rolled out to the target environments.
- `4k`: Now that you are running JVM Servers, this has more of an impact.
- `4l`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `4m`: Ensure that the updated zFS files are propagated to the target environments when maintenance is applied to CICS. PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM

=== ON / BGE ===

Evidence state: `ALL`; evidence hash: `046e0a0aa118d1eff83bd1c441856b06bf4698c85165375be6df61e955997487`

Support units:
- `E1.S1`: java ; cemt set program newcopy ; cemt set program phasein ; ceci exec cics ; jvm jvmpool 5697E9300 R300 300 R630 630 HCI6300 5697-E93 5697E93 5655M1500 R640 640 R400 400 HCI6400 R650 650 R500 500 HCI6500 R670 670 R700 700 HCI6700 5655-S97 5655S97 KIXINFO TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You make changes to your Java™ program and recompile it. Then you enter CEMT SET PROGRAM(java-program) with the NEWCOPY or PHASEIN options and receive a response of NORMAL. The next time you run your Java program you expect CICS to use the new version. However, CICS continues to use the version that does not contain your latest changes.
- `E1.S3`: CAUSE
NEWCOPY and PHASEIN are not valid for Java programs, and are ignored if specified. The command returns NORMAL because it completed without error. This is documented as follows in the CICS TS V4.2 information center under CEMT SET PROGRAM [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v4r2/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.systemprogramming.doc/transactions/cemt/dfha7ai.html]:
- `E1.S4`: You cannot specify NEWCOPY for a program specified with the HOLD option or for a Java program that runs in a JVM. Use the PERFORM JVMPOOL PHASEOUT command to refresh Java programs that run in a pooled JVM. Disable and enable the JVMSERVER resource to refresh a Java program that runs in a JVM server.
- `E1.S5`: You cannot specify PHASEIN for a program specified with the HOLD option or for a Java program that runs in a JVM. Use the PERFORM JVMPOOL PHASEOUT command to refresh Java programs that run in a pooled JVM. Disable and enable the JVMSERVER resource to refresh a Java program that runs in a JVM server
- `E1.S6`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
If using CICS Transaction Server for z/OS (CICS TS) V3.1, use CEMT SET JVMPOOL PHASEOUT [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v3r2/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.doc/dfha7/transactions/cemt/dfha7ng.html] to pull in the newest version of your Java program. This will also delete the Java Virtual Machines (JVM) when the task using each JVM is no longer dependent on it. The next time you enter your transaction, a new JVM will be built and it will use the new version of your program.
- `E1.S7`: If using CICS TS 3.2 and above with pooled JVMs, enter CEMT PERFORM JVMPOOL PHASEOUT [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v4r2/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.systemprogramming.doc/transactions/cemt/dfha7_performjvmpool.html]. Afterwards, when new JVMs are started they will run the new version of the program.
- `E1.S8`: If using CICS TS 4.2 with JVM servers, enter CEMT SET JVMSERVER(jvmserver) DISABLED [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v4r2/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.systemprogramming.doc/commands/dfha8_setjvmserver.html] then ENABLED to disable and enable the JVMSERVER [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v4r2/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.resourcedefinition.doc/resources/jvmserver/dfha4_overview.html] resource that the Java program uses.
- `E1.S9`: CEMT SET JVMPOOL Phaseout, Purge, and Forcepurge functions are deprecated in CICS TS V3.2. That is why you should use the corresponding functions of the PERFORM JVMPOOL command when using CICS TS V3.2 and above.
- `E1.S10`: Note that CICS TS V3.2 supports Java V5. If using the shared class cache [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v4r2/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.java.doc/topics/dfhpjd3.html], a PHASEOUT is not needed with Java V5 onwards. Any changed classes are automatically phased in to the cache as they are used.
- `E1.S11`: PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM

- `E2.S4`: DFHSJ0914 [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v5r1/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.messages.doc/DFHSJ/DFHSJ0914E.html] JVMSERVER jvmserver is DISABLED because the Language Environment Enclave was not created.

- `E3.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  An application server JVM can hang if a thread logging an FFDC
   hangs.
- `E3.S5`: The problem can be detected by observing the WSVR0605W hung
   thread notifications in the SystemOut.log.
- `E3.S6`: One thread will be running the FFDCFilter.processException()
   which can be invoked from any WebSphere Application Server
   component.  The thread will get stuck doing its work.
   In the following example, the thread which invoked
   FFDCFilter.processException() is stuck waiting on a response to
   the OracleConnectionWrapper.getMetaData() method call:

   is/are 16 thread(s) in total in the server that may be hung.
    at

   Wrapper.java:150)
    at

    at sun.reflect.NativeMethodAccessorImpl.invoke0(Native Method)
    at

    at java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(Method.java:611)

- `E3.S12`: It is possible that the first FFDC thread which got hung (in

- `E3.S14`: It is possible that the first FFDC thread which got hung (in
   this example, "ORB.thread.pool : 32") will eventually complete.
   If it does complete, the threads will start moving and the hang
   will clear up.  However, if it never completes, then it is the
   same as if a true thread deadlock had occurred.
- `E3.S15`: This same type of analysis can be performed using a
   javacore/thread dump, however, javacores are not always
   available.
- `E3.S16`: LOCAL FIX
- `E3.S17`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  All users of IBM WebSphere Application      *
   *                  Server V7.0 and V8.0                        *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Syncrhonization between FFDC            *
   *                      incidents can cause a server hang       *
   *                      when an unrecoverable problem           *
   *                      occurs in a given incident.             *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   Syncrhonization between FFDC incidents can cause a server hang
   when an unrecoverable problem occurs in a given incident.
- `E3.S18`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  FFDC has been modified to ensure that incidents can continue
   to be logged from other components when a given component's
   incident-handling hangs a thread.  The impact to this is that
   the FFDC summary log may indicate that the incident file of a
   bad thread was created, while the thread may not have returned
   so the incident file will not exist.  Therefore, a missing
   incident entry that might have appeared in a summary file is
   an indication that the component logging to FFDC did not
   return control.

   http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980]

 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E5.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  You are running CICS 5.2 and have a CICS IPIC connection
   stuck in Freeing state. It never goes into Released state, and
   the region must be recycled to clear.
   A dump at the time the connection was in freeing state, shows
   a Tran number associated with an IPIC session, but this task is
   no longer in the system.  It issued the following message:
   DFHIS1025 APPLID Failed to attach mirror transaction xxxx on
            IPCONN IPIC. Error code is X'0619'
   This task tried to send an error response back to the client,
   but
   fails due to the connection being closed.
   There is a problem in this scenario, where we do not
   free up the session control block- ISSB. This leaves it on the
   active chain, preventing the IPCONN from ever getting to
   RELEASED
   state.
   Additional Symptom(s) Search Keyword(s): KIXREVEPH
- `E5.S5`: LOCAL FIX
- `E5.S6`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * All CICS users.                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * IPCONN remain in FREEing state after a                       *
   * mirror transaction failed to attach                          *
   * because it was disable.                                      *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * .                                                            *
   ****************************************************************
   CICS region A and region B are connected via IPIC. The IPCONN is
   in ACQUIRE status. Region A send a DPL request to region B.
   The mirror transaction in region B is disabled. Transaction CSAC
   get attached instead of the mirror transaction. DFHACP attempt
   to send an IS7 with sense code 084C0000 with message DFHIS1025
   to region A. The send failed because the IPIC socket has been
   closed. The CSAC transaction terminates without FREEing the
   receive ISSB that was allocated to the task.
   .
   The SOCKET closed causes transaction CIST to be attached to
   release the IPCONN. During the IPCONN termination the orphan
   ISSB is found causing the IPCONN to remain in FREEing state.
- `E5.S7`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  DFHISZA and DFHISIS have been changed to ensure that the receive
   ISSB used to send an IS7 response to the client region is FREE
   when socket domain returned an exception.
