- `E1.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  You are running CICS 5.2 and have a CICS IPIC connection
   stuck in Freeing state. It never goes into Released state, and
   the region must be recycled to clear.
   A dump at the time the connection was in freeing state, shows
   a Tran number associated with an IPIC session, but this task is
   no longer in the system.  It issued the following message:
   DFHIS1025 APPLID Failed to attach mirror transaction xxxx on
            IPCONN IPIC. Error code is X'0619'
   This task tried to send an error response back to the client,
   but
   fails due to the connection being closed.
   There is a problem in this scenario, where we do not
   free up the session control block- ISSB. This leaves it on the
   active chain, preventing the IPCONN from ever getting to
   RELEASED
   state.
   Additional Symptom(s) Search Keyword(s): KIXREVEPH
- `E1.S5`: LOCAL FIX
- `E1.S6`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * All CICS users.                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * IPCONN remain in FREEing state after a                       *
   * mirror transaction failed to attach                          *
   * because it was disable.                                      *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * .                                                            *
   ****************************************************************
   CICS region A and region B are connected via IPIC. The IPCONN is
   in ACQUIRE status. Region A send a DPL request to region B.
   The mirror transaction in region B is disabled. Transaction CSAC
   get attached instead of the mirror transaction. DFHACP attempt
   to send an IS7 with sense code 084C0000 with message DFHIS1025
   to region A. The send failed because the IPIC socket has been
   closed. The CSAC transaction terminates without FREEing the
   receive ISSB that was allocated to the task.
   .
   The SOCKET closed causes transaction CIST to be attached to
   release the IPCONN. During the IPCONN termination the orphan
   ISSB is found causing the IPCONN to remain in FREEing state.
- `E1.S7`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  DFHISZA and DFHISIS have been changed to ensure that the receive
   ISSB used to send an IS7 response to the client region is FREE
   when socket domain returned an exception.

- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You install preventative maintenance to CICS Transaction Server for z/OS (CICS TS). Now when you install a JVMServer you receive DFHSJ0214 and DFHSJ0914 error messages.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
DFHSJ0215 [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v5r1/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.messages.doc/DFHSJ/DFHSJ0215.html] The JVM Server jvmserver failed to initialize the OSGi framework. The JVM will be terminated.
- `E3.S4`: DFHSJ0914 [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/cicsts/v5r1/topic/com.ibm.cics.ts.messages.doc/DFHSJ/DFHSJ0914E.html] JVMSERVER jvmserver is DISABLED because the Language Environment Enclave was not created.
- `E3.S5`: CAUSE
zFS files not propagated to target environment(s)
- `E3.S6`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
When you applied the maintenance, the zFS files were updated. However, due to a procedural error, these updated files were not rolled out to the target environments. Now that you are running JVM Servers, this has more of an impact.
- `E3.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Ensure that the updated zFS files are propagated to the target environments when maintenance is applied to CICS.

- `E4.S1`: ABENDs - Dumps TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 Why am I receiving ABEND AKEA in IODM module EKCCMTOM at offset x'1A68' when trying to run in a CICS Version 3.3.0 region? The error occurs shortly after restarting IODM without the cycling region.
- `E4.S3`: In the CICS system initialization table (SIT), STGPROT is set to "No" and RENTPGM is set to NOPROTECT. System modifications (sysmods), UN54096 and UN60897, have been applied.
- `E4.S4`: ANSWER
Refer to authorized program analysis report (APAR) PN56650 for information about IODM module EKCCMTOM and program DFHZNEP. Set both programs to the EXECKEY parameter of CICS® and give them a datalocation value of "Any." Also, change the queue status field (QUESTAT) of the IDPARMTB table from 'E' to 'D'. The IDPARMTB table defines system-wide Object Distribution Manager parameters vital to the system's operation. Making this change frees you from relying on the use of the send queue processing operator commands, OAQM and OAQC, that are between OID1 and OID2. OID1 is the ImagePlus Object Distribution Manager first-stage, and OID2 the second-stage, shutdown CICS transaction. OID2 completes the Object Distribution Manager shutdown.
- `E4.S5`: The mode settings for program DFHZNEP state that DFHZNEP must be RMODE=any, AMODE=31. Relink your DFHZNEP as 31 bit so that DFHZNAC can link to ZNEP.
- `E4.S6`: When you relink DFHZNEP as 31 bit, expect to receive error message: IEW2646 for modules DFHZNEP, EKCCVECT, and EKCCFMSG. Error message: IEW2646I is issued when an RMODE value that is specified in the PARM statement is different than the one in the electrostatic discharge (ESD) record. Included is a binder message, which warns of a conflict. As a result, the RMODE value in the PARM statement will be used, based on the hierarchy specified in the Program Management Manual.
- `E4.S7`: You might get intermittent failures in OID1 in IODM module EKCCMTOM. Continue to try the failing transaction until you receive a normal completion.
- `E4.S8`: Another element to this error was revealed during its testing. The abend appears after cycling ODM but without cycling the CICS region. For example, you might first start the CICS region, then OIUP, OID1, OID2, OIUP, OID1 (which fails), OID2 (which also fails). By cycling the CICS region, the first OID1 and OID2 will function normally.
- `E4.S9`: In this situation, the second OIUP, which initializes the Object Distribution Manager, and all other functions (DISP and so on), function without incident.
- `E4.S10`: * If you use the LMODs from EKCPSTLK with the CICS330 libraries (instead of with the CICS211 libraries), OID1 and OID2 fail after the first shutdown of ODM. 
 * If you cycle the whole region, OID1 and OID2 work the first time after an OIUP. 
 * If you bring ODM up and then try to shut it down again, you will get the abends. 
 * With the CICS330 links, the failure is consistent. 
 * With the CICS211 links, the failure is intermittent. 
 * Additionally, with the CICS330 modules: 
 * DFHECI links clean 
 * error message: IEW2646I is not produced 
 * the offset of the abend moves about 8 bytes
- `E4.S11`: Note: The error described in this document was accompanied by error message: EKC0304A return code 8 reason code 00070017 after restarting IODM without a cycling region.

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
The information is available in IBM’s English Security Bulletin, “Security Bulletin: Multiple vulnerabilities in IBM Java Runtime affect WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus (CVE-2016-3485)”: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21994213 [E2.S4]

The bulletin covers vulnerabilities in IBM Runtime Environment Java Technology Edition 6.0.16.26 and earlier for WebSphere Message Broker, 7.0.9.40 and earlier for WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus, and 7.1.3.40 and earlier for IBM Integration Bus. [E1.S2]

Affected products include IBM Integration Bus V9 and V10 and WebSphere Message Broker V8. [E1.S4] [E1.S5]

For remediation, APAR IT16743 is included in IBM Integration Bus V10 fix pack 10.0.0.7 and V9 fix pack 9.0.0.7; an interim fix for WebSphere Message Broker V8 is available through IBM Fix Central. [E1.S7]

The IBM Java SDK Security Bulletin is also listed as a reference: http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21986642. [E1.S12]

### techqa_DEV_Q084#row-0069

Question: Is ITCAM for J2EE 7.1.1 agent supported on RHEL7.x? 

When I try to install IBM Tivoli Composite Application Manager Agent for J2EE V7.1.1.0,Linux on x86, English (CN0PKEN) on RHEL 7.2 64-bits

I am getting the following error message:

install.sh failure: KCI1138E could not determine the machine's architecture.

Is ITCAM for J2EE 7.1.1 supported on RHEL7?


Reference / gold answer:
Yes, ITCAM for J2EE 7.1.1 is supported on RHEL7.x. However, the error message suggests that there may be an issue related to determining the machine's architecture during the installation process. To address this issue, make sure you have the correct version for the Linux x86 platform. If the error persists, you may need to contact IBM support for further assistance.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `4e`: As of 4Q2015, RHEL7 64-bit has now been certified for use with ITCAM for J2EE v7.1.1.0.1 and higher.
- `4f`: Also, please be aware of this APAR for a known ITM problem: http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21960089 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21960089]

- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 What application servers are supported by ITCAM for J2EE agent v7.1.1? What has changed if compared to the previous version of this product?
- `E1.S3`: ANSWER
These application servers and J2SE applications are supported:
- Apache Tomcat 4.x, 5.x, 6.x, 7.x 
- JBoss 3.x, 4.x, and 5.x
- Oracle WebLogic Server 9.x, 10.x, and 12.x; Oracle WebLogic Portal Server 9.x and 10.x
- SAP NetWeaver 7.0 (2004s), 7.1, 7.3, and 7.4
- J2SE applications
- `E1.S4`: JBoss EAP versions 6.1.0, 6.2.0, 6.3.0, and 6.4.0 support has been introduced starting from 7.1.1.0-TIV-ITCAM_J2EE-IF0003
- `E1.S5`: Support for versions highlighted in boldface is new in release 7.1.1
- `E1.S6`: Support for versions highlighted in italics had already been introduced starting from 6.1 FP6 and later interim-fixes (typically 6.1.0.6-TIV-ITCAMfJ2EE_MP-IF000x, see their readmes for details).
In fact J2EE v6.x has gone out of support at this point, so you will have to upgrade to v7.1.1.0.x to use a supported version.
- `E1.S7`: Java 7 support has been officially introduced in version 7.1.1.
Java 8 support has been introduced starting from 7.1.1.0-TIV-ITCAM_J2EE-IF0003
- `E1.S8`: The following application servers are not supported anymore in the J2EE agent 7.1.1:
- `E1.S9`: - Oracle/BEA Application Server
- Sun JSAS
- WebSphere Application Server Community Edition

- `E3.S3`: QUESTION
 Commonly used APM / IBM Monitoring V8.1.2 part numbers.
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
Here are the commonly used part numbers to search for when downloading the new IBM Monitoring / APM V8.1.2 components. The Agents package here will contain the WebSphere and other J2EE agents to be used for monitoring the WAS / J2EE servers. 
Note these are the upgrade part numbers, so you will need to use the base code parts [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21961194] first. You can choose to download the eAssembly or the individual packages that you need.

- `E4.S1`: ITCAM; appservers; prerequisites; CAMJ2ALL; CAMJ2ENV TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E4.S2`: QUESTION
 What application servers are supported by ITCAM for J2EE agent v7.1.1? What has changed if compared to the previous version of this product?
- `E4.S3`: ANSWER
These application servers and J2SE applications are supported:
- Apache Tomcat 4.x, 5.x, 6.x, 7.x 
- JBoss 3.x, 4.x, and 5.x
- Oracle WebLogic Server 9.x, 10.x, and 12.x; Oracle WebLogic Portal Server 9.x and 10.x
- SAP NetWeaver 7.0 (2004s), 7.1, 7.3, and 7.4
- J2SE applications
- `E4.S4`: JBoss EAP versions 6.1.0, 6.2.0, 6.3.0, and 6.4.0 support has been introduced starting from 7.1.1.0-TIV-ITCAM_J2EE-IF0003
- `E4.S5`: Support for versions highlighted in boldface is new in release 7.1.1
- `E4.S6`: Support for versions highlighted in italics had already been introduced starting from 6.1 FP6 and later interim-fixes (typically 6.1.0.6-TIV-ITCAMfJ2EE_MP-IF000x, see their readmes for details).
In fact J2EE v6.x has gone out of support at this point, so you will have to upgrade to v7.1.1.0.x to use a supported version.
- `E4.S7`: Java 7 support has been officially introduced in version 7.1.1.
Java 8 support has been introduced starting from 7.1.1.0-TIV-ITCAM_J2EE-IF0003
- `E4.S8`: The following application servers are not supported anymore in the J2EE agent 7.1.1:
- `E4.S9`: - Oracle/BEA Application Server
- Sun JSAS
- WebSphere Application Server Community Edition

### techqa_DEV_Q096#row-0127

Question: I am using persistent messages, but I never got the messages I am using persistent messages, but I never got the messages. How can I determine what happen to the messages?


Reference / gold answer:
If you are using persistent messages and never received them, it is important to check the following:

1. Check if the WebSphere MQ queue manager ended in a normal way via `endmqm`. If the queue manager ends abruptly due to a sudden machine reboot, there may be issues with message recovery upon restart.

2. Look for error messages related to message persistence or message retrieval in the logs or console output. These messages may indicate any problems that occurred during the message delivery process.

3. If you suspect a potential issue with message retrieval, analyze the `javacore` and `heapdump` files generated when the issue occurred. These files can provide valuable insight into the state of the application and any memory-related issues that may have occurred.

By following these steps and analyzing the relevant logs and diagnostic information, you can determine what happened to the persistent messages and identify any potential issues that may have caused them not to be received.

- `E1.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  If a queue manager ends other than in the normal way via endmqm
   (e.g. due to a sudden machine reboot), then recovery actions by
   the queue manager on restart may result in a damaged queue.
- `E1.S5`: The queue is at risk of becoming damaged in that circumstance,
   if it is used with a mixture of persistent and non-persistent
   messages. This problem may be more prevalent for transmit
   queues, which can often hold both persistent and non-persistent
   messages.
- `E1.S6`: It is also possible that the problem could manifest as the
   reappearance of previously got persistent messages on the
   queue, rather than the queue being reported as damaged.
- `E1.S7`: There is only a very small possibility of encountering this
   problem, due to a number of factors needing to co-exist for it
   to occur.
- `E1.S8`: The typical damaged queue resulting from this problem will be
   of size 1712 bytes, or more likely, 10240 bytes. Examination of
   the q file (by IBM Service) would reveal a non-null head of
   message chain, but no message.
- `E1.S9`: LOCAL FIX
- `E1.S10`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   You may encounter this issue if you do not always end the queue
   manager gracefully, via endmqm. In addition, to encounter the
   problem you must also be using some queues with a mixture of
   persistent and non-persistent messages.
- `E1.S11`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   This problem requires the following sequence of operations to
   occur (some are user driven, and some are driven by the queue
   manager itself):
- `E1.S12`: Put some persistent messages to a queue.
- `E1.S13`: Flush the persistent messages to disk, other than by a
   checkpoint. That can happen when setting queue attributes.
- `E1.S14`: Get all of the persistent messages.
- `E1.S15`: Initiate a checkpoint.
- `E1.S16`: After initiating the checkpoint, but before the queue itself is
   checkpointed, put a non-persistent message.
- `E1.S17`: That sets up a possibility that the queue checkpoint will fail
   to flush a null head of message chain, and it may also truncate
   the queue to below the q file message area. It is important to
   flush a null head because all the persistent messages have been
   got and we had previously flushed the persistent messages to
   disk.
- `E1.S18`: If the queue manager is hard-crashed immediately after the
   checkpoint, then on queue manager restart the queue file may
   contain persistent messages that had previously all been got.
   Or, if the queue checkpoint operation before the queue manager
   crash truncated the queue, then the queue will be reported as
   damaged on attempting to access it.
- `E1.S19`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The queue checkpoint logic was revised to correctly handle the
   problem situation described.
- `E1.S20`: on queue manager restart the queue file may
   contain persistent messages that had previously all been got.
   Or, if the queue checkpoint operation before the queue manager
   crash truncated the queue, then the queue will be reported as

- `E2.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 How can I make use of the WebSphere MQ Read Ahead functionality from an application that uses the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS to create a subscription on a topic, and then synchronously receives messages that are published on that topic?
- `E2.S3`: ANSWER
WebSphere MQ V7 introduced a new feature called "Read Ahead [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q026310_.htm]". This performance optimization allows WebSphere MQ queue managers to stream non-persistent messages to client applications connecting via TCP/IP before the application has requested them. The client stores these messages in a Read Ahead Buffer. When an application requests a message, the client removes the message from the buffer and gives it to the application for processing.
JMS applications running in one of the following environments:
- `E2.S4`: * The WebSphere MQ classes for JMS. 
 * The WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter. 
 * The WebSphere MQ OSGi bundles.
- `E2.S5`: that connect to a WebSphere MQ queue manager using the CLIENT transport in WebSphere MQ messaging provider normal mode, [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.connect.doc/intro_jms_msgprov.htm] and receive messages synchronously, can make use of the new functionality.
- `E2.S6`: This technote will look at how applications that subscribe to a topic need to be written in order to take advantage of the Read Ahead functionality, as well as discussing what JMS Destination and WebSphere MQ properties need to be set to turn on Read Ahead.
- `E2.S7`: Applications running within an WebSphere Application Server environment can also make use of this functionality. Details of how to do this will be covered in a future technote.
- `E2.S8`: Writing a JMS application to use Read Ahead to receive messages synchronously 
The Read Ahead feature will only stream non-persistent messages to client applications that are getting messages outside of a transaction.
- `E2.S9`: In JMS terms, this means that the application must be using a non-transacted JMS session that has an acknowledgement mode of either AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE or DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE in order to be eligible to make use of Read Ahead.
- `E2.S10`: Here is an example which shows an application creating a non-transacted, AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE JMS Session: 
 *
- `E2.S11`: The non-transacted JMS Session can then be used to create a MessageConsumer object for the JMS Destination that maps to the WebSphere MQ topic which the non-persistent messages will be published on.
- `E2.S12`: Once the MessageConsumer has been created, applications that get non-persistent messages by calling one of the following methods: 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 *
- `E2.S13`: will be eligible to make use of Read Ahead, if the JMS Destination and the WebSphere MQ topic that the Destination maps to allows this functionality.
- `E2.S14`: Configuring the JMS Destination and WebSphere MQ to allow Read Ahead 
When an application uses the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS to subscribe to a WebSphere MQ topic, a managed subscription will be created. This managed subscription will either be durable or non-durable, depending upon how the application created the subscription.
- `E2.S15`: With managed subscriptions, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create a managed queue for the application. Every time a message is published on the WebSphere MQ topic that the application has subscribed to, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will take a copy of that message and put it onto the managed queue.
- `E2.S16`: or non-durable, depending upon how the application created the subscription.
- `E2.S17`: With managed subscriptions, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create a managed queue for the application. Every time a message is published on the WebSphere MQ topic that the application has subscribed to, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will take a copy of that message and put it onto the managed queue. When the JMS application requests a message, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will remove a message from the managed queue and returns it to the application for processing.
- `E2.S18`: By default, the managed queue that the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create for applications that take out a subscription will be based on one of the following model queues: 
 * SYSTEM.DURABLE.MODEL.QUEUE 
 * SYSTEM.NDURABLE.MODEL.QUEUE
- `E2.S19`: The model queues used to create the managed subscriptions can be changed by modifying the WebSphere MQ Topic properties MDURMDL and MNDURMDL [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.explorer.doc/e_properties_topics.htm].
- `E2.S20`: Whether Read Ahead will be enabled when the MessageConsumer gets the non-persistent messages that are published on the topic the MessageConsumer is subscribed to depends upon the following two properties: 
 * The JMS Destination Property READAHEADALLOWED (RAALD) [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.ref.dev.doc/q112370_.htm] 
 * The WebSphere MQ queue property DEFREADA of the model queue used to create the managed queue used by the managed subscription created for the application. [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q032570_.htm]
- `E2.S21`: The WebSphere MQ queue property DEFREADA specifies whether applications that get messages from this queue can use Read Ahead if they are getting non-persistent messages outside of a transaction.
- `E2.S22`: The JMS Destination property READAHEADALLOWED controls whether JMS applications using a non-transacted Session that has an acknowledgement mode of either AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE or DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE will use Read Ahead when getting non-persistent messages from a queue.
- `E2.S23`: It is a combination of these two properties that determines if Read Ahead will be used.

- `E3.S1`: Pub Sub; Publish Subscribe; JMS; MustGather; MustGathers; Must Gather; Collect Troubleshooting Data; MustGatherDocument; Collecting; Trouble; Shooting TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You are designing an application solution with WebSphere Message Broker (WMB) and IBM Integration Bus (IIB) and are having problems with JMS.
- `E3.S3`: This MustGather document explains how to troubleshoot this problem by yourself, how to generate diagnostic data when the problem is happening, how to collect the available data from your system, and how to share that data with IBM support.
- `E3.S4`: ENVIRONMENT
These instructions are for WebSphere Message Broker or IBM Integration Bus on Windows systems.
Return to the WMB / IIB MustGather index [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21209857] for other systems.
- `E3.S5`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E3.S6`: STEP 1: SELF-GUIDED TROUBLESHOOTING
- `E3.S7`: 1. Consider Using the Test Client in trace and debug mode [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/af52260_.htm].
 2. 
 3. A user level trace [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed.
    It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior.
 4. 
 5. Check for known issues:
    Troubleshooting JMS nodes [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/ac24877_.htm]
    developerWorks Forums: WebSphere Message Broker: JMS [https://www.ibm.com/developerworks/community/forums/html/forum?id=11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000281&query=jms]
    WebSphere Message Broker support site [http://www.ibm.com/support/entry/portal/Overview/Software/WebSphere/WebSphere_Message_Broker]
- `E3.S8`: STEP 2: COLLECT DATA
- `E3.S9`: 1. mqsidc See: mqsidc usage instructions [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSKM8N_8.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/bu46012_.htm]
- `E3.S10`: * When running the tool, select the option for 'Broker Collector', when prompted.
- `E3.S11`: 2. 
 3. JMS details
    Export a current view of your JMS configuration with these items:  * mqsireportproperties <broker> -c JMSProviders -o <JMSProvider> -r
     * the contents of the jarsURL directory
     * the JNDI bindings file
- `E3.S12`: 4. 
 5. Project Interchange files for the problematic flow/set/ESQL/model
     * You can export your Message Flow and Message Set project(s) into an archive file for easy transmission to IBM Support.
       See: Exporting your message flow projects from the Toolkit [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21418121]
- `E3.S13`: 6. 
 7. Traces If the problem occurs during a runtime test or with the Toolkit test facility, WMB execution group traces [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321] can be used to gain a better understanding of the problem.  * A user level trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#1] is intended to assist users with understanding how their ESQL is processed. It will also show a high level view of the message flow behavior.
     * A service level trace [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21177321#2] is intended to be provided to IBM Support to assist in the diagnosis of your issue.
- `E3.S14`: 8. 
 9. General Broker information
    If the mqsidc tool was not run, then capture this information manually  * Record the WebSphere Message Broker version, release, and maintenance level.
       This can be captured using the command 'mqsiservice -v'.
     * Record the operating system version, release, and maintenance level.
     * Record the version, release, and maintenance level of any related products and components for the problematic application.
     * Collect the local error log.
       On Window systems, the local error log is the Windows Application Event Log.
       You can find the Event Viewer from the Windows Control Panel.
       See: Event viewer logs [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=849&uid=swg21295454]
     * Collect the Standard Output/Error logs.
       On Window systems, WMB writes information to a 'console.out' file.
       This file is located under the Message Broker workpath.
       See: Standard System Logs [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSMKHH_9.0.0/com.ibm.etools.mft.doc/au14165_.htm]
- `E3.S15`: ATTENTION: A good problem description is one of the most important tools IBM needs to analyze your data!

- `E1.S2`: SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.
- `E1.S3`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E1.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  If a queue manager ends other than in the normal way via endmqm
   (e.g. due to a sudden machine reboot), then recovery actions by
   the queue manager on restart may result in a damaged queue.
- `E1.S5`: The queue is at risk of becoming damaged in that circumstance,
   if it is used with a mixture of persistent and non-persistent
   messages. This problem may be more prevalent for transmit
   queues, which can often hold both persistent and non-persistent
   messages.
- `E1.S6`: It is also possible that the problem could manifest as the
   reappearance of previously got persistent messages on the
   queue, rather than the queue being reported as damaged.
- `E1.S7`: There is only a very small possibility of encountering this
   problem, due to a number of factors needing to co-exist for it
   to occur.
- `E1.S8`: The typical damaged queue resulting from this problem will be
   of size 1712 bytes, or more likely, 10240 bytes. Examination of
   the q file (by IBM Service) would reveal a non-null head of
   message chain, but no message.
- `E1.S9`: LOCAL FIX
- `E1.S10`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   You may encounter this issue if you do not always end the queue
   manager gracefully, via endmqm. In addition, to encounter the
   problem you must also be using some queues with a mixture of
   persistent and non-persistent messages.
- `E1.S11`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   This problem requires the following sequence of operations to
   occur (some are user driven, and some are driven by the queue
   manager itself):
- `E1.S12`: Put some persistent messages to a queue.
- `E1.S13`: Flush the persistent messages to disk, other than by a
   checkpoint. That can happen when setting queue attributes.
- `E1.S14`: Get all of the persistent messages.
- `E1.S15`: Initiate a checkpoint.
- `E1.S16`: After initiating the checkpoint, but before the queue itself is
   checkpointed, put a non-persistent message.
- `E1.S17`: That sets up a possibility that the queue checkpoint will fail
   to flush a null head of message chain, and it may also truncate
   the queue to below the q file message area. It is important to
   flush a null head because all the persistent messages have been
   got and we had previously flushed the persistent messages to
   disk.
- `E1.S18`: If the queue manager is hard-crashed immediately after the
   checkpoint, then on queue manager restart the queue file may
   contain persistent messages that had previously all been got.
   Or, if the queue checkpoint operation before the queue manager
   crash truncated the queue, then the queue will be reported as
   damaged on attempting to access it.
- `E1.S19`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The queue checkpoint logic was revised to correctly handle the
   problem situation described.
- `E1.S20`: on queue manager restart the queue file may
   contain persistent messages that had previously all been got.
   Or, if the queue checkpoint operation before the queue manager
   crash truncated the queue, then the queue will be reported as
   damaged on attempting to access it.
- `E1.S21`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The queue checkpoint logic was revised to correctly handle the
   problem situation described.

- `E2.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E2.S2`: QUESTION
 How can I make use of the WebSphere MQ Read Ahead functionality from an application that uses the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS to create a subscription on a topic, and then synchronously receives messages that are published on that topic?
- `E2.S3`: ANSWER
WebSphere MQ V7 introduced a new feature called "Read Ahead [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q026310_.htm]". This performance optimization allows WebSphere MQ queue managers to stream non-persistent messages to client applications connecting via TCP/IP before the application has requested them. The client stores these messages in a Read Ahead Buffer. When an application requests a message, the client removes the message from the buffer and gives it to the application for processing.
JMS applications running in one of the following environments:
- `E2.S4`: * The WebSphere MQ classes for JMS. 
 * The WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter. 
 * The WebSphere MQ OSGi bundles.
- `E2.S5`: that connect to a WebSphere MQ queue manager using the CLIENT transport in WebSphere MQ messaging provider normal mode, [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.connect.doc/intro_jms_msgprov.htm] and receive messages synchronously, can make use of the new functionality.
- `E2.S6`: This technote will look at how applications that subscribe to a topic need to be written in order to take advantage of the Read Ahead functionality, as well as discussing what JMS Destination and WebSphere MQ properties need to be set to turn on Read Ahead.
- `E2.S7`: Applications running within an WebSphere Application Server environment can also make use of this functionality. Details of how to do this will be covered in a future technote.
- `E2.S8`: Writing a JMS application to use Read Ahead to receive messages synchronously 
The Read Ahead feature will only stream non-persistent messages to client applications that are getting messages outside of a transaction.
- `E2.S9`: In JMS terms, this means that the application must be using a non-transacted JMS session that has an acknowledgement mode of either AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE or DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE in order to be eligible to make use of Read Ahead.
- `E2.S10`: Here is an example which shows an application creating a non-transacted, AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE JMS Session: 
 *
- `E2.S11`: The non-transacted JMS Session can then be used to create a MessageConsumer object for the JMS Destination that maps to the WebSphere MQ topic which the non-persistent messages will be published on.
- `E2.S12`: Once the MessageConsumer has been created, applications that get non-persistent messages by calling one of the following methods: 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 * 
 *
- `E2.S13`: will be eligible to make use of Read Ahead, if the JMS Destination and the WebSphere MQ topic that the Destination maps to allows this functionality.
- `E2.S14`: Configuring the JMS Destination and WebSphere MQ to allow Read Ahead 
When an application uses the WebSphere MQ classes for JMS to subscribe to a WebSphere MQ topic, a managed subscription will be created. This managed subscription will either be durable or non-durable, depending upon how the application created the subscription.
- `E2.S15`: With managed subscriptions, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create a managed queue for the application. Every time a message is published on the WebSphere MQ topic that the application has subscribed to, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will take a copy of that message and put it onto the managed queue.
- `E2.S16`: or non-durable, depending upon how the application created the subscription.
- `E2.S17`: With managed subscriptions, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create a managed queue for the application. Every time a message is published on the WebSphere MQ topic that the application has subscribed to, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will take a copy of that message and put it onto the managed queue. When the JMS application requests a message, the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will remove a message from the managed queue and returns it to the application for processing.
- `E2.S18`: By default, the managed queue that the WebSphere MQ Publish/Subscribe Engine will create for applications that take out a subscription will be based on one of the following model queues: 
 * SYSTEM.DURABLE.MODEL.QUEUE 
 * SYSTEM.NDURABLE.MODEL.QUEUE
- `E2.S19`: The model queues used to create the managed subscriptions can be changed by modifying the WebSphere MQ Topic properties MDURMDL and MNDURMDL [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.explorer.doc/e_properties_topics.htm].
- `E2.S20`: Whether Read Ahead will be enabled when the MessageConsumer gets the non-persistent messages that are published on the topic the MessageConsumer is subscribed to depends upon the following two properties: 
 * The JMS Destination Property READAHEADALLOWED (RAALD) [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.ref.dev.doc/q112370_.htm] 
 * The WebSphere MQ queue property DEFREADA of the model queue used to create the managed queue used by the managed subscription created for the application. [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSFKSJ_8.0.0/com.ibm.mq.dev.doc/q032570_.htm]
- `E2.S21`: The WebSphere MQ queue property DEFREADA specifies whether applications that get messages from this queue can use Read Ahead if they are getting non-persistent messages outside of a transaction.
- `E2.S22`: The JMS Destination property READAHEADALLOWED controls whether JMS applications using a non-transacted Session that has an acknowledgement mode of either AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE or DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE will use Read Ahead when getting non-persistent messages from a queue.
- `E2.S23`: It is a combination of these two properties that determines if Read Ahead will be used.

- `E3.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 The messaging engine XXXXYYYYZZZ cannot be started as there is no runtime
initialized for it yet, retry the operation once it has initialized.
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
By looking at the systemout.log, we have something like:
.
- `E3.S4`: [6/24/14 15:05:32:488 EDT] 0000001e SibMessage E [XXXXYYYYZZZ] CWSIS1561E: The messaging engine's unique id does not match that found in the file store. ME_UUID=BPE98764B8E93CB4, ME_UUID(FS)=4587F87990047458
.
These are the messaging engine UUID mismatch scenarios: 
. 
. 
1) When the data store or file store of different messaging engine is pointed to the current one. 
. 
2) A backup of the data store or file store taken at an earlier time was restored. 
. 
3) You have deleted the messaging engine and recreated the Messaging Engine with the same name and trying to use the previous file store which was associated with the old messaging engine(UUID).
- `E3.S5`: ANSWER
To resolve the issue you will have to delete the file store for this Messaging Engine: .
- `E3.S6`: XXXXYYYYZZZ 
. 
Delete the existing file stores for this messaging engine and restart the JVM. 
This action will create the new file store for the new UUID's.
- `E3.S7`: Note1: You must treat the log file, the temporary store file, and the permanent store file as one unit; that is, delete operation must be performed on all three files.
Note2:By performing the suggested action, all the messages in the filestore will be lost.
- `E3.S8`: RELATED INFORMATION
 Deleting files following removal of a messaging engine [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSAW57_7.0.0/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/info/ae/ae/tjm1060_.html]

Visible answer:
A queue manager that ends abnormally—for example, after a sudden machine reboot—may, during restart recovery, leave a damaged queue or cause previously retrieved persistent messages to reappear. [E1.S4] [E1.S6] [E1.S18]

To investigate, check whether the queue is reported as damaged when accessed. A typical damaged queue may be 1712 bytes or, more likely, 10240 bytes; IBM Service can examine the queue file for a non-null message-chain head with no message. [E1.S8] [E1.S18]

The queue-checkpoint logic was revised to correct this problem. Fixes are available in WebSphere MQ 6.0.2.12, 7.0.1.10, 7.1.0.3, and 7.5.0.1, with platform-specific fix details listed for the affected releases. [E1.S19] [E1.S1] [E1.S23] [E1.S24] [E1.S25] [E1.S26]

Caused by: com.ibm.ejs.container.SessionBeanTimeoutException: Stateful bean CMStatefulBeanO(BeanId(server1# mySessionBean.jar# StdEJBReader, A5667152-014B-4000-E000-9AD20A8E643B), state = METHOD_READY) timed out ... 26 more
Do you know how to resolve such SessionBeanTimeoutExceptions in general?

Reference / gold answer:
To resolve SessionBeanTimeoutException in WebSphere Application Server, you can try the following steps:

1. Increase the session timeout value:
   - You can adjust the session timeout value in your WebSphere Application Server settings to allow the session beans more time to complete their tasks before timing out.

2. Check for any long-running processes:
   - Investigate if there are any long-running processes or tasks within your session beans that might be causing them to time out. Optimizing these processes can help prevent the timeout exceptions.

3. Review the server resources:
   - Ensure that your server has enough resources (CPU, memory, etc.) to handle the workload of your application. Insufficient resources can lead to performance issues and timeouts.

4. Check for any network issues:
   - Verify that there are no network issues causing communication delays between the application server and other components. Network problems can also contribute to timeout exceptions.

5. Monitor and analyze logs:
   - Monitor your server logs for any recurring timeout exceptions and analyze them to identify patterns or common causes. This can help you pinpoint the root cause of the timeouts.

6. Consider updating to the latest version:
   - If you are using an older version of WebSphere Application Server, consider updating to the latest version that may have bug fixes or improvements related to timeout handling.

By following these steps and investigating the specific circumstances of your SessionBeanTimeoutException, you should be able to diagnose and resolve the issue effectively.

- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere Extended Deployment   *
   *                 version 6.0.1.1.                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When  attempting to issue a             *
   *                      long-running scheduler command using    *
   *                      lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand    *
   *                      Router (ODR), an IOException will be    *
   *                      returned as follows:                    *
   *                                                              *
   *                      C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd    *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch :  *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\Simple *
   *                      CIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port>             *
   *                      -host=<ODR hostname> failed:            *
   *                      com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.      *
   *                      IOException:Connection close: Read      *
   *                      failed.  Possible end of stream         *
   *                      encountered.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The problem was caused by assuming in the code the every SOAP
   request will have a web module with web service and operation
   node defined. Therefore for the cases where web service and
   operation nodes do not exist, trying to use the operation map
   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.
- `E4.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  For each SOAP over HTTP request, check for the definition of
   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 The embedded WebSphere Application Server that is installed with IBM InfoSphere Content Collector can use only the Oracle ojdbc6.jar JDBC driver to connect to an Oracle data store.
- `E5.S3`: SYMPTOM
Errors like the following are logged:
- `E5.S4`: J2CA0036E: An exception occurred while invoking method setDataSourceProperties on com.ibm.ws.rsadapter.spi.WSManagedConnectionFactoryImpl used by resource jdbc/afuConfigurationDatabase : com.ibm.ws.exception.WsException: DSRA0023E: The DataSource implementation class "oracle.jdbc.xa.client.OracleXADataSource" could not be found.
- `E5.S5`: CAUSE
You can specify the directory of the JDBC driver in the IBM InfoSphere Content Collector Configuration Manager. However, you cannot specify a specific JDBC driver file.
- `E5.S6`: If you connect to an Oracle data store, Content Collector uses the value of the WebSphere environment variable ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH to locate the Oracle JDBC driver and assumes that the driver file name is ojdbc6.jar. If ojdbc6.jar is not found, the Content Collector WebApplications service cannot connect to the Oracle data store. Various connectivity errors are logged.
- `E5.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Check the resources.xmlfile in the directory
- `E5.S8`: <ContentCollector>\AFUWeb\profiles\<profile name>\config\cells\<CellName>\nodes\<nodename>
- `E5.S9`: Resolve the problem as mentioned below if it contains the following class path element:
<classpath>${ORACLE_JDBC_DRIVER_PATH}/ojdbc6.jar</classpath>
Do not modify the resources.xml file.
- `E5.S10`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To resolve the problem:
- `E5.S11`: 1. Create a copy of the Oracle JDBC driver that is installed on the IBM InfoSphere Content Collector system in the same location where the current driver resides (for example, copy ojdbc14.jar for Oracle 10g). 
 2. Rename the copy as ojdbc6.jar. 
 3. Restart the IBM InfoSphere Content Collector WebApplications service.

Visible answer:
The exception indicates that the stateful session bean’s session access timed out. [E1.S4] [E1.S5]

Increase the WebSphere session-access timeout by adding the JVM custom property `com.ibm.websphere.ejbcontainer.defaultSessionAccessTimeout` with the desired value, for example `30000`. In the administrative console, use Application servers > server name > Process definition > Java Virtual Machine > Custom properties, select New, add the property and value, save it, and restart the JVM for the change to take effect. [E1.S7]

- `E3.S1`: search; connections; work managers; CNTR0020E; node; start TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM
How to resolve an issue when the search application is starting on some nodes, but not others in a new deployment.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
On the WebSphere Integrated Solutions Console, the Search application status reports "Partial Start".
- `E3.S4`: Checking the systemout.log, you see messages like the following after attempting to start the Search application on these nodes:
- `E3.S5`: LocalExceptio E CNTR0020E: EJB threw an unexpected (non-declared) exception during invocation of method "getBean" on bean "BeanId(Search#dboard.search.ejb.jar#Search
ServiceLocator, null)". Exception data: org.springframework.beans.factory.access.BootstrapException: Unable to initialize group definition. Group resource name [classpath*:spring/search/app/SearchBeanRefF
actory.xml], factory key [spring.search.app]; nested exception is org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanCreationException: Error creating bean with name 'spring.search.app' defined in URL [wsjar:file:/E:/
IBM/WebSphere/AppServer/profiles/connect1/installedApps/ConnectionsCell/Search.ear/search.common.jar!/spring/search/app/SearchBeanRefFactory.xml]: Instantiation of bean failed; nested exception is org.springframework.beans.BeanInstantiationException: Could not instantiate bean class [org.springframework.context.support.ClassPathXmlApplicationContext]: Constructor threw exception; nested exception is org.springframework.beans.factory.BeanCreationException: Error creating bean with name 'INDEXER:dcsWorkManager' defined in class path resource [spring/search/service/IndexingServices.xml]: Invocation of init method failed; nested exception is javax.naming.NameNotFoundException: Context: ConnectionsCell/clusters/InfraCluster, name: wm/search-dcs: First component in name search-dcs not found. [Root exception is org.omg.CosNaming.NamingContextPackage.NotFound: IDL:omg.org/CosNaming/NamingContext/NotFound:1.0]
at org.springframework.beans.factory.access.SingletonBeanFactoryLocator.useBeanFactory(SingletonBeanFactoryLocator.java:389)
- `E3.S6`: ...
- `E3.S7`: CAUSE
When IBM Connections is first installed, each node is automatically given a Work Manager for Search. However, you must create the Work Managers manually for any subsequent nodes created. The behavior described here indicates that additional Work Managers have not been created.
- `E3.S8`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Once the Work Managers are created, the Search application should start on all affected Nodes. Instructions on how to do this are available here, in the IBM Connections documentation:
http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSYGQH_5.0.0/admin/admin/t_admin_search_create_work_managers.dita [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSYGQH_5.0.0/admin/admin/t_admin_search_create_work_managers.dita]

- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: All users of WebSphere Extended Deployment   *
   *                 version 6.0.1.1.                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: When  attempting to issue a             *
   *                      long-running scheduler command using    *
   *                      lrcmd.[bat|sh] through the On-Demand    *
   *                      Router (ODR), an IOException will be    *
   *                      returned as follows:                    *
   *                                                              *
   *                      C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\bin>lrcmd    *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4940I: com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch :  *
   *                      -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\SimpleCIxJCL.xml   *
   *                      -port=<ODR port> -host=<ODR hostname>   *
   *                                                              *
   *                      CWLRB4880E: -cmd=submit -xJCL=C:\Simple *
   *                      CIxJCL.xml -port=<ODR port>             *
   *                      -host=<ODR hostname> failed:            *
   *                      com.ibm.ws.batch.wsbatch: java.io.      *
   *                      IOException:Connection close: Read      *
   *                      failed.  Possible end of stream         *
   *                      encountered.                            *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   The problem was caused by assuming in the code the every SOAP
   request will have a web module with web service and operation
   node defined. Therefore for the cases where web service and
   operation nodes do not exist, trying to use the operation map
   to get a key results in a null pointer exception. To the
   caller this wrapped up exception shows up as an IO Exception.
- `E4.S9`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  For each SOAP over HTTP request, check for the definition of
   web service and web service operation nodes, if they exist use
   them to fetch the workclasses and perform further request
   classification as necessary, otherwise, use the original
   request mapping to route request.

- `E5.S1`: JNDI; EJB; EJB3; name; RES; BRES TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E5.S2`: QUESTION
 How do I deploy Rule Execution Server EJB rule sessions more than once, for each application that uses them on the same server, and call them remotely?
- `E5.S3`: ANSWER
An EJB module can be shared among several applications on the same server or cell. However, you will find it more convenient for maintainability to bundle Rule Execution Server EJB rule sessions within each application that calls Rule Execution Server through EJBs because doing so, you can redeploy the application EAR when necessary (for an application code or XOM modification, for example) without affecting the availability of other applications. You can also have those applications call different versions of Rule Execution Server.
- `E5.S4`: When you deploy the same EJB on the same server or cell more than once, you must give each instance a unique global JNDI name to avoid conflict errors, because those names need to uniquely identify a bean in a given context. See section "Rule Execution Server > Introducing Rule Execution Server > Rule Execution Server basics > JNDI bindings > Reference bindings for Rule Execution Server modules" of the JRules 7.1 documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/brjrules/v7r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.ilog.jrules.doc/Content/Business_Rules/Documentation/_pubskel/JRules/ps_JRules_Global941.html].
- `E5.S5`: Here is an example of the error you might get in WebSphere Application Server 7:
- `E5.S6`: Unable to start EJB jar, IlrStatelessRuleSessionEJB: The ilog.rules.bres.session.ejb.IlrStatelessRuleSessionHome interface of the IlrStatelessRuleSessionEJB bean in the jrules-res-session-WAS7.jar module of the jrules-res-session-WAS7_jar_2 application cannot be bound to the ejb/IlrStatelessRuleSessionEJB name location. The ilog.rules.bres.session.ejb.IlrStatelessRuleSessionHome interface of the IlrStatelessRuleSessionEJB bean in the jrules-res-session-WAS7.jar module of the jrules-res-session-WAS7_jar application has already been bound to the ejb/IlrStatelessRuleSessionEJB name location.
- `E5.S7`: For EJB3, you can set your own unique names for the EJB business interfaces at deployment time (see the documentation of your application server) or you can have them generated by the server automatically. For example, WebSphere AS 7 generates the following JNDI name for the remote business interface of Rule Execution Server stateless rule sessions:
- `E5.S8`: ejb/My RES application/jrules-res-session-ejb3-WAS7.jar/IlrStatelessSessionEJB3#ilog.rules.res.session.impl.ejb3.IlrStatelessSessionRemote
- `E5.S9`: (See "Network Deployment (All operating systems), Version 7.0 > Developing and deploying applications > EJB applications > Assembling EJB 3.x enterprise beans > EJB 3.0 application bindings overview > Default bindings for EJB business interfaces and homes" in the WebSphere AS 7 documentation [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/fep/topic/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/info/ae/ae/cejb_bindingsejbfp.html#cejbbindingsejbfp__ejb30defaultbindings])
- `E5.S10`: In that case, you must adjust the JNDI name in the Rule Execution Server client code by using the method IlrEJB3SessionFactory.setStatelessRemoteJndiName(String jndiName).
- `E5.S11`: For EJB2, you add a prefix to the JNDI names that are specified in the application-server-specific deployment descriptors and deployment scripts, or by using the console of your application server at deployment. For example:
- `E5.S12`: myApplication/ejb/IlrStatefulRuleSessionEJB
- `E5.S13`: and add that prefix at the end of the provider URL (java.naming.provider.url) on the client side through the rule session client API or in the jndi.properties file. For example, for WebSphere AS 7:
- `E5.S14`: corbaname:iiop:<host name>:<port>#myApplication
- `E5.S15`: *
- `E5.S16`: Note: Default JNDI names and provider URL formats vary from one application server to another. Refer to the corresponding documentation to know what is appropriate in your configuration. 
RELATED INFORMATION
#JNDI bindings for RES V7.5 [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/dmanager/v7r5/topic/com.ibm.dserver.res/Content/Business_Rules/_pubskel/Infocenter_Primary/ps_DS_Rule_Execution_Server1556.html]

- `E5.S18`: corbaname:iiop:<host name>:<port>#myApplication

Visible answer:
The exception indicates that access to the stateful session bean timed out; the documented cause is “Session access timed out.” [E1.S4] [E1.S5]

Increase the WebSphere EJB default session-access timeout by adding the JVM custom property `com.ibm.websphere.ejbcontainer.defaultSessionAccessTimeout` with the desired value, for example `30000`. In the administrative console, go to Application servers > server name > Process definition > Java Virtual Machine > Custom properties, select New, add the property and value, save it, and restart the JVM. ### techqa_DEV_Q106#row-0129

Question: Why does WebSphere DataPower spike with a high CPU rate when a WebSphere MQ connection is unavailable? I have noticed when my MQ backends go down unexpectedly it can result in a high CPU rate on DataPower. And how can I resolve this? 

Reference / gold answer:
When the WebSphere MQ connection is unavailable, WebSphere DataPower spikes with a high CPU rate because the value of Retry Attempts is set to 0 on the DataPower MQ Queue Manager object, which leads to continuous retry attempts using the specified Retry Interval. 

The solution to this issue is to change the Retry Attempts parameter on the Configure MQ Queue Manager window from 0 to a specific number, such as 6. Additionally, it is recommended to change the Retry Interval to a longer period, such as 10 seconds, and set a Long Retry Interval of, for example, 600 seconds (10 minutes). This configuration allows the MQ Queue Manager object to retry a set number of times with intervals and then switch to longer intervals after those attempts, preventing continuous high CPU usage when the MQ connection is unavailable.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `3b`:  Why does WebSphere DataPower spike with a high CPU rate when a WebSphere MQ connection is unavailable?
- `3c`: Is there a solution to this issue? CAUSE
- `3d`: If the value of Retry Attempts is set to 0 on the DataPower MQ Queue Manager object, this negates the benefits of the Long Retry Interval since it will not be used.
- `3e`: DataPower will retry forever using the specified Retry Interval.
- `3f`: The default setting of Retry Attempts as 0 and Retry Interval as 1 second is provided to preserve backward compatibility.
- `3g`: However, these default values should be changed to take advantage of Long Retry Interval feature available in firmware. ANSWER
- `3h`: The solution to the issue of having DataPower vulnerable to the MQ Queue Manager being inaccessible is to change the Retry Attempts parameter on the Configure MQ Queue Manager window from 0 to some number.
- `3i`: As an example, change the parameters as follows:
- `3j`:  *  Retry Attempts - change the default of 0 to 6 Retry Interval - change the default of 1 to 10 seconds Long Retry Interval - change the default of 1800 to 600 seconds (10 minutes)
- `3k`: In the event that the Queue Manager is down or a connection is not established, the above example configuration will allow the MQ QM Object to retry 6 times with 10 second intervals.
- `3l`: After 6 attempts, the MQ QM object will retry every 10 minutes.

- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 Why does WebSphere DataPower spike with a high CPU rate when a WebSphere MQ connection is unavailable? Is there a solution to this issue?
- `E1.S3`: CAUSE
If the value of Retry Attempts is set to 0 on the DataPower MQ Queue Manager object, this negates the benefits of the Long Retry Interval since it will not be used. DataPower will retry forever using the specified Retry Interval. The default setting of Retry Attempts as 0 and Retry Interval as 1 second is provided to preserve backward compatibility. However, these default values should be changed to take advantage of Long Retry Interval feature available in firmware.
- `E1.S4`: ANSWER
The solution to the issue of having DataPower vulnerable to the MQ Queue Manager being inaccessible is to change the Retry Attempts parameter on the Configure MQ Queue Manager window from 0 to some number. As an example, change the parameters as follows:
- `E1.S5`: *  Retry Attempts - change the default of 0 to 6 Retry Interval - change the default of 1 to 10 seconds Long Retry Interval - change the default of 1800 to 600 seconds (10 minutes)
- `E1.S6`: In the event that the Queue Manager is down or a connection is not established, the above example configuration will allow the MQ QM Object to retry 6 times with 10 second intervals. After 6 attempts, the MQ QM object will retry every 10 minutes.
- `E1.S7`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower Integration Appliance XI50 Firmware 3.8 Business Integration WebSphere DataPower Low Latency Appliance XM70 Firmware 3.8

- `E2.S4`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E2.S5`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  CPU usage can spike and cause performance degradation when new
   synchronous replicas request data from primary shards during
   startup.
- `E2.S6`: LOCAL FIX
 *  TBD
- `E2.S7`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  WebSphere eXtreme Scale users running with  *
   *                  the eXtreme IO (XIO) transport.             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: New synchronous replicas that           *
   *                      aggressively copy data from the         *
   *                      primary shard can cause high CPU        *
   *                      usage.                                  *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   New synchronous replicas request data quickly from primary
   shards during startup. The aggressive replication can cause
   high CPU usage during this time. After a synchronous replica
   copies all the existing data from the primary shard, it
   receives data in real time from the primary shard, and the CPU
   returns to normal.
   Customers using asynchronous replicas can see a similar
   problem when primary shards move to new containers. The method
   of transferring an existing primary to a new location uses a
   temporary synchronous replica and can see high CPU usage
   during this time.
   This fix automatically regulates the replication rate based on
   how fast the primary shard responds to the synchronous replica
   in XIO environments.
- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Apply the interim fix.

   The queue manager works normally. When machine is loaded with

   the system schedules other tasks. But anyway because of the
   high CPU intensive monitoring by the process manager some

- `E4.S1`: 720limitation; MQ; CERTLABL; 2539; 0x000009eb; MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 After setting CERTLABL for an SSL channel on MQ Server, DataPower can no longer connect to that channel.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
When CERTLABL is configured on the channel that DataPower is using to connect to queue manager, the connection would fail and DataPower MQ Queue Manager object would be down.
- `E4.S4`: The following errors will be seen in the DataPower logs:
- `E4.S5`: * [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): test connection failed (2539) 
   [mq][error] mq-qm(mqqm): tid(238161): Queue Manager Error: 'mq-server.ibm.com:1111' ''. Reason code - 2539 
   The reason code is: 2539 0x000009eb MQRC_CHANNEL_CONFIG_ERROR
- `E4.S6`: On MQ Server, there will be error logs explaining this connection failure:  * 
 * 
 *
- `E4.S7`: * 
 * The SSL or TLS channel 'SSL.SVRCONN.2' is configured to use certificate label 
   'SSL.SVRCONN.2'. However, the remote peer did not send the necessary 
   information to allow the local channel to use the correct certificate. The 
   remote host is 'datapower (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx)'.
- `E4.S8`: * This error occurs when the local channel definition has a certificate label and 
   the remote peer does not support selection of certificates. 
   The channel did not start.
- `E4.S9`: * 
 * Ensure that the remote peer supports certificate label configuration. Refer to 
   the Security section of the WebSphere MQ Information Center for details of 
   certificate label requirements. Alternatively, alter the local channel 
   definition so that it does not specify a certificate label.
- `E4.S10`: CAUSE
MQ version 8 and the later version provides a new parameter "CERTLABL" for administrators to specify a certificate to be used when making a SSL connection to a channel. This allows multiple certificates to be configured, one for each channel. All certificates are managed in the same queue manager on MQ Server. In order to utilize this function, both ends of the channel must be running MQ version 8 or the later version and must support Server Name Indication (SNI). 
Although DataPower version 7.2.0 runs MQ version 8 client and also supports SNI for the rest of the services, it does not support SNI for MQ Queue Manager object.
- `E4.S11`: ENVIRONMENT
MQ Server version 8, DataPower version 7.2.0
- `E4.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
In order for DataPower to connect to the queue manager, the CERTLABL must be removed from the channel, which means you must not configure the CERTLABL on the MQ Server. After removing the CERTLABL from the channel, the channel would use the default certificate as configured in queue manager's properties.
- `E4.S13`: RELATED INFORMATION
 IBM MQ V8 Features and Enhancements [http://www.redbooks.ibm.com/redbooks/pdfs/sg248218.pdf]
- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When to enable Sharing Conversations in DataPower MQ Queue Manager (mq-qm) object along with SHARECNV attribute of the MQ SVRCONN channel?
- `E5.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases provide sharing conversations (SHARECNV) attribute on SVRCONN channel that specifies the maximum number of conversations that can share each TCP/IP channel instance. This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel. 
The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object. The same default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is 
negotiated between MQ server and DataPower and the lower value takes effect. However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server.
- `E5.S4`: There are three use cases to configure Sharing Conversations in DataPower mq-qm object:
- `E5.S5`: Case #1 : The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0 - The channel runs in a mode similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not uses features such as
- `E5.S6`: · Administrator stop-quiesce
· Heartbeating 
· Read ahead 
· Client asynchronous consume
- `E5.S7`: Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower to disable sharing conversations regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E5.S8`: Case #2: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 1 - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features as outlined in case #1, but each TCP/IP channel instance has a single conversation.
- `E5.S9`: Set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower as shown in the following picture and a value of 1 on IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E5.S10`: The Share Single Conversation attribute is only visible when "Sharing Conversations" is configured with value of "1" and then <RETURN> key is entered. For values greater than 1, the "Share Single Conversation" attribute is hidden in the mq-qm object.
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1]
- `E5.S11`: Case #3: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features and each TCP/IP channel instance supports 2 or more conversations.
- `E5.S12`: Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower and on the MQ SVRCONN channel.
- `E5.S13`: On average, processing of messages from client applications is 15 percent slower when using SHARECNV(10) as compared to SHARECNV(0). Please refer to Performance Implications of Sharing [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm]
Conversations on Client-connection Channels. [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm].
- `E5.S14`: Since DataPower uses a connection pool in processing MQ messages, there are no additional benefits of using sharing conversations with the mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E5.S15`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call.

Visible answer:
Resolve the issue by changing Retry Attempts from 0 to a finite number in the Configure MQ Queue Manager window. One example is Retry Attempts = 6, Retry Interval = 10 seconds, and Long Retry Interval = 600 seconds (10 minutes). [E1.S4] [E1.S5]

Support units:
- `E1.S1`: retries; high CPU; MQ queue manager; Retry Interval; Retry Attempts; Long Retry Interval TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 Why does WebSphere DataPower spike with a high CPU rate when a WebSphere MQ connection is unavailable? Is there a solution to this issue?
- `E1.S3`: CAUSE
If the value of Retry Attempts is set to 0 on the DataPower MQ Queue Manager object, this negates the benefits of the Long Retry Interval since it will not be used. DataPower will retry forever using the specified Retry Interval. The default setting of Retry Attempts as 0 and Retry Interval as 1 second is provided to preserve backward compatibility. However, these default values should be changed to take advantage of Long Retry Interval feature available in firmware.
- `E1.S4`: ANSWER
The solution to the issue of having DataPower vulnerable to the MQ Queue Manager being inaccessible is to change the Retry Attempts parameter on the Configure MQ Queue Manager window from 0 to some number. As an example, change the parameters as follows:
- `E1.S5`: *  Retry Attempts - change the default of 0 to 6 Retry Interval - change the default of 1 to 10 seconds Long Retry Interval - change the default of 1800 to 600 seconds (10 minutes)
- `E1.S6`: In the event that the Queue Manager is down or a connection is not established, the above example configuration will allow the MQ QM Object to retry 6 times with 10 second intervals. After 6 attempts, the MQ QM object will retry every 10 minutes.
- `E1.S7`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower Integration Appliance XI50 Firmware 3.8 Business Integration WebSphere DataPower Low Latency Appliance XM70 Firmware 3.8
- `E2.S1`: FIXES ARE AVAILABLE
Fix packs for DataPower Gateway version 7.1 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24038524]
Fix packs for DataPower Gateway version 7.5 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24041543]

- `E3.S4`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E3.S5`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  CPU usage can spike and cause performance degradation when new
   synchronous replicas request data from primary shards during
   startup.
- `E3.S6`: LOCAL FIX
 *  TBD
- `E3.S7`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  WebSphere eXtreme Scale users running with  *
   *                  the eXtreme IO (XIO) transport.             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: New synchronous replicas that           *
   *                      aggressively copy data from the         *
   *                      primary shard can cause high CPU        *
   *                      usage.                                  *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   New synchronous replicas request data quickly from primary
   shards during startup. The aggressive replication can cause
   high CPU usage during this time. After a synchronous replica
   copies all the existing data from the primary shard, it
   receives data in real time from the primary shard, and the CPU
   returns to normal.
   Customers using asynchronous replicas can see a similar
   problem when primary shards move to new containers. The method
   of transferring an existing primary to a new location uses a
   temporary synchronous replica and can see high CPU usage
   during this time.
   This fix automatically regulates the replication rate based on
   how fast the primary shard responds to the synchronous replica
   in XIO environments.
- `E3.S8`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Apply the interim fix.
