- `E4.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When to enable Sharing Conversations in DataPower MQ Queue Manager (mq-qm) object along with SHARECNV attribute of the MQ SVRCONN channel?
- `E4.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases provide sharing conversations (SHARECNV) attribute on SVRCONN channel that specifies the maximum number of conversations that can share each TCP/IP channel instance. This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel. 
The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object. The same default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is 
negotiated between MQ server and DataPower and the lower value takes effect. However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server.
- `E4.S4`: There are three use cases to configure Sharing Conversations in DataPower mq-qm object:
- `E4.S5`: Case #1 : The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0 - The channel runs in a mode similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not uses features such as
- `E4.S6`: · Administrator stop-quiesce
· Heartbeating 
· Read ahead 
· Client asynchronous consume
- `E4.S7`: Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower to disable sharing conversations regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E4.S8`: Case #2: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 1 - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features as outlined in case #1, but each TCP/IP channel instance has a single conversation.
- `E4.S9`: Set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower as shown in the following picture and a value of 1 on IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E4.S10`: The Share Single Conversation attribute is only visible when "Sharing Conversations" is configured with value of "1" and then <RETURN> key is entered. For values greater than 1, the "Share Single Conversation" attribute is hidden in the mq-qm object.
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1]
- `E4.S11`: Case #3: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features and each TCP/IP channel instance supports 2 or more conversations.
- `E4.S12`: Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower and on the MQ SVRCONN channel.
- `E4.S13`: On average, processing of messages from client applications is 15 percent slower when using SHARECNV(10) as compared to SHARECNV(0). Please refer to Performance Implications of Sharing [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm]
Conversations on Client-connection Channels. [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm].
- `E4.S14`: Since DataPower uses a connection pool in processing MQ messages, there are no additional benefits of using sharing conversations with the mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E4.S15`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call.
- `E4.S16`: mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E4.S17`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call. However, when mixed message sizes are processed by the same MQ Front Side Handler (FSH), it requests buffer pool based on maximum message size configured in the mq-qm object. The use of fixed buffer pool for small and large messages can deplete MQ server's allocated buffer and contribute to unexpected termination of MQ SVRCONN channel instance and may terminate the queue manager. In such a situation, using a negotiated sharing conversations value of 1 as in case #2 will benefit DataPower mq-qm object as it will use IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 Read Ahead feature and the new buffer management feature for MQGET API call. IBM WebSphere MQ V8 release provides enhanced performance for case #2, when the negotiated sharing conversations value is 1.
- `E4.S18`: For DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, one should follow case #1 and use a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0. If you configure these firmware versions with case #2 or case #3, DataPower device may reload or hang due to connection instability and generate many MQ errors with Reason Code - 2009 and 2059.
- `E4.S19`: Cases #2 and #3 can be used in firmware releases 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later. We suggest to use a value of 10 or less in Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object and verify the configuration empirically to make sure that IBM WebSphere MQ server can sustain load from DataPower with the negotiated Sharing Conversations of 10.
- `E4.S20`: Note: In order to use sharing conversations, make sure you have applied APAR IV24821 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IV24821] ("Client C application process hangs after cancelling thread") to the IBM WebSphere MQ server. IV24821 is included in IBM WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.10 and later, IBM WebSphere MQ V7.1.0.3 and later, IBM WebSphere MQ V7.5.0.1 and later, and IBM WebSphere MQ V8.
- `E4.S21`: In order to identify the negotiated Sharing Conversations status, the following MQ commands are used in the distributed platform.
- `E4.S22`: runmqsc <qmgr>
display chs(CHANNEL3) maxshcnv curshcnv
- `E4.S23`: display chs(CHANNEL3) maxshcnv curshcnv

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
Resolve it by changing Retry Attempts from 0 to a finite number in the DataPower MQ Queue Manager configuration. One example is Retry Attempts = 6, Retry Interval = 10 seconds, and Long Retry Interval = 600 seconds (10 minutes). [E1.S4] [E1.S5]

With that example, DataPower retries six times at 10-second intervals when the queue manager is down, then retries every 10 minutes. [E1.S6]

A separate high-CPU issue is documented for MQ Sharing Conversation: customers using MQ Sharing Conversation can get high CPU, and a fix is available in DataPower 7.1.0.7. [E2.S7] [E2.S8]

For older DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, the Sharing Conversations guidance is to use a negotiated value of 0; configuring values of 1 or more may cause reloads or hangs due to connection instability and generate MQ reason codes 2009 and 2059. [E4.S18]

### techqa_DEV_Q135#row-0131

Question: DataPower upgrade message Loading firmware failed: Preserve user modified data failed: Insufficient flash space available Could not install firmware image. The system will not reboot. In the process of upgrading my IBM DataPower Gateway I saw the following message:
"Loading firmware failed: Preserve user modified data failed: Insufficient flash space available Could not install firmware image. The system will not reboot."
What does this mean and what are the appropriate next actions? 

Reference / gold answer:
The error message indicates that there is not enough available flash memory space on the IBM DataPower Gateway to install the firmware image. In this case, the system is unable to reboot after the failed installation.

To address this issue, the appropriate next actions would be:

1. Check the available flash memory space on the IBM DataPower Gateway to determine how much space is currently being used and how much is available.
2. If possible, free up additional space on the flash memory by deleting unnecessary files or data to make room for the firmware installation.
3. Consider removing any user-modified data that may be taking up unnecessary space and preventing the firmware installation.
4. Once enough space is available, attempt to install the firmware image again.
5. If the issue persists, consult IBM support for further assistance in resolving the insufficient flash space error and successfully completing the firmware upgrade.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `4d`: This firmware release includes improved capability and new features for WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Version 2.1.
- `4e`: Caution: After you upgrade either 9235-92X or 7199-92X appliance types with Version 2.1 firmware, you cannot roll back to any previous firmware version.
- `4g`: When you are upgrading to Version 2.1, you cannot run a firmware upgrade on a collective that is currently servicing workload.
- `4i`: In addition, all members of the collective must be upgraded to the same major version (Version 2.1.0.x) before service can be restored.
- `4j`: Upgrades between fix packs, for example, versions 2.1.0.0 to 2.1.0.1, can be done with no loss of service and while servicing workload as long as each appliance is upgraded individually and you wait for the upgraded appliance to reboot and re-replicate before proceeding to upgrade the next appliance.
- `4k`: When you are running firmware upgrades on the appliances in a collective from a version prior to 2.1, the appliance that you upgrade does not fully restart until all of the appliances in the collective are upgraded to Version 2.1.

- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 How do I add the Application Optimization feature to an IBM WebSphere DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance?
- `E1.S3`: The following document provides assistance on upgrading a DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance to add the Option for Application Optimization feature.
- `E1.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To add the Application Optimization feature:
- `E1.S5`: * The appliance must be a Type 9235 XML Security Gateway XS40 or Integration Appliance XI50 running firmware 3.7.3.0 or later or must be a Type 4195 Integration Blade XI50B running firmware 3.8.1.0 or later.
   Note: For Type 7199 appliances, see technote 1501194 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501194]. 
 * You purchased the feature and received a letter that contains the Controlled Access Key to download the firmware image.
- `E1.S6`: Part 1: Accessing the Web site that contains the firmware image. 
Using your IBM account and Controlled Access Key, access the web site to download the firmware image that contains the Application Optimization feature. 
 1. Identify the serial number for your appliance  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Version Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show version command.
- `E1.S7`: 2. Follow the instructions in the Authorized Feature Download letter to access the WebSphere DataPower Registered Downloads portal [http://www.ibm.com/services/forms/preLogin.do?lang=en_US&source=swg-datapowerapps]. 
 3. Sign in using your IBM user ID and password. Register, if you do not have an ID. 
 4. Enter the Controlled Access Key in the letter to access the web page containing the firmware images. Ensure that the first 7-characters of the Controlled Access Key in the letter matches the serial number for the appliance that you obtained in step 1.
- `E1.S8`: You are now ready to continue to Part 2 to download the firmware image.
- `E1.S9`: Part 2: Downloading the firmware image. 
Determine which firmware image you need and download that image.
- `E1.S10`: Notes:  * Starting with version 3.8.1, firmware that contain the MQ libraries do not contain .mq as part of its file name. 
 * If you purchased the Option for Application Optimization feature after 10-June-2011, there is only a single image. Therefore, you do not need to identify libraries to determine which image to download.
- `E1.S11`: 1. Identify the library information for your appliance. That is whether the appliance has the libraries for the Database connection (ODBC), IBM Tivoli Access Manager (TAM), WebSphere MQ (MQ), and TIBCO EMS features.  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Library Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show library-version command.
- `E1.S12`: 2. Download the image that corresponds to the available libraries on your appliance. For example:  * Download xs3800.tam6.scrypt2 if your XML Security Gateway XS40 has TAM 6.0 
     * Download xi3800.mq.odbc.tam61.scrypt2 if your Integration Appliance XI50 has ODBC, MQ, and TAM 6.1
- `E1.S13`: 3. Do not transfer the image to the appliance at this time. You will install the image in Part 4: Installing the firmware image.
- `E1.S14`: Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash.
- `E1.S15`: at this time. You will install the image in Part 4: Installing the firmware image.
- `E1.S16`: Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade.

- `E1.S18`: Part 4: Installing the firmware image. 
Install the firmware image. Each firmware image uses the serial number of the appliance as the key. 
 1. Remove appliance from production. 
 2. Following the instructions upgrade documentation in the information center:  * Remove extraneous files 
     * Reboot the appliance to release temporary storage 
     * Transfer the firmware image to the appliance 
     * Install the firmware image

- `E1.S20`: If the installation is successful and the list does not include the Application Optimization feature, the most likely reason is that the firmware image was for a different appliance. Each firmware image to add the Application Optimization feature uses the serial number of the appliance as the key. If you install a downloaded image to a different appliance, you will notice that the firmware is upgraded to that firmware level and that the Application for Optimization feature is not available.
- `E1.S21`: If you accessed the download site using the Controlled Access Key and installed the downloaded image to the appliance with the matching serial number and the feature list does not include the Application Optimization feature, contact IBM Support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322].

When reporting the problem to IBM Support, the representative will need your Controlled Access Key in addition to the standard information to include. Go to Contacting IBM WebSphere DataPower Appliances Support [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21236322].

- `E2.S1`: you begin. 1. Ensure that the server is in service processor standby. Service processor standby is indicated when the server is powered off, and the power-on LED on the control panel is blinking slowly. 2. Insert the USB flash drive into one of the following:
- `E2.S2`: o The top USB port on the back on a rack-mounted system
o The right-most USB port on a deskside system 
For additional information, refer to the Location Codes section in the host model of the service guide.
- `E2.S3`: The firmware level will load automatically. The level of firmware on the USB flash drive will be installed onto both the P and T sides of the service processor assembly.
- `E2.S4`: Several checkpoints will be posted on the control panel during the installation of the firmware. They are as follows:
- `E2.S5`: o C100B101: The firmware image is being installed on a side of the flash. 
o C100B102: The firmware image is being installed on the other side of the flash. 
o C100B103: The firmware installation has been completed successfully.
- `E2.S6`: Note: If a C100B104 code is displayed, the firmware installation has failed. You should perform the following steps:
- `E2.S7`: 1. Ensure that the USB flash drive contains the firmware fix. If necessary, copy the firmware to the USB flash drive again. 
2. Retry the task with another USB flash drive. 
3. If necessary, consult your service provider. 
4. After checkpoint C100B103 is displayed on the control panel, you can safely remove the USB flash drive. 
5. Continue with verifying that the firmware installed correctly.
- `E2.S8`: Verifying that the firmware installed correctly
- `E2.S9`: To verify that the firmware installed correctly, you should perform the following steps: 1. Access the ASMI and view the level of server firmware displayed in the upper-right corner below the copyright statement on the Welcome pane. 2. Verify that the level of server firmware that is displayed is the level that you installed. 3. If the level of server firmware that is displayed is not the level that you installed, retry installing the firmware using another USB flash drive. If the problem persists, contact your next level of support.

- `E3.S1`: DOWNLOADABLE FILES
- `E3.S2`: ABSTRACT
 Download the IBM WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Version 2.1 firmware upgrade. You can also download the client, which is required for WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance to work
- `E3.S3`: DOWNLOAD DESCRIPTION
This firmware release includes improved capability and new features for WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Version 2.1.
- `E3.S4`: Caution: After you upgrade either 9235-92X or 7199-92X appliance types with Version 2.1 firmware, you cannot roll back to any previous firmware version. You must operate at the Version 2.1 or higher firmware level.
- `E3.S5`: When you are upgrading to Version 2.1, you cannot run a firmware upgrade on a collective that is currently servicing workload. When you upgrade a collective from a previous major version of DataPower XC10 Appliance, all of the data, not including your configuration, that was loaded into the data grids is lost. In addition, all members of the collective must be upgraded to the same major version (Version 2.1.0.x) before service can be restored. Upgrades between fix packs, for example, versions 2.1.0.0 to 2.1.0.1, can be done with no loss of service and while servicing workload as long as each appliance is upgraded individually and you wait for the upgraded appliance to reboot and re-replicate before proceeding to upgrade the next appliance. When you are running firmware upgrades on the appliances in a collective from a version prior to 2.1, the appliance that you upgrade does not fully restart until all of the appliances in the collective are upgraded to Version 2.1.
- `E3.S6`: You must complete the firmware upgrade process on one appliance before starting the process on another appliance within the collective. Do not make any configuration changes until all of the appliances are on the same firmware level. See Updating the firmware [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/wdpxc/v2r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.datapower.xc.doc/aa/aat_updating_firmware.html] in the WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Information Center, for more information.
- `E3.S7`: For IBM WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance to work with WebSphere Application Server or clients in a stand-alone environment, you must install the WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client or package the client Java archive (JAR) files with your application. You can download the client from this document as well.
- `E3.S8`: Client installation: If you have a previous version of the client, an upgrade is not available. Use IBM Installation Manager to install the full version of the client.
- `E3.S9`: INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS
Complete the following instructions to download the firmware and client images.
- `E3.S10`: 1. Initialize and configure the appliance.
    The firmware upgrades for the 9235-92x and 7199-92x appliances are available in this document. See Initializing and configuring WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wdpxc/v2r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.datapower.xc.doc/tinitappl.html] in the product information center for more information about the initialization and firmware upgrade process. 
 2. Install the client for your appliance to work.  1. Download one or more of the following images from this page:
        Description File name WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client in a stand-alone environment image_xs_client.8500.zip WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client for WebSphere Application Server Version 6 image_xs_client_was6.8500.zip WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client for WebSphere Application Server Version 7 image_xs_client_was7.8500.zip WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client for WebSphere Application Server Version 8 image_xs_client_was8.8500.zip 
     2. Install IBM Installation Manager [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24031300].

- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 A 9235 appliance may restart or in rare cases the boot up may not complete due to Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) communications loss.
- `E4.S3`: CAUSE
NOTE: DataPower highly recommends upgrading to a version containing the fix for APAR IC80983
- `E4.S4`: A DataPower 9235 appliance may be restarted without a back trace by its hardware watchdog due to a Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) communications loss.
- `E4.S5`: This also rarely causes a failure to restart successfully.
- `E4.S6`: If a failure to restart occurs, the appliance needs to be manually power cycled by removing and then replacing the power cords.
- `E4.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Due to the potential impact of this problem, DataPower highly recommends upgrading to a version containing the fix for APAR IC80983.

- `E4.S11`: The fix was first included in the 3.8.1.20, 3.8.2.11, 4.0.1.8, and 4.0.2.4 fixpacks. Please install [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21237631]this fixpack level or higher.

- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 How do I add the Application Optimization feature to an IBM WebSphere DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance?
- `E1.S3`: The following document provides assistance on upgrading a DataPower Type 9235 or Type 4195 appliance to add the Option for Application Optimization feature.
- `E1.S4`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To add the Application Optimization feature:
- `E1.S5`: * The appliance must be a Type 9235 XML Security Gateway XS40 or Integration Appliance XI50 running firmware 3.7.3.0 or later or must be a Type 4195 Integration Blade XI50B running firmware 3.8.1.0 or later.
   Note: For Type 7199 appliances, see technote 1501194 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21501194]. 
 * You purchased the feature and received a letter that contains the Controlled Access Key to download the firmware image.
- `E1.S6`: Part 1: Accessing the Web site that contains the firmware image. 
Using your IBM account and Controlled Access Key, access the web site to download the firmware image that contains the Application Optimization feature. 
 1. Identify the serial number for your appliance  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Version Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show version command.
- `E1.S7`: 2. Follow the instructions in the Authorized Feature Download letter to access the WebSphere DataPower Registered Downloads portal [http://www.ibm.com/services/forms/preLogin.do?lang=en_US&source=swg-datapowerapps]. 
 3. Sign in using your IBM user ID and password. Register, if you do not have an ID. 
 4. Enter the Controlled Access Key in the letter to access the web page containing the firmware images. Ensure that the first 7-characters of the Controlled Access Key in the letter matches the serial number for the appliance that you obtained in step 1.
- `E1.S8`: You are now ready to continue to Part 2 to download the firmware image.
- `E1.S9`: Part 2: Downloading the firmware image. 
Determine which firmware image you need and download that image.
- `E1.S10`: Notes:  * Starting with version 3.8.1, firmware that contain the MQ libraries do not contain .mq as part of its file name. 
 * If you purchased the Option for Application Optimization feature after 10-June-2011, there is only a single image. Therefore, you do not need to identify libraries to determine which image to download.
- `E1.S11`: 1. Identify the library information for your appliance. That is whether the appliance has the libraries for the Database connection (ODBC), IBM Tivoli Access Manager (TAM), WebSphere MQ (MQ), and TIBCO EMS features.  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Library Information. 
     * From the command line, issue the show library-version command.
- `E1.S12`: 2. Download the image that corresponds to the available libraries on your appliance. For example:  * Download xs3800.tam6.scrypt2 if your XML Security Gateway XS40 has TAM 6.0 
     * Download xi3800.mq.odbc.tam61.scrypt2 if your Integration Appliance XI50 has ODBC, MQ, and TAM 6.1
- `E1.S13`: 3. Do not transfer the image to the appliance at this time. You will install the image in Part 4: Installing the firmware image.
- `E1.S14`: Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash.
- `E1.S15`: at this time. You will install the image in Part 4: Installing the firmware image.
- `E1.S16`: Part 3: Preparing for the firmware upgrade. 
Review the installation instructions and prepare your appliance for the firmware upgrade. 
 1. Read the upgrade documentation in the version-specific DataPower information center. Instructions for accessing the correct information center is in the [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=2362&uid=swg21377654]IBM WebSphere DataPower Product Documentation Portal [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21377654] technical flash. The steps in this flash provide additional information to use with the upgrade documentation in the information center. 
 2. Save the current configuration.  * From the WebGUI, click Save Config. 
     * From the command line, issue the write memory command.
- `E1.S17`: 3. Create a backup of the entire system, and store the configuration in a safe location off of the appliance. 
 4. Confirm that you have a working admin account and a back up privileged account that can change the password for the admin account, if needed. 
 5. Make sure that the passwords for both accounts were recently changed.
- `E1.S18`: Part 4: Installing the firmware image. 
Install the firmware image. Each firmware image uses the serial number of the appliance as the key. 
 1. Remove appliance from production.

     * Reboot the appliance to release temporary storage 
     * Transfer the firmware image to the appliance 
     * Install the firmware image
- `E1.S19`: 3. Verify that the appliance has the Application Optimization feature.  * From the WebGUI, click Status -> System -> Device Features. The list includes Option for Application Optimization. 
     * From the command line, issue the show features command. The list includes AppOpt.
- `E1.S20`: If the installation is successful and the list does not include the Application Optimization feature, the most likely reason is that the firmware image was for a different appliance. Do not make any configuration changes until all of the appliances are on the same firmware level. See Updating the firmware [http://pic.dhe.ibm.com/infocenter/wdpxc/v2r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.datapower.xc.doc/aa/aat_updating_firmware.html] in the WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance Information Center, for more information.
- `E2.S7`: For IBM WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance to work with WebSphere Application Server or clients in a stand-alone environment, you must install the WebSphere eXtreme Scale Client or package the client Java archive (JAR) files with your application. You can download the client from this document as well.
- `E2.S8`: Client installation: If you have a previous version of the client, an upgrade is not available. Use IBM Installation Manager to install the full version of the client.
- `E2.S9`: INSTALLATION INSTRUCTIONS
Complete the following instructions to download the firmware and client images.
- `E2.S10`: 1. Initialize and configure the appliance.
    The firmware upgrades for the 9235-92x and 7199-92x appliances are available in this document. See Initializing and configuring WebSphere DataPower XC10 Appliance [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wdpxc/v2r1/topic/com.ibm.websphere.datapower.xc.doc/tinitappl.html] in the product information center for more information about the initialization and firmware upgrade process. 
 2. Install the client for your appliance to work.  1. Download one or more of the following images from this page:

     2. Install IBM Installation Manager [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg24031300].

- `E3.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 What is included in the encrypted and temporary directories in the 9235/9004 and 7199/7198 IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliances?
- `E3.S3`: ANSWER
The IBM WebSphere DataPower SOA Appliance file system is split into several sections when viewing the "show filesystem" CLI command or Status -> Filesystem Information in the WebGUI:
Encrypted space, Temporary space and Internal space.
- `E3.S4`: * Encrypted Space:
- `E3.S5`: * 
 *

 * Setting up and troubleshooting the RAID Array on a 9235 device with optional hard drives 
 *

 * 
 * Temporary and Internal Space
   The "temporary" and "internal" space are not persisted storage and the files will be lost if the appliance is rebooted or powered down but will not be cleared if use the "Reload" option.
- `E3.S6`: The temporary space includes these user accessible directories: temporary, image, export and logtemp 
   The internal space is not accessible by the user.
- `E3.S7`: Both the "temporary" and "internal" space are also used for various processing actions during operation.
- `E3.S8`: NOTES: 
1) It is not possible to account for all the space displayed in the "show filesystem" output by adding the file sizes as there are internal files as well as the "rollback image" that are not visible to the user.
- `E3.S9`: 2) In the M/T 7199 and 7198 the "temporary" and "internal" space listed in the "show filesystem" output will vary by firmware release. This is due to how the available memory is utilized in each release.

 Log viewer vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System.
- `E2.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2014-6190 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-6190]

Visible answer:
The IBM PureApplication System bulletin states that IBM WebSphere Application Server contains a vulnerability allowing a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions. [E1.S2] [E1.S3]

For the detailed vulnerability information, consult IBM’s bulletin “Security Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server” at http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883573. [E1.S4]

The bulletin identifies CVE-2015-1920, with a CVSS base score of 9.3 and vector (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C). [E1.S3]

Affected products listed are IBM PureApplication System versions 2.1, 2.0, and 1.1. [E1.S5] [E1.S6]

Support units:
- `E1.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E1.S2`: SUMMARY
 IBM PureApplication System contains IBM WebSphere Application Server, which has a security vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.
- `E1.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2015-1920 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-1920]
DESCRIPTION: WebSphere Application Server could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and executing a specific sequence of instructions.
CVSS Base Score: 9.3
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/102404 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/102404] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C)
- `E1.S4`: Please consult the security bulletin: Security Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883573]for additional vulnerability details and information
- `E1.S5`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
IBM PureApplication Server bundles WebSphere Application Server in its Web Application Pattern.
- `E1.S6`: IBM PureApplication System V2.1
IBM PureApplication System V2.0
IBM PureApplication System V1.1
- `E1.S7`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
The solution is to apply an update to the Web Application pattern type included in IBM PureApplication System:
- `E1.S8`: IBM PureApplication System V2.1
· Web Application Pattern Type V2.0.4.2
http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-2.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=fc [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-2.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=fc]
- `E1.S9`: · Web Application Pattern Type V1.0.4.2
http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-1.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=f [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=PureSystems&product=ibm/WebSphere/PureApplication+System&release=All&platform=All&function=fixId&fixids=webapp-1.0.4.2-sys&includeSupersedes=0&source=f]
- `E1.S10`: IBM PureApplication System V2.0 
The solution is to upgrade to IBM PureApplication System V2.0.0.1 Interim Fix 5

Contact IBM customer support for upgrade options.

- `E2.S2`: SUMMARY
 Log viewer vulnerability affects IBM PureApplication System.

CVEID: CVE-2014-6190 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2014-6190]

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
The requested IBM PureApplication System bulletin is documented in the supplied security bulletin. It describes CVE-2015-1920 in the bundled WebSphere Application Server: a remote attacker could execute arbitrary code by connecting to a management port and following a specific sequence of instructions. The CVSS base score is 9.3, with vector AV:N/AC:M/Au:N/C:C/I:C/A:C. [E1.S2] [E1.S3]

For additional vulnerability details, consult IBM’s “Security Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server” bulletin: http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21883573 [E1.S4]

The affected PureApplication System versions listed are V2.1, V2.0, and V1.1; the WebSphere Application Server bundle is included in the Web Application Pattern. [E1.S5] [E1.S6]

For PureApplication System V2.0, upgrade to V2.0.0.1 Interim Fix 5. For V1.1 and earlier, contact IBM customer support for upgrade options. [E1.S10] [E1.S11]

### techqa_DEV_Q199#row-0007

Question: How do I resolve a WSVR0605W hung thread issue in the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter? The following WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter hung thread can prevent an application server from starting...

WSVR0605W: Thread "WMQJCAResourceAdapter : 6" (0000001b) has been active for 698530 milliseconds and may be hung. There is 1 thread(s) in total in the server that may be hung. at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method) at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:167) at com.ibm.ejs.container.MessageEndpointFactoryImpl.createEndpoint(MessageEndpointFactoryImpl.java:498) at com.ibm.mq.connector.inbound.WorkImpl.run(WorkImpl.java:149)

Reference / gold answer:
To resolve a WSVR0605W hung thread issue in the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter, you need to tune the thread pool size for the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter. By default, the WebSphere MQ Resource Adapter thread pool is created with a minimum of 2 threads and a maximum of 20 threads. The Growable option is set to true, allowing the number of threads to go beyond the maximum if needed. To prevent blocked threads, you may need to limit and tune the maximum thread pool size. Individual performance tuning in a pre-production test environment is recommended to avoid performance problems on a production server.

You can access the configuration for work managers in the administrative console under Resources > Asynchronous beans > Work managers > WMQJCAResourceAdapter. It is important to configure work managers according to your specific requirements and workload to prevent hung thread issues.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `3q`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `3r`: To resolve the problem, you must tune the thread pool size for the es-workmanager thread pool.
- `3s`: By default, the es-workmanager thread pool is created with a minimum of 2 threads and a maximum of 20 threads.
- `3t`: Also, the Growable option is set to true, which means that the number of threads can go beyond the maximum, if needed.
- `3u`: When the defaults are used, this issue should not happen because the thread pool can grow, if necessary.
- `3v`: However, in certain situations, it might be necessary to limit and tune the maximum thread pool size.
- `3w`: In these situations, individual performance tuning is necessary to prevent blocked threads.
- `3x`: You can tune es-workmanager thread-pool properties in a pre-production test environment to avoid performance problems on a production server.
- `3y`: You can access the configuration for work managers in the administrative console under Resources > Asynchronous beans > Work managers > es-workmanager.

Support units:
- `E1.S1`: WSVR0605W; WorkManager; es-workmanager; hanging threads; thread pool; v61rnotes; v612rnotes; v62rnotes; v70rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 WebSphere Process Server (WPS) is unable to process event-sequenced messages due to es-workmanager hung threads. WSVR0605W warnings are thrown in the log files and traces.
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
Message processing, that is related to event-sequenced operations, stops. After handling several messages, further messages wait in the Service Component Architecture (SCA) bus queues and event-sequenced es-workmanager hung-thread WSVR0605W warnings are seen in the log files and traces. The entire process of event-sequenced messages in the system is effectively blocked.
- `E1.S4`: The following code is an example of an es-workmanager hung-thread warning:
- `E1.S5`: [01/01/11 12:00:37:844 CEST] 0000000d ThreadMonitor W WSVR0605W: Thread "WorkManager.es-workmanager : 9" (0000012e) has been active for 602495 milliseconds and may be hung. There is/are 5 thread(s) in total in the server that may be hung.
at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method)
at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:231)
at com.ibm.ws.util.BoundedBuffer.waitPut_(BoundedBuffer.java:229)
at com.ibm.ws.util.BoundedBuffer.put(BoundedBuffer.java:339)
at com.ibm.ws.util.ThreadPool.execute(ThreadPool.java:1189)
at com.ibm.ws.util.ThreadPool.execute(ThreadPool.java:1040)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkItemImpl$PoolExecuteProxy.run(WorkItemImpl.java:197)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkItemImpl.executeOnPool(WorkItemImpl.java:211)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.queueWorkItemForDispatch(WorkManagerImpl.java:425)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.startWork(WorkManagerImpl.java:381)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.startWork(WorkManagerImpl.java:510)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.startWork(WorkManagerImpl.java:525)
at com.ibm.wbiserver.sequencing.service.BaseEsService.submitWork(BaseEsService.java:417)
...
- `E1.S6`: CAUSE
Event sequencing uses a WebSphere Application Server (WAS) thread pool. This event-sequencing thread pool is named "es-workmanager," by default, and it is configured during the profile creation process. The startWork method behavior is that the method is blocked until the work is placed in the thread pool and then returned. The work is later run asynchronously. If there are not enough threads available in the es-workmanager thread pool, the startWork call to the work manager is blocked indefinitely and the WSVR0605W es-workmanager hung-thread warnings are thrown. With each warning, the number of blocked threads increases.
- `E1.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To resolve the problem, you must tune the thread pool size for the es-workmanager thread pool. By default, the es-workmanager thread pool is created with a minimum of 2 threads and a maximum of 20 threads. Also, the Growable option is set to true, which means that the number of threads can go beyond the maximum, if needed. When the defaults are used, this issue should not happen because the thread pool can grow, if necessary. However, in certain situations, it might be necessary to limit and tune the maximum thread pool size. In these situations, individual performance tuning is necessary to prevent blocked threads. You can tune es-workmanager thread-pool properties in a pre-production test environment to avoid performance problems on a production server.
- `E1.S8`: You can access the configuration for work managers in the administrative console under Resources > Asynchronous beans > Work managers > es-workmanager. The task of configuring work managers is also described in the Configuring work managers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/v7r0/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.nd.doc/info/ae/asyncbns/tasks/tasb_workmanager.html] topic within the information center:

- `E3.S1`: CLOSE_WAIT; CORBA.NO_RESPONSE; iiop connection refused; ce client connection failed TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Attempts to connect to a P8 Content Engine from any CE client (e.g. ICN, ICM, Workplace, WorkplaceXT) or custom client application, result in connection failures.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
There may be a number of different errors depending on the client application. For example:
- `E3.S4`: The Repository is not available.
- `E3.S5`: failed to establish connection using iiop://<server>:port/FileNet/Engine
- `E3.S6`: CORBA.NO_RESPONSE
- `E3.S7`: WebSphere may report ORB thread starvation or multiple ORB hung threads, for example:-
- `E3.S8`: WSVR0606W: Thread "ORB.thread.pool : 90" (000000e0) was previously reported to be hung but has completed. It was active for approximately 1626228 milliseconds. There is/are 4 thread(s) in total in the server that still may be hung.
- `E3.S9`: CAUSE
Excessive load balancer health monitor calls against the default WebSphere EJB port may use all available ORB threads and may leave TCP connections in the CLOSE_WAIT state, resulting in connection failures from other clients.
- `E3.S10`: ENVIRONMENT
High availability IBM FileNet P8 Content Engine load balanced farm.
- `E3.S11`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Check the WebSphere systemout.log for messages relating to hung threads or thread starvation.
Use netstat to collect information about port usage and remote connections.
Collect the load balancer health monitor configurations for all target P8 CE ports.
- `E3.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Review the following points in order to prevent this problem from occurring:
- `E3.S13`: * Avoid using a health monitor against the EJB/bootstrap port. 
 * The preferred load balancer health monitor for P8 Content Engine is to use the CE start-up context page, also known as the CE ping page. This should be configured against the HTTP port: 
   http://<<server>>:<<port>>/FileNet/Engine 
 * A typical load balancer HTTP health monitor configuration will only require the context path string:
   /FileNet/Engine 
 * The monitor interval should be set to the largest practical time interval, typically greater than 5 seconds. and a time-out value of not less than 15 seconds. 
 * The Content Engine application server instance will need to be re-started to close the accumulated open connections.
- `E3.S14`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Application Servers WebSphere Application Server

- `E5.S18`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  FFDC has been modified to ensure that incidents can continue
   to be logged from other components when a given component's
   incident-handling hangs a thread.  The impact to this is that
   the FFDC summary log may indicate that the incident file of a
   bad thread was created, while the thread may not have returned
   so the incident file will not exist.  Therefore, a missing
   incident entry that might have appeared in a summary file is
   an indication that the component logging to FFDC did not
   return control.

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
The documented resolution for this type of hung-thread condition is to tune the `es-workmanager` thread-pool size. Its defaults are a minimum of 2 threads, a maximum of 20, and Growable set to true; if the maximum has been limited, performance tuning may be needed to prevent blocked threads. Test the tuning in a pre-production environment first. [E1.S7]

Configure the work manager in the administrative console at Resources > Asynchronous beans > Work managers > es-workmanager. [E1.S8]

If the hang occurs while stopping an application containing a resource adapter, a separate WebSphere Application Server deadlock defect may be involved; the J2C synchronization fix was targeted for fix packs 7.0.0.35, 8.0.0.10, and 8.5.5.3. [E2.S3] [E2.S4]

- `E2.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  This APAR contains a fix to optimize how the workload
   management (WLM) component will compress and decompress data
   being sent betweenprocesses. This is designed to reduce
   compression overhead in large WebSphere Process Server or
   service integration bus (SIBus) topologies, specifically with
   a large number of destinations (more effective at 2,000 or more
   destinations). It addresses scenarios in which many clusters
   have been defined and one or more non-messaging engine (ME)
   clusters are restarted while the messaging engine cluster is
   running. A customer experiencing this may see the following:

   at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:199)
   at

- `E2.S6`: In addition this fixes a rare condition which could result in
   compressed data being lost.  This would only occur if a series
   of bytes to be compressed could not actually be compressed
   (every byte was unique). This would then cause a potential loss
   of data due to how WLM handled the uncompressed bytes.
- `E2.S7`: LOCAL FIX
- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY

 *  This APAR contains a fix to optimize how the WLM component
   will compress and decompress data being sent between
   processes. This is designed to reduce compression overhead in
   large WPS/SIB topologies, specifically with a large number of

- `E3.S1`: WSVR0605W; WorkManager; es-workmanager; hanging threads; thread pool; v61rnotes; v612rnotes; v62rnotes; v70rnotes TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 WebSphere Process Server (WPS) is unable to process event-sequenced messages due to es-workmanager hung threads. WSVR0605W warnings are thrown in the log files and traces.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
Message processing, that is related to event-sequenced operations, stops. After handling several messages, further messages wait in the Service Component Architecture (SCA) bus queues and event-sequenced es-workmanager hung-thread WSVR0605W warnings are seen in the log files and traces. The entire process of event-sequenced messages in the system is effectively blocked.
- `E3.S4`: The following code is an example of an es-workmanager hung-thread warning:
- `E3.S5`: [01/01/11 12:00:37:844 CEST] 0000000d ThreadMonitor W WSVR0605W: Thread "WorkManager.es-workmanager : 9" (0000012e) has been active for 602495 milliseconds and may be hung. There is/are 5 thread(s) in total in the server that may be hung.
at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method)
at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:231)
at com.ibm.ws.util.BoundedBuffer.waitPut_(BoundedBuffer.java:229)
at com.ibm.ws.util.BoundedBuffer.put(BoundedBuffer.java:339)
at com.ibm.ws.util.ThreadPool.execute(ThreadPool.java:1189)
at com.ibm.ws.util.ThreadPool.execute(ThreadPool.java:1040)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkItemImpl$PoolExecuteProxy.run(WorkItemImpl.java:197)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkItemImpl.executeOnPool(WorkItemImpl.java:211)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.queueWorkItemForDispatch(WorkManagerImpl.java:425)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.startWork(WorkManagerImpl.java:381)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.startWork(WorkManagerImpl.java:510)
at com.ibm.ws.asynchbeans.WorkManagerImpl.startWork(WorkManagerImpl.java:525)
at com.ibm.wbiserver.sequencing.service.BaseEsService.submitWork(BaseEsService.java:417)
...
- `E3.S6`: CAUSE
Event sequencing uses a WebSphere Application Server (WAS) thread pool. This event-sequencing thread pool is named "es-workmanager," by default, and it is configured during the profile creation process. The startWork method behavior is that the method is blocked until the work is placed in the thread pool and then returned. The work is later run asynchronously. If there are not enough threads available in the es-workmanager thread pool, the startWork call to the work manager is blocked indefinitely and the WSVR0605W es-workmanager hung-thread warnings are thrown. With each warning, the number of blocked threads increases.
- `E3.S7`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To resolve the problem, you must tune the thread pool size for the es-workmanager thread pool. By default, the es-workmanager thread pool is created with a minimum of 2 threads and a maximum of 20 threads. Also, the Growable option is set to true, which means that the number of threads can go beyond the maximum, if needed. When the defaults are used, this issue should not happen because the thread pool can grow, if necessary. However, in certain situations, it might be necessary to limit and tune the maximum thread pool size. In these situations, individual performance tuning is necessary to prevent blocked threads. You can tune es-workmanager thread-pool properties in a pre-production test environment to avoid performance problems on a production server.
- `E3.S8`: You can access the configuration for work managers in the administrative console under Resources > Asynchronous beans > Work managers > es-workmanager. The task of configuring work managers is also described in the Configuring work managers [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/wasinfo/v7r0/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.nd.doc/info/ae/asyncbns/tasks/tasb_workmanager.html] topic within the information center:
- `E3.S9`: RELATED INFORMATION
#WebSphere Process Server V7.0 Information Center [http://publib.boulder.ibm.com/infocenter/dmndhelp/v7r0mx/index.jsp?topic=/com.ibm.websphere.wps.doc/welcome_wps.html]
- `E3.S10`: PRODUCT ALIAS/SYNONYM
 WPS

Visible answer:
The documented cause is a deadlock between the application-stop thread and the J2C resource-adapter work thread performing a lookup; synchronization issues can prevent the application from stopping. [E1.S14]

This issue is associated with WebSphere Application Server fix pack levels that include APAR PM93319. [E1.S9]

Resolve it by applying a WebSphere Application Server fix pack containing the correction. The fix was targeted for WebSphere Application Server 7.0.0.35, 8.0.0.10, and 8.5.5.3; later listed fix packs are also available, including 7.0.0.45, 8.0.0.15, and 8.5.5.13. [E1.S15] [E1.S1]

The correction updates WebSphere Application Server J2C code to properly synchronize the locking objects. [E1.S15]

### techqa_DEV_Q209#row-0107

Question: How to change the maximum string length for properties in FileNet Administration Console for Content Engine (ACCE) I am trying to change the maximum string length in ACCE like we do in FileNet Enterprise Manager, but in the more Tab, I am not seeing the option. In this case, how can I change it? 

Reference / gold answer:
To change the maximum string length for properties in FileNet Administration Console for Content Engine (ACCE), you will need to follow these steps:

1. Launch ACCE.
2. Navigate to the object stores folder and click on the object store you want to work with to open the Object store tab.
3. Expand the Data Design folder and then the Classes folder. Click on the document class you are interested in to open the Document Class tab.
4. From the Properties tab, open the Property Definitions drop down and select the property definition you want to modify.
5. ACCE will open that property definition in a new Properties tab.
6. Look for the option to change the maximum string length for the property in this new Properties tab.
7. Make the necessary modifications to change the maximum string length as required.
8. Once done, go back to the Class Definition tab and click Save to save the changes.

By following these steps in ACCE, you can change the maximum string length for properties in the FileNet Administration Console for Content Engine.

- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 Administration Console for Content Platform Engine (ACCE) is the new standard interface for managing Content Engine (CE) server; however, FileNet Enterprise Manager (FEM) has been used in CE 3.5.x, 4.x, 5.0, and 5.1. The ACCE interface arranges objects differently than FEM, and users may have trouble finding some objects/directories in ACCE.
- `E3.S3`: ANSWER
Here is a table of common directories and objects within FEM, and it's new locations in ACCE.
- `E3.S4`: === Domain Level ===
- `E3.S5`: FEM ACCE AddOns Global Configuration -> Data Design -> Add-ons Database Connections Global Configuration -> Administration -> Database Connections External Repositories Global Configuration -> Administration -> External Repositories Fixed Content Devices Global Configuration -> Administration -> Fixed Content Devices Marking Sets Global Configuration -> Data Design -> Marking Sets Object Stores Global Configuration -> Object Stores PE Connection Points Global Configuration -> Object Stores-> <OS> -> Administration -> Workflow System -> Connection Points PE Region Ids Global Configuration -> Object Stores-> <OS> -> Administration -> Workflow System -> Connection Points Replication Groups Global Configuration -> Administration -> Replication Groups Sites Global Configuration -> Administration -> Sites <Domain> -> Properties -> IBM Search Server Global Configuration -> Administration -> Text Search Servers <Domain> -> Properties -> Content Cache Global Configuration -> Administration -> Content Cache Areas === Object Stores Level ===
- `E3.S6`: FEM ACCE Change Preprocessor Actions Events, Actions, Processes -> Change Preprocessor Actions Choice Lists Data Design -> Choice Lists Document Class Data Design -> Classes Document Classification Action Events, Actions, Processes -> Document Classification Action Document Lifecycles -> Document Lifecycle Action Events, Actions, Processes -> Document Lifecycle Action Document Lifecycles -> Document Lifecycle Policies Events, Actions, Processes -> Document Lifecycle Policies Events -> Event Action Events, Actions, Processes -> Event Action Events -> Subscriptions Events, Actions, Processes -> Subscriptions Export Manifest N/A Index Areas Administrative -> Index Areas Other Classes Data Design -> Classes -> Other Classes Property Templates Data Design -> Property Templates Publishing Queue Administrative -> Publishing Queue Replication Queue Administrative -> Replication Queue Root Folder Browse -> Root Folder Saved Searches Search Search Results Search Security Policies Administrative -> Security Policies Storage Areas Administrative -> Storage Areas Storage Policies Administrative -> Storage Policies Unfiled Documents Browse -> Unfiled Documents Workflow Definitions Events, Actions, Processes -> Workflow Definitions Index Job Management (Right-click ObjectStore -> All Tasks -> Index Job Management) Administrative -> Index Job Manager
- `E4.S1`: CSS index area FNRCE0010E E_BAD_VALUE: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Attempts to create an index area using Administration Console Content Engine (ACCE) fails with error The 'index_area_name' object was not created.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
The P8 server logs will show the following message:
- `E4.S4`: CBR FNRCE0010E - ERROR CSEDispatcherForSPI:Master serial=91 running with error , with message The value given for a property or list element lies outside the permitted range or value set, or exceeds the maximum length allowed. Failed to decode the password property value, most likely because the property value was not UTF-8 encoded, then encrypted.\ncom.filenet.api.exception.EngineRuntimeException: FNRCE0010E: E_BAD_VALUE: The value given for a property or list element lies outside the permitted range or value set, or exceeds the maximum length allowed. Failed to decode the password property value, most likely because the property value was not UTF-8 encoded, then encrypted.\n at com.filenet.engine.util.Encryption.masterDecryptDecode(Encryption.java:151)\n at com.filenet.engine.util.Encryption.masterDecryptDecodeString(Encryption.java:170)\n at 
,,,,\nCaused by: com.filenet.api.exception.EngineRuntimeException: FNRCE0066E: E_UNEXPECTED_EXCEPTION: An unexpected exception occurred. The unexpected exception is chained to this exception. Message was: General exception while encrypting or decrypting data\n
- `E4.S5`: CAUSE
The FileNet Content Engine Content Search Services authentication token in ACCE does not match the token configured for the IBM Content Search Services server.
- `E4.S6`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E4.S7`: 1. To find the authentication token configTool printToken –configPath path
- `E4.S8`: For example:
C:\Program Files\IBM\Content Search Services\CSS Server\bin>configTool printToken -configPath "C:\ProgramFiles\IBM\Content Search Services\CSS Server\config"
- `E4.S9`: 2. Access the properties for the server in the ACCE:
- `E4.S10`: i In the domain navigation pane, click the Text Search Servers folder.
ii In the details pane, click the name of the IBM® Content Search Services server. 
iii Click the General tab and in the Authentication token field, enter the correct token value.

- `E5.S5`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Administration Console for Content Platform Engine (ACCE) does
   not handle replication mapping of the same CE class to multiple
   Image Service (IS) external repositories correctly.
- `E5.S6`: Configuration steps:
   -Create same IS class and properties name on the 2 IS servers
   (ISClass1, ISProp1, ISProp2, etc).
   -On CE side via FileNet Enterprise Manager (FEM) or ACCE, add 2
   Fix Content Devices (FCD) to connect to the 2 Image Services
   (IS) servers
   -Add the 2 External repositories to connect to each of the FCD
   above (IS_REP1, IS_REP2)
   -Add a CE class (CEClass1) to map to both of the above 2
   external repositories
- `E5.S7`: Steps to Reproduce:
- `E5.S8`: Issue 1: Class mappings with same CE class show the same
   External name in ACCE- OS - Replication Mapping tab.
- `E5.S9`: For class mappings added via FEM with same CE class added
   previously, if you view it via ACCE- OS - Replication Mapping
   tab, it shows both with CE class mapping property with the same
   External name.
   FEM reflects the correct External Repository name when you go
   into the configuration of each class mapping 2 class mappings to
   same CE class with different external respository which were
   added via FEM.
   Click on each of the Class mapping each class and BOTH show the
   same External Repository.
   It does not show one for each of the repository.
- `E5.S10`: Issue 2: Duplicate property names appear in the CE mapping
   class.
- `E5.S11`: If you click on ACCE - OS - Replication mapping tab - select a
   CE class mapping -Replication Property Mapping tab - you will
   see all the property names are duplicated. It displays the
   property mapping for both class mappings for same CE class when
   it should only display the property mapping for the class
   mapping selected. Removing the mapping can remove the wrong
   property mapping for the other class mapping.
   FEM does not show duplicate properties.
- `E5.S12`: LOCAL FIX
 *  Use FileNet Enterprise Manager.
- `E5.S13`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:                                              *
   * Customers using 5.2.0.3-P8CPE-IF006 or 5.2.1.0-P8CPE and     *
   * prior ACCE to manage replication mappings with multiple      *
   * Image Services.                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION:                                         *
   * Administration Console for Content Platform Engine (ACCE)    *
   * does not handle replication mapping of the same CE class to  *
   * multiple Image Service (IS) external repositories correctly. *
   * The class mapping to the second IS repository may not be     *
   * created.  The property mappings associated with a class      *
   * mapping might be listed under the wrong class mapping.       *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * Upgrade to 5.2.0.4-P8CPE-FP004 or 5.2.1.2-P8CPE-FP002 or     *
   * later.                                                       *
   ****************************************************************
- `E5.S14`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Fixed in 5.2.0.4-P8CPE-FP004 and 5.2.1.2-P8CPE-FP002 and higher.
- `E5.S15`: IS repository may not be     *
   * created.  The property mappings associated with a class      *
   * mapping might be listed under the wrong class mapping.       *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   * Upgrade to 5.2.0.4-P8CPE-FP004 or 5.2.1.2-P8CPE-FP002 or     *
   * later.                                                       *
   ****************************************************************
- `E5.S16`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  Fixed in 5.2.0.4-P8CPE-FP004 and 5.2.1.2-P8CPE-FP002 and higher.
   When there are multiple IS external repositories with same set
   of external classes, ACCE should allow multiple class mappings
   between the same CPE class and the same IS class in different IS
   repository.  The associated property mappings should be listed
   correctly.

- `E1.S1`: ACCE; CE; Property; FEM TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 With IBM FileNet Enterprise Manager (FEM), we can follow the steps below to overwrite the property definition in a document class
- `E1.S3`: 1. Launch FEM
2. Expand the object store and document class tree. Right click on the document class and select "Properties"
3. Go to "Properties Definitions" tab, highlight the property definition and click "Edit"
4. Make the modification and click OK
5. Click OK again to save the change
- `E1.S4`: How to perform the same operation with FileNet Content Engine - ACCE?
- `E1.S5`: ANSWER
Follow the below steps to update the property definition properties on ACCE:
- `E1.S6`: 1. Launch ACCE 
 2. Expand the object stores folder and click the object store to open the Object store tab 
 3. Expand the Data Design folder and Classes folder. Click the document class to open Document Class tab 
 4. From Properties tab, open Property Definitions drop down and select the property definition you want to modify 
 5. ACCE will open that property definition in a new Properties tab 
 6. Modify the property definition as required 
 7. Go back to the Class Definition tab and click Save

### techqa_DEV_Q210#row-0151

Question: startNode failed with ADML3000E after a deployment failure Client had a deployment failure due to "Too many open files" error.

Afterwards, the startNode failed with ADML3000E:

What could cause the "Too many open files error?

Reference / gold answer:
The "Too many open files" error could be caused by a system configuration limitation where all available file handles for the process have been used up. This may be the result of file handles being leaked by some part of the application. Additionally, the ulimit for the number of file handles may be set too low by default. To resolve this issue, the ulimit should be increased to allow for more open files.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `1p`: Message: APT_CombinedOperatorController(0),0: Fatal Error: Unexpected error in APT_TSort_ScratchFile::nextInputDescriptor: could not open file: E:\Data\DS_TEST\Scratchspace/tsort4qb08d3n; error: No such file or directory CAUSE
- `1q`: MKS Toolkit does not have sufficient free File Locks available for the number of DataStage jobs running on the Windows Server.
- `1r`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
- `1s`: On the Windows Server, go to Start - Control Panel - Configure MKS Toolkit.
- `1t`: Go to the Runtime Tab and select Category = Miscellaneous Setting.
- `1u`: Under File Lock, check what has been set for "Max number of active file locks"
- `1v`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `1w`: By default "Max number of active file locks" is set to 255.
- `1x`: Increase this number to 300.
- `1y`: Then click on the "OK" button.
- `1z`: You will need to restart the Windows server for this change to take effect.
- `3b`:  This technote explains how to debug the "Too many open files" error message on Microsoft Windows, AIX, Linux and Solaris operating systems. SYMPTOM
- `3c`: The following messages could be displayed when the process has exhausted the file handle limit:
- `3g`: New sockets/file descriptors can not be opened after the limit has been reached. CAUSE
- `3h`: System configuration limitation.
- `3i`: When the "Too Many Open Files" error message is written to the logs, it indicates that all available file handles for the process have been used (this includes sockets as well).
- `3j`: In a majority of cases, this is the result of file handles being leaked by some part of the application.
- `3m`: On UNIX and Linux operating systems, the ulimit for the number of file handles can be configured, and it is usually set too low by default.
- `3n`: Increasing this ulimit to 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime, but this depends on your applications and your file/socket usage.
- `3o`: Additionally, file descriptor leaks can still occur even with a high value.
- `3p`: Display the current soft limit: ulimit -Sn
- `3q`: Display the current hard limit: ulimit -Hn

Guidelines for setting ulimits (WebSphere Application Server)
http://www.IBM.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21469413 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21469413]
- `E2.S16`: Operating Systems
- `E2.S17`: Windows By default, Windows does not ship with a tool to debug this type of problem. Instead Microsoft provides a tool that you can download called Process Explorer [http://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896653]. This tool identifies the open handles/files associated with the Java™ process (but usually not sockets opened by the Winsock component) and determines which handles are still opened. These handles result in the "Too many open files" error message.
- `E2.S18`: To display the handles, click on the Gear Icon [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&amp;aid=1] in the toolbar (or press CTRL+ H to toggle the handles view). The icon will change to the icon for DLL files (so you can toggle it back to the DLL view).
- `E2.S19`: It is important that you change the Refresh Rate. Select View > Update Speed, and change it to 5 seconds.
- `E2.S20`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&aid=2]
- `E2.S21`: There is also another Microsoft utility called Handle that you can download from the following URL: 
https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896655.aspx [https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896655.aspx]
- `E2.S22`: This tool is a command line version of Process Explorer. The URL above contains the usage instructions.
- `E2.S23`: AIX 
The commands lsof and procfiles are usually the best commands to determine what files and sockets are opened..
- `E2.S24`: lsof 
To determine if the number of open files is growing over a period of time, issue lsof to report the open files against a PID on a periodic basis.
- `E2.S25`: the usage instructions.
- `E2.S26`: AIX 
The commands lsof and procfiles are usually the best commands to determine what files and sockets are opened..
- `E2.S27`: lsof 
To determine if the number of open files is growing over a period of time, issue lsof to report the open files against a PID on a periodic basis. For example:
- `E2.S28`: lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E2.S29`: This output does not give the actual file names to which the handles are open. It provides only the name of the file system (directory) in which they are contained. The lsof command indicates if the open file is associated with an open socket or a file. When it references a file, it identifies the file system and the inode, not the file name.
- `E2.S30`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.
- `E2.S31`: procfiles 
The procfiles command does provide similar information, and also displays the full filenames loaded. It may not show sockets in use.
- `E2.S32`: procfiles -n [PID] > procfiles.out
- `E2.S33`: Other commands (to display filenames that are opened)
- `E2.S34`: INODES and DF 
df -kP filesystem_from_lsof | awk '{print $6}' | tail -1 
>> Note the filesystem name 
find filesystem_name -inum inode_from_lsof -print > filelist.out 
>> Shows the actual file name
- `E2.S35`: svmon 
svmon -P PID -m | grep pers (for JFS) 
svmon -P PID -m | grep clnt (for JFS2, NFS) 
(this opens files in the format: filesystem_device:inode)
- `E2.S36`: Use the same procedure as above for finding the actual file name.
- `E2.S37`: Linux To determine if the number of open files is growing over a period of time, issue lsof to report the open files against a PID on a periodic basis. For example:
- `E2.S38`: lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E2.S39`: The output will provide you with all of the open files for the specified PID. You will be able to determine which files are opened and which files are growing over time.
- `E2.S40`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.
- `E2.S41`: Alternately you can list the contents of the file descriptors as a list of symbolic links in the following directory, where you replace PID with the process ID. This is especially useful if you don't have access to the lsof command:
- `E2.S42`: ls -al /proc/PID/fd
- `E2.S43`: Solaris Run the following commands to monitor open file (socket) descriptors on Solaris:
- `E2.S44`: pfiles 
/usr/proc/bin/pfiles [ PID ] > pfiles.out
- `E2.S45`: lsof 
lsof -p [ PID ] > lsof.ou t
- `E2.S46`: This will get one round of lsof output. If you want to determine if the number of open files is growing over time, you can issue the command with the -r option to capture multiple intervals: 
lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E2.S47`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.
- `E2.S48`: HP-UX 
lsof 
lsof -p [ PID ] > lsof.out
- `E2.S49`: This will get one round of lsof output.

- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 DataStage Parallel job fails with error message "too many open files" when running on Windows platform
- `E1.S3`: SYMPTOM
In the DataStage job log, error messages seen are:
- `E1.S4`: Item #: 867
Event ID: 2172
Timestamp: 2011-11-15 10:09:47
Type: Fatal
User Name: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Message Id: IIS-DSEE-TOSO-00048
Message: APT_CombinedOperatorController(0),1: Fatal Error: Unexpected error in APT_TSort_ScratchFile::nextInputDescriptor: could not open file: E:\Data\DS_TEST\Scratchspace/tsortOggtbvxt; error: Too many open files
- `E1.S5`: Followed by the following error message a few entries later:
Item #: 873
Event ID: 2178
Timestamp: 2011-11-15 10:09:50
Type: Fatal
User Name: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
Message Id: IIS-DSEE-TOSO-00048
Message: APT_CombinedOperatorController(0),0: Fatal Error: Unexpected error in APT_TSort_ScratchFile::nextInputDescriptor: could not open file: E:\Data\DS_TEST\Scratchspace/tsort4qb08d3n; error: No such file or directory
- `E1.S6`: CAUSE
MKS Toolkit does not have sufficient free File Locks available for the number of DataStage jobs running on the Windows Server.
- `E1.S7`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
On the Windows Server, go to Start - Control Panel - Configure MKS Toolkit.
- `E1.S8`: Go to the Runtime Tab and select Category = Miscellaneous Setting.
- `E1.S9`: Under File Lock, check what has been set for "Max number of active file locks"
- `E1.S10`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
By default "Max number of active file locks" is set to 255. Increase this number to 300.
- `E1.S11`: Then click on the "OK" button. You will need to restart the Windows server for this change to take effect.

- `E3.S1`: wasrun; wasjdk; open; files; too; ProblemDeterminationDocument; JCC was appserver app server TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 This technote explains how to debug the "Too many open files" error message on Microsoft Windows, AIX, Linux and Solaris operating systems.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
The following messages could be displayed when the process has exhausted the file handle limit:
- `E3.S4`: java.io.IOException: Too many open files
- `E3.S5`: [3/14/15 9:26:53:589 EDT] 14142136 prefs W Could not lock User prefs. Unix error code 24.
- `E3.S6`: New sockets/file descriptors can not be opened after the limit has been reached.
- `E3.S7`: CAUSE
System configuration limitation.
- `E3.S8`: When the "Too Many Open Files" error message is written to the logs, it indicates that all available file handles for the process have been used (this includes sockets as well). In a majority of cases, this is the result of file handles being leaked by some part of the application. This technote explains how to collect output that identifies what file handles are in use at the time of the error condition.
- `E3.S9`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
- `E3.S10`: Determine Ulimits
- `E3.S11`: On UNIX and Linux operating systems, the ulimit for the number of file handles can be configured, and it is usually set too low by default. Increasing this ulimit to 8000 is usually sufficient for normal runtime, but this depends on your applications and your file/socket usage. Additionally, file descriptor leaks can still occur even with a high value.
- `E3.S12`: Display the current soft limit:
ulimit -Sn
- `E3.S13`: Display the current hard limit:
ulimit -Hn
- `E3.S14`: Or capture a Javacore, the limit will be listed in that file under the name NOFILE:
kill -3 PID
- `E3.S15`: Please see the following document if you would like more information on where you can edit ulimits:
Guidelines for setting ulimits (WebSphere Application Server)
http://www.IBM.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21469413 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg21469413]
- `E3.S16`: Operating Systems
- `E3.S17`: Windows By default, Windows does not ship with a tool to debug this type of problem. Instead Microsoft provides a tool that you can download called Process Explorer [http://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896653]. This tool identifies the open handles/files associated with the Java™ process (but usually not sockets opened by the Winsock component) and determines which handles are still opened. These handles result in the "Too many open files" error message.
- `E3.S18`: To display the handles, click on the Gear Icon [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&amp;aid=1] in the toolbar (or press CTRL+ H to toggle the handles view). The icon will change to the icon for DLL files (so you can toggle it back to the DLL view).
- `E3.S19`: It is important that you change the Refresh Rate. Select View > Update Speed, and change it to 5 seconds.
- `E3.S20`: [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&aid=2] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21067352&aid=2]
- `E3.S21`: There is also another Microsoft utility called Handle that you can download from the following URL: 
https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896655.aspx [https://technet.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/bb896655.aspx]
- `E3.S22`: This tool is a command line version of Process Explorer. The URL above contains the usage instructions.
- `E3.S23`: AIX 
The commands lsof and procfiles are usually the best commands to determine what files and sockets are opened..
- `E3.S24`: lsof 
To determine if the number of open files is growing over a period of time, issue lsof to report the open files against a PID on a periodic basis.
- `E3.S25`: with the -r option to capture multiple intervals: 
lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E3.S26`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.
- `E3.S27`: HP-UX 
lsof 
lsof -p [ PID ] > lsof.out
- `E3.S28`: This will get one round of lsof output. If you want to determine if the number of open files is growing over time, you can issue the command with the -r option to capture multiple intervals: 
lsof -p [PID] -r [interval in seconds, 1800 for 30 minutes] > lsof.out
- `E3.S29`: It is best to capture lsof several times to see the rate of growth in the file descriptors.
- `E3.S30`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Application Servers Runtimes for Java Technology Java SDK
