- `E5.S1`: CLOSE_WAIT; CORBA.NO_RESPONSE; iiop connection refused; ce client connection failed TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E5.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Attempts to connect to a P8 Content Engine from any CE client (e.g. ICN, ICM, Workplace, WorkplaceXT) or custom client application, result in connection failures.
- `E5.S3`: SYMPTOM
There may be a number of different errors depending on the client application. For example:
- `E5.S4`: The Repository is not available.
- `E5.S5`: failed to establish connection using iiop://<server>:port/FileNet/Engine
- `E5.S6`: CORBA.NO_RESPONSE
- `E5.S7`: WebSphere may report ORB thread starvation or multiple ORB hung threads, for example:-
- `E5.S8`: WSVR0606W: Thread "ORB.thread.pool : 90" (000000e0) was previously reported to be hung but has completed. It was active for approximately 1626228 milliseconds. There is/are 4 thread(s) in total in the server that still may be hung.
- `E5.S9`: CAUSE
Excessive load balancer health monitor calls against the default WebSphere EJB port may use all available ORB threads and may leave TCP connections in the CLOSE_WAIT state, resulting in connection failures from other clients.
- `E5.S10`: ENVIRONMENT
High availability IBM FileNet P8 Content Engine load balanced farm.
- `E5.S11`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Check the WebSphere systemout.log for messages relating to hung threads or thread starvation.
Use netstat to collect information about port usage and remote connections.
Collect the load balancer health monitor configurations for all target P8 CE ports.
- `E5.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Review the following points in order to prevent this problem from occurring:
- `E5.S13`: * Avoid using a health monitor against the EJB/bootstrap port. 
 * The preferred load balancer health monitor for P8 Content Engine is to use the CE start-up context page, also known as the CE ping page. This should be configured against the HTTP port: 
   http://<<server>>:<<port>>/FileNet/Engine 
 * A typical load balancer HTTP health monitor configuration will only require the context path string:
   /FileNet/Engine 
 * The monitor interval should be set to the largest practical time interval, typically greater than 5 seconds. and a time-out value of not less than 15 seconds. 
 * The Content Engine application server instance will need to be re-started to close the accumulated open connections.
- `E5.S14`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Application Servers WebSphere Application Server

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
The “Too many open files” error means the process has exhausted its available file handles, including sockets, so it cannot open new sockets or file descriptors. In most cases, this is caused by file handles being leaked by part of the application; it can also result from a system configuration limit that is set too low. [E3.S6] [E3.S7] [E3.S8]

If the deployment was running on Windows with DataStage, a specific cause is that MKS Toolkit did not have enough free file locks for the number of DataStage jobs running. Its default maximum of 255 active file locks may need to be increased, for example to 300, followed by a Windows server restart. [E1.S6] [E1.S10] [E1.S11]

### techqa_DEV_Q215#row-0010

Question: When should I use conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers? MQ version 7.0 introduced a new feature, conversation sharing. Are there any special values on DataPower when configuring conversation sharing?

Reference / gold answer:
Conversation sharing in DataPower MQ queue managers should be used when negotiating the sharing conversations value. It is beneficial to configure the Sharing Conversations attribute with a specific value based on the negotiated value with the MQ server. 

Three different use cases for configuring sharing conversations in DataPower MQ queue managers are outlined:
1. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 0, it is recommended to set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute in DataPower to disable sharing conversations.
2. If the negotiated sharing conversations value is 1, it is advised to set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute in DataPower. 
3. When the negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more, it is recommended to set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute.

It is important to configure the Sharing Conversations attribute appropriately to ensure optimal performance and avoid potential errors or instability in the MQ environment.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `1d`: IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases provide sharing conversations (SHARECNV) attribute on SVRCONN channel that specifies the maximum number of conversations that can share each TCP/IP channel instance.
- `1e`: This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel.
- `1f`: The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object.
- `1j`: However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server.
- `1l`: Case #1 : The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0 - The channel runs in a mode similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not uses features such as
- `1p`: Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower to disable sharing conversations regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `1r`: Set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower as shown in the following picture and a value of 1 on IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `1v`: Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower and on the MQ SVRCONN channel.

- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When to enable Sharing Conversations in DataPower MQ Queue Manager (mq-qm) object along with SHARECNV attribute of the MQ SVRCONN channel?
- `E1.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases provide sharing conversations (SHARECNV) attribute on SVRCONN channel that specifies the maximum number of conversations that can share each TCP/IP channel instance. This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel. 
The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object. The same default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is 
negotiated between MQ server and DataPower and the lower value takes effect. However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server.
- `E1.S4`: There are three use cases to configure Sharing Conversations in DataPower mq-qm object:
- `E1.S5`: Case #1 : The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0 - The channel runs in a mode similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not uses features such as
- `E1.S6`: · Administrator stop-quiesce
· Heartbeating 
· Read ahead 
· Client asynchronous consume
- `E1.S7`: Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower to disable sharing conversations regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E1.S8`: Case #2: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 1 - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features as outlined in case #1, but each TCP/IP channel instance has a single conversation.
- `E1.S9`: Set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower as shown in the following picture and a value of 1 on IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E1.S10`: The Share Single Conversation attribute is only visible when "Sharing Conversations" is configured with value of "1" and then <RETURN> key is entered. For values greater than 1, the "Share Single Conversation" attribute is hidden in the mq-qm object.
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1]
- `E1.S11`: Case #3: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features and each TCP/IP channel instance supports 2 or more conversations.
- `E1.S12`: Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower and on the MQ SVRCONN channel.
- `E1.S13`: On average, processing of messages from client applications is 15 percent slower when using SHARECNV(10) as compared to SHARECNV(0). Please refer to Performance Implications of Sharing [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm]
Conversations on Client-connection Channels. [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm].
- `E1.S14`: Since DataPower uses a connection pool in processing MQ messages, there are no additional benefits of using sharing conversations with the mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E1.S15`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call.
- `E1.S16`: mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E1.S17`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call. However, when mixed message sizes are processed by the same MQ Front Side Handler (FSH), it requests buffer pool based on maximum message size configured in the mq-qm object. The use of fixed buffer pool for small and large messages can deplete MQ server's allocated buffer and contribute to unexpected termination of MQ SVRCONN channel instance and may terminate the queue manager. In such a situation, using a negotiated sharing conversations value of 1 as in case #2 will benefit DataPower mq-qm object as it will use IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 Read Ahead feature and the new buffer management feature for MQGET API call. IBM WebSphere MQ V8 release provides enhanced performance for case #2, when the negotiated sharing conversations value is 1.
- `E1.S18`: For DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, one should follow case #1 and use a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0. If you configure these firmware versions with case #2 or case #3, DataPower device may reload or hang due to connection instability and generate many MQ errors with Reason Code - 2009 and 2059.
- `E1.S19`: Cases #2 and #3 can be used in firmware releases 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later. We suggest to use a value of 10 or less in Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object and verify the configuration empirically to make sure that IBM WebSphere MQ server can sustain load from DataPower with the negotiated Sharing Conversations of 10.
- `E1.S20`: Note: In order to use sharing conversations, make sure you have applied APAR IV24821 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IV24821] ("Client C application process hangs after cancelling thread") to the IBM WebSphere MQ server. IV24821 is included in IBM WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.10 and later, IBM WebSphere MQ V7.1.0.3 and later, IBM WebSphere MQ V7.5.0.1 and later, and IBM WebSphere MQ V8.

 *  WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS V7.0.1.5 (or later): Failure

- `E2.S7`: LOCAL FIX
- `E2.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   This issue affects users of the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.5 Classes
   for Java/JMS (or later) who have established a remote connection
   to a Queue Manager via a channel that has Conversation Sharing
   disabled (SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1).
- `E2.S9`: This includes users of:
- `E2.S10`: - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Classes for JMS
   - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V7.0 and V8.0 WebSphere MQ
   messaging provider.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V6.1 WebSphere MQ messaging
   provider who have configured the WebSphere variable
   MQ_INSTALL_ROOT to point to a WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 installation.
- `E2.S11`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   By default in the WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS,
   conversation
   sharing is enabled and set to 10 on the client side. The client
   only discovers that Conversation Sharing is disabled following
   negotiation with a Queue Manager on the completion of a
   connection over a Channel that has SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1.
- `E2.S12`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requests a
   remote connection to a Queue Manager the client first attempts
   to find an already established TCP/IP connection which can be
   shared. As part of this process the list of known TCP/IP
   connections are matched for their suitability, this list
   includes connections which are in the process of being
   established (MQCONN reply not received from the Queue Manager).
- `E2.S13`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requested a
   remote connection it was matched for sharing with a connection
   that was still in the process of being established. The
   WebSphere MQ Client waited for the connection to complete and
   due to a small timing window began incorrectly sharing the
   connection without confirming the connection's suitability. If
   the connection's suitability had been checked then the
   connection
   would have been marked unsuitable due to the Negotiated Channel
   specifying that Conversation Sharing was disabled (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).
   As the connection (which did not support conversation sharing)
   was now shared by two threads, packets destined for one thread
   were erroneously received by the other, this led to the client
   being in an inconsistent state and the two FDCs being generated.
- `E2.S14`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS have been modified to
   correctly restrict conversation sharing when using a connection
   that does not support conversation sharing (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).

Visible answer:
Use conversation sharing only when appropriate for your DataPower firmware and workload. DataPower uses a connection pool, so sharing conversations generally provides no additional benefit; however, with mixed message sizes, case #2 (negotiated value 1) can benefit the mq-qm object through MQ Version 7 buffer management and Read Ahead. [E1.S14] [E1.S17]

For DataPower firmware 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, use a negotiated sharing-conversations value of 0. Configuring case #2 or #3 on those releases may cause reloads or hangs due to connection instability. [E1.S18]

Cases #2 and #3 are supported for firmware 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later. IBM suggests using 10 or less in the DataPower Sharing Conversations attribute and empirically verifying that the MQ server can sustain the negotiated load. [E1.S19]

To disable sharing regardless of the SVRCONN setting, set DataPower Sharing Conversations to 0 or 1. In current DataPower firmware, a configured value of 1 is treated as 0 during negotiation. [E1.S3] [E1.S7]

For a negotiated value of 1, set DataPower Sharing Conversations to 1, select Share Single Conversation = on, and set the MQ SVRCONN value to 1. The Share Single Conversation attribute appears only when Sharing Conversations is set to 1 and Return is pressed; it is hidden for values greater than 1. [E1.S8] [E1.S9] [E1.S10]

For a negotiated value of 2 or more, set Sharing Conversations to 2 or more on both the DataPower mq-qm object and the MQ SVRCONN channel. [E1.S11] [E1.S12]

Before using sharing conversations, apply MQ APAR IV24821; it is included in MQ V7.0.1.10 and later, V7.1.0.3 and later, V7.5.0.1 and later, and MQ V8. [E1.S20]

Support units:
- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E1.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 When to enable Sharing Conversations in DataPower MQ Queue Manager (mq-qm) object along with SHARECNV attribute of the MQ SVRCONN channel?
- `E1.S3`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
IBM WebSphere MQ server version 7.0 and later releases provide sharing conversations (SHARECNV) attribute on SVRCONN channel that specifies the maximum number of conversations that can share each TCP/IP channel instance. This feature can be configured in DataPower as it uses client connection with queue manager SVRCONN channel. 
The default setting of sharing conversations (SHARECNV) value is zero in DataPower mq-qm object. The same default value for MQ SVRCONN channel is 10. The sharing conversations value is 
negotiated between MQ server and DataPower and the lower value takes effect. However, in current versions of the DataPower firmware, the sharing conversations setting of 1 is treated as 0 when negotiating with MQ server.
- `E1.S4`: There are three use cases to configure Sharing Conversations in DataPower mq-qm object:
- `E1.S5`: Case #1 : The negotiated sharing conversations value is 0 - The channel runs in a mode similar to WebSphere MQ V6 and does not uses features such as
- `E1.S6`: · Administrator stop-quiesce
· Heartbeating 
· Read ahead 
· Client asynchronous consume
- `E1.S7`: Set a value of 0 or 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower to disable sharing conversations regardless of the IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E1.S8`: Case #2: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 1 - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ V7 and later release features as outlined in case #1, but each TCP/IP channel instance has a single conversation.
- `E1.S9`: Set a value of 1 on the Sharing Conversations attribute and select "on" in Share Single Conversation attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower as shown in the following picture and a value of 1 on IBM WebSphere MQ SVRCONN setting.
- `E1.S10`: The Share Single Conversation attribute is only visible when "Sharing Conversations" is configured with value of "1" and then <RETURN> key is entered. For values greater than 1, the "Share Single Conversation" attribute is hidden in the mq-qm object.
[/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1] [/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21647231&aid=1]
- `E1.S11`: Case #3: The negotiated sharing conversations value is 2 or more - The channel supports IBM WebSphere MQ 7 and later release features and each TCP/IP channel instance supports 2 or more conversations.
- `E1.S12`: Set a value of 2 or more on the Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object in DataPower and on the MQ SVRCONN channel.
- `E1.S13`: On average, processing of messages from client applications is 15 percent slower when using SHARECNV(10) as compared to SHARECNV(0). Please refer to Performance Implications of Sharing [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm]
Conversations on Client-connection Channels. [http://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSFKSJ_7.0.1/com.ibm.mq.csqzaf.doc/mi12240_.htm].
- `E1.S14`: Since DataPower uses a connection pool in processing MQ messages, there are no additional benefits of using sharing conversations with the mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E1.S15`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call.
- `E1.S16`: mq-qm object. However, in situations when mixed message sizes are used by the same mq-qm object, using case #2 will benefit mq-qm object as it will use new buffer management feature of IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 when making MQGET API call.
- `E1.S17`: When using a negotiated shared conversations value of 0 as in case #1, mq-qm object uses maximum message size as the buffer pool for the MQGET API call. However, when mixed message sizes are processed by the same MQ Front Side Handler (FSH), it requests buffer pool based on maximum message size configured in the mq-qm object. The use of fixed buffer pool for small and large messages can deplete MQ server's allocated buffer and contribute to unexpected termination of MQ SVRCONN channel instance and may terminate the queue manager. In such a situation, using a negotiated sharing conversations value of 1 as in case #2 will benefit DataPower mq-qm object as it will use IBM WebSphere MQ Version 7 Read Ahead feature and the new buffer management feature for MQGET API call. IBM WebSphere MQ V8 release provides enhanced performance for case #2, when the negotiated sharing conversations value is 1.
- `E1.S18`: For DataPower firmware releases 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x and earlier, one should follow case #1 and use a negotiated sharing conversations value of 0. If you configure these firmware versions with case #2 or case #3, DataPower device may reload or hang due to connection instability and generate many MQ errors with Reason Code - 2009 and 2059.
- `E1.S19`: Cases #2 and #3 can be used in firmware releases 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x and later. We suggest to use a value of 10 or less in Sharing Conversations attribute of the mq-qm object and verify the configuration empirically to make sure that IBM WebSphere MQ server can sustain load from DataPower with the negotiated Sharing Conversations of 10.
- `E1.S20`: Note: In order to use sharing conversations, make sure you have applied APAR IV24821 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1IV24821] ("Client C application process hangs after cancelling thread") to the IBM WebSphere MQ server. IV24821 is included in IBM WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.10 and later, IBM WebSphere MQ V7.1.0.3 and later, IBM WebSphere MQ V7.5.0.1 and later, and IBM WebSphere MQ V8.

- `E3.S1`: retries; high CPU; MQ queue manager; Retry Interval; Retry Attempts; Long Retry Interval TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E3.S2`: QUESTION
 Why does WebSphere DataPower spike with a high CPU rate when a WebSphere MQ connection is unavailable? Is there a solution to this issue?
- `E3.S3`: CAUSE
If the value of Retry Attempts is set to 0 on the DataPower MQ Queue Manager object, this negates the benefits of the Long Retry Interval since it will not be used. DataPower will retry forever using the specified Retry Interval. The default setting of Retry Attempts as 0 and Retry Interval as 1 second is provided to preserve backward compatibility. However, these default values should be changed to take advantage of Long Retry Interval feature available in firmware.
- `E3.S4`: ANSWER
The solution to the issue of having DataPower vulnerable to the MQ Queue Manager being inaccessible is to change the Retry Attempts parameter on the Configure MQ Queue Manager window from 0 to some number. As an example, change the parameters as follows:
- `E3.S5`: *  Retry Attempts - change the default of 0 to 6 Retry Interval - change the default of 1 to 10 seconds Long Retry Interval - change the default of 1800 to 600 seconds (10 minutes)
- `E3.S6`: In the event that the Queue Manager is down or a connection is not established, the above example configuration will allow the MQ QM Object to retry 6 times with 10 second intervals. After 6 attempts, the MQ QM object will retry every 10 minutes.
- `E3.S7`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Business Integration WebSphere DataPower Integration Appliance XI50 Firmware 3.8 Business Integration WebSphere DataPower Low Latency Appliance XM70 Firmware 3.8

 *  WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS V7.0.1.5 (or later): Failure
   Data Capture (FDC) files
   with Probe
   ID JO076001 and JO205001 are generated following a remote
   connection to a Queue Manager that has conversation sharing
   disabled:
- `E4.S5`: | Probe Id     :- JO076001
   | Component    :- RemoteFAP.MQOPEN(Hconn,MQOD,int,Phobj,Pi

- `E4.S6`: | Probe Id     :- JO205001
   | Component    :- RemoteConnection.removeHconn(RemoteTls,R
   | Probe Type   :- INCORROUT
   | Comment1     :- Hconn is not associated with this connection
- `E4.S7`: LOCAL FIX
- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   This issue affects users of the WebSphere MQ V7.0.1.5 Classes
   for Java/JMS (or later) who have established a remote connection
   to a Queue Manager via a channel that has Conversation Sharing
   disabled (SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1).
- `E4.S9`: This includes users of:
- `E4.S10`: - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Classes for JMS
   - The WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 Resource Adapter.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V7.0 and V8.0 WebSphere MQ
   messaging provider.
   - The WebSphere Application Server V6.1 WebSphere MQ messaging
   provider who have configured the WebSphere variable
   MQ_INSTALL_ROOT to point to a WebSphere MQ V7.0.1 installation.
- `E4.S11`: Platforms affected:
   All Distributed (iSeries, all Unix and Windows)
   ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   By default in the WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS,
   conversation
   sharing is enabled and set to 10 on the client side. The client
   only discovers that Conversation Sharing is disabled following
   negotiation with a Queue Manager on the completion of a
   connection over a Channel that has SHARECNV=0 or SHARECNV=1.
- `E4.S12`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requests a
   remote connection to a Queue Manager the client first attempts
   to find an already established TCP/IP connection which can be
   shared. As part of this process the list of known TCP/IP
   connections are matched for their suitability, this list
   includes connections which are in the process of being
   established (MQCONN reply not received from the Queue Manager).
- `E4.S13`: When a WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS application requested a
   remote connection it was matched for sharing with a connection
   that was still in the process of being established. The
   WebSphere MQ Client waited for the connection to complete and
   due to a small timing window began incorrectly sharing the
   connection without confirming the connection's suitability. If
   the connection's suitability had been checked then the
   connection
   would have been marked unsuitable due to the Negotiated Channel
   specifying that Conversation Sharing was disabled (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).
   As the connection (which did not support conversation sharing)
   was now shared by two threads, packets destined for one thread
   were erroneously received by the other, this led to the client
   being in an inconsistent state and the two FDCs being generated.
- `E4.S14`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  The WebSphere MQ Classes for Java/JMS have been modified to
   correctly restrict conversation sharing when using a connection
   that does not support conversation sharing (SHARECNV=0 or
   SHARECNV=1).
- `E4.S15`: ---------------------------------------------------------------

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
IBM WebSphere MQ 7.0 and later support the SVRCONN channel SHARECNV attribute, which sets the maximum number of conversations sharing each TCP/IP channel instance. DataPower negotiates its configured value with the MQ server, and the lower value takes effect. [E1.S3]

For DataPower firmware 7.0.0.x, 7.1.0.x, 7.2.0.x, and earlier, use a negotiated value of 0. Configuring case 2 or case 3 on those firmware versions may cause reloads or hangs and MQ reason codes 2009 and 2059. [E1.S18]

For firmware 7.5.0.x, 7.5.1.x, and later, cases 2 and 3 can be used. The documentation suggests configuring 10 or less and empirically verifying that the MQ server can sustain the resulting load. [E1.S19]

To disable conversation sharing regardless of the SVRCONN setting, configure Sharing Conversations as 0 or 1 on the DataPower mq-qm object. DataPower treats a configured value of 1 as 0 during negotiation in current firmware versions. [E1.S3] [E1.S7]

The Share Single Conversation attribute is displayed only when Sharing Conversations is set to 1 and the Return key is entered; it is hidden for values greater than 1. [E1.S10]

Use a value of 2 or more on both the DataPower mq-qm object and the MQ SVRCONN channel when each TCP/IP channel instance should support at least two conversations. [E1.S11] [E1.S12]

Because DataPower uses a connection pool, sharing conversations generally provides no additional benefit. An exception is mixed message sizes on the same mq-qm object, where case 2 can benefit from MQ 7 buffer management and Read Ahead; case 1 uses the maximum configured message size as the MQGET buffer pool. [E1.S14] [E1.S15] [E1.S17]

### techqa_DEV_Q249#row-0011

Question: Help with Security Bulletin: IBM WebSphere MQ Administration command could cause denial of service (CVE-2016-8971) I need to understand details regarding Security Bulletin: IBM WebSphere MQ Administration command could cause denial of service (CVE-2016-8971). Where can I find this information?


Reference / gold answer:
To find the details regarding the Security Bulletin for IBM WebSphere MQ Administration command that could cause a denial of service (CVE-2016-8971), you can refer to the original document published by IBM on the IBM Security Bulletin website. The bulletin contains information about the vulnerability, its description, CVSS scores, affected products and versions, remediation/fixes, workarounds and mitigations, references, related information, change history, and disclaimer.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `2a`:  SECURITY BULLETIN SUMMARY
- `2b`:  An administration command can cause IBM MQ to access an invalid memory address, leading to a segmentation failure and causing the queue manager to become unresponsive. VULNERABILITY DETAILS
- `2c`: CVEID: CVE-2016-8971 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-8971]
- `2d`: DESCRIPTION: IBM MQ could allow an authenticated user with queue manager permissions to cause a segmentation fault.
- `2e`: This would result in the machine needing to be rebooted to resume normal operations.
- `2f`: CVSS Base Score: 5.3
- `2g`: CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/118862 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/118862] for the current score
- `2h`: CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined

- `E1.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E1.S2`: SUMMARY
 OpenSSLの脆弱性はOpenSSL Projectによって2015年3月19日に開示されました。 OpenSSLは、IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security for the IBM iプラットフォーム、 IBM WebSphere MQ HP-NSSとIBM WebSphere MQ Paho MQTT クライアントで使用されます。
IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security for the IBM i とIBM WebSphere MQ HP-NSS クライアントは、該当のCVEに対処しました。
- `E1.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
脆弱性の詳細：
- `E1.S4`: CVEID: CVE-2015-0209 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0209]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSL could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on the system, caused by a use-after-free error in the d2i_ECPrivateKey or EVP_PKCS82PKEY function. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt memory and execute arbitrary code on the system and cause a denial of service.
CVSS Base Score: 7.5
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/101674 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/101674] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:P/A:P)
- `E1.S5`: CVEID: CVE-2015-0286 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0286]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSL is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by an error in the ASN1_TYPE_cmp function when attempting to compare ASN.1 boolean types. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to crash any certificate verification operation and cause a denial of service.
CVSS Base Score: 5
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/101666 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/#/vulnerabilities/101666] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:N/I:N/A:P)
- `E1.S6`: CVEID: CVE-2015-0289 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2015-0289]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSL is vulnerable to a denial of service, caused by the failure to properly handle missing outer ContentInfo by the PKCS#7 parsing code. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability using a malformed ASN.1-encoded PKCS#7 blob to trigger a NULL pointer dereference.
CVSS Base Score: 5

- `E4.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E4.S2`: SUMMARY
 OpenSSL vulnerabilities were disclosed on September 22 and 26, 2016 by the OpenSSL Project. OpenSSL is used by HP SSL on HP OpenVMS. IBM WebSphere MQ on OpenVMS Alpha and Itanium uses HP SSL and has addressed the applicable CVE ( CVE-2016-2183 ) known as “SWEET32 Birthday attack" .
- `E4.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2016-2183 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-2183]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSL could allow a remote attacker to obtain sensitive information, caused by an error in the in the Triple-DES on 64-bit block cipher, used as a part of the SSL/TLS protocol. By capturing large amounts of encrypted traffic between the SSL/TLS server and the client, a remote attacker able to conduct a man-in-the-middle attack could exploit this vulnerability to recover the plaintext data and obtain sensitive information. This vulnerability is known as the SWEET32 Birthday attack.
CVSS Base Score: 3.7
CVSS Temporal Score: See https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/116337 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/116337] for the current score
CVSS Environmental Score*: Undefined
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
- `E4.S4`: AFFECTED PRODUCTS AND VERSIONS
The vulnerability affects version 6.0 of IBM WebSphere MQ on OpenVMS Alpha & Itanium.
- `E4.S5`: REMEDIATION/FIXES
- `E4.S6`: Product VRMF APAR Remediation/First Fix IBM WebSphere MQ on OpenVMS Alpha and Itanium. 
6.0.2.13 IT18095 Download from Fix Central [http://www.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/quickorder?parent=ibm%2FWebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/WebSphere+MQ&release=All&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=IT18095&source=fc] 
On HP OpenVMS, IBM MQ V6.0.2.13 is a pre-requisite for applying the fix , refer to APAR IT18095 for additional details on the fix. WORKAROUNDS AND MITIGATIONS
None

- `E5.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E5.S2`: SUMMARY
 There is a potential bypass security restriction vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server. This will only occur in environments that have the webcontainer custom property HttpSessionIdReuse enabled. There is a potential denial of service with IBM WebSphere Application Server when using SIP services. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty could allow a remote attacker to conduct phishing attacks, caused by an open redirect vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to redirect a victim to arbitrary Web sites. IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty is vulnerable to cross-site scripting in OpenID Connect clients caused by improper validation of input. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability using a specially-crafted URL to execute script in a victim's Web browser within the security context of the hosting Web site, once the URL is clicked. An attacker could use this vulnerability to steal the victim's cookie-based authentication credentials. There is an Information Disclosure Vulnerability in IBM WebSphere Application Server Liberty. Apache Commons Fileupload vulnerability affects WebSphere Application Server. There is a potential information disclosure in WebSphere Application Server.
- `E5.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2016-0385 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-0385]
DESCRIPTION: IBM WebSphere Application Server could allow a remote attacker to bypass security restrictions caused by a buffer overflow. This could allow the attacker to view unauthorized data.

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
An authenticated user with queue-manager permissions could trigger a segmentation fault; normal operations might require rebooting the machine. The CVSS base score is 5.3, with vector CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H. [E2.S3]

Affected versions are IBM MQ V9.0.0.0 in the V9.0 Long Term Support Release and IBM MQ V8.0.0.0 through V8.0.0.5 maintenance levels. [E2.S4] [E2.S5] [E2.S6] [E2.S7]

For remediation, apply maintenance level 9.0.0.1 for the V9.0 Long Term Support Release or 8.0.0.6 for IBM MQ V8.0. [E2.S8] [E2.S9] [E2.S10] [E2.S11]

You can find related IBM security information through the IBM Secure Engineering Web Portal and the IBM Product Security Incident Response Blog; the bulletin also provides a Japanese translation link. [E2.S16] [E2.S20]

- `E1.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E1.S2`: SUMMARY
 An administration command can cause IBM MQ to access an invalid memory address, leading to a segmentation failure and causing the queue manager to become unresponsive.
- `E1.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
CVEID: CVE-2016-8971 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-8971]
DESCRIPTION: IBM MQ could allow an authenticated user with queue manager permissions to cause a segmentation fault. This would result in the machine needing to be rebooted to resume normal operations.

- `E2.S1`: SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E2.S2`: SUMMARY
 OpenSSLプロジェクトから、OpenSSLの脆弱性が2016年9月22日、26日に公開されました。
IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security はIBM i プラットフォーム上でのみ、OpenSSLを使用しています。
このため IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security はこれらのCVEの影響を受けます。
- `E2.S3`: 最新の情報については下記の文書（英語）をご参照ください。 
Security Bulletin: Vulnerabilities in OpenSSL affect IBM WebSphere MQ Advanced Message Security (CVE-2016-2177, CVE-2016-2178)
http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21999724 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21999724]
- `E2.S4`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
- `E2.S5`: CVEID: CVE-2016-2177 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-2177] 
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSLはサービス拒否を引き起こす脆弱性を含んでいます。
これはヒープ・バッファーのバウンダリー・チェックで用いられる、ポインタ演算子の不正な利用によって引き起こされます。
予期しないmallocを使用することで、リモートの攻撃者はこの脆弱性を悪用してintegerのオーバーフローを引き起こし、アプリケーションをクラッシュさせることができます。
CVSS Base Score: 5.9
CVSS Temporal Score: 現時点のスコアは以下のサイトを参照してください。https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113890 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113890] 
CVSS Environmental Score*: 未定義
CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)
- `E2.S6`: CVEID: CVE-2016-2178 [http://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2016-2178]
DESCRIPTION: OpenSSLはDSA実装に含まれるエラーによって、リモート攻撃者に重要な情報を与えてしまう可能性があります。このエラーは特定の操作を不特定の時間に許すため、攻撃者はこの脆弱性を悪用してキャッシュタイミング攻撃を使用し、DSA秘密鍵を取得することが可能です
CVSS Base Score: 5.3
CVSS Temporal Score: 現時点のスコアは以下のサイトを参照してください。 https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113889 [https://exchange.xforce.ibmcloud.com/vulnerabilities/113889]

- `E3.S1`: WMB IIB SECURITY BULLETIN
- `E3.S2`: SUMMARY
 Multiple security vulnerabilities exist in the IBM® Runtime Environment Java™ Technology Edition Version 6 Service Refresh 16 Fix Pack 41 and earlier releases used by WebSphere Message Broker, and the IBM® Runtime Environment Java™ Technology Edition Version 7 Service Refresh 10 Fix Pack 1 and earlier releases used by WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus, and the IBM® Runtime Environment Java™ Technology Edition Version 7R1 Service Refresh 4 Fix Pack 1 and earlier releases used by IBM Integration Bus. These issues were disclosed as part of the IBM Java SDK updates in April 2017. WebSphere Message Broker and IBM Integration Bus have addressed the applicable CVEs
- `E3.S3`: VULNERABILITY DETAILS
If you run your own Java code using the IBM Java Runtime delivered with this product, you should evaluate your code to determine whether the complete list of vulnerabilities are applicable to your code. For a complete list of vulnerabilities, refer to the “IBM Java SDK Security Bulletin”, located in the References section for more information.

Visible answer:
The bulletin explains that an IBM MQ administration command can access an invalid memory address, causing a segmentation failure and making the queue manager unresponsive. [E1.S2]

CVE-2016-8971 affects authenticated users with queue manager permissions; exploitation can cause a segmentation fault and require a machine reboot. The CVSS base score is 5.3. [E1.S3]

Affected versions are IBM MQ V9.0.0.0 and IBM MQ V8.0.0.0 through V8.0.0.5. [E1.S4] [E1.S5] [E1.S6] [E1.S7]

For IBM MQ V9.0 LTS, apply maintenance level 9.0.0.1; for IBM MQ V8.0, apply maintenance level 8.0.0.6. [E1.S8] [E1.S9] [E1.S10] [E1.S11]

You can find related security information through IBM’s Secure Engineering Web Portal and Product Security Incident Response Blog. The bulletin also links to the CVE record and IBM X-Force page for the current CVSS temporal score. [E1.S3] [E1.S16]

### techqa_DEV_Q266#row-0025

Question: How to install Packaging utility? How to install Packaging utility? 

Reference / gold answer:
To install Packaging Utility, you can follow these steps:

1. Download the fix pack from the provided download URL.
2. Extract the compressed file in an appropriate directory, such as C:\temp.
3. Add the fix pack's repository location in IBM Installation Manager by browsing to the extracted directory.
4. Start IBM Installation Manager and go to File > Preferences > Repositories.
5. Click on Add Repository and enter the file path to the extracted directory.
6. Close the Preferences page.
7. If IBM Packaging Utility is already installed, click on Update Packages on the Installation Manager start page and follow the wizard to update it.
8. If IBM Packaging Utility is not installed, click on Install Packages on the Installation Manager start page and follow the wizard to install it.

- `E1.S46`: DEFINITIONS
Regression: An error in the Maintenance Delivery Vehicle [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27008656] (MDV) that produces incorrect or unexpected behavior causing a supported feature to stop functioning as designed. 
This includes:
- `E1.S47`: * Coding errors that cause a regression
 * Documentation or packaging problems that cause a regression
 * Errors reported in a new function delivered in a MDV that cause a regression
- `E1.S48`: Incomplete: An error in the MDV has not regressed, but does not work as designed. 
This includes:
- `E1.S49`: * Fixed APARs which did not solve the original problem but did not break anything new
 * APARs reporting documentation errors, such as readme errors, that cause problems applying an MDV but do not lead to a regression
- `E1.S50`: Notes:  * Regression and incomplete APARs are considered fix-in-error or MDV-in-error
 * Definitions above apply only to valid APARs that result in product fixes (APARs returned as working-as-designed are not assessed for being fix-in-error)
 * Issues in major releases due to new functionality do not apply in this definition
- `E1.S51`: There are no known regressions to report.

- `E3.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 You install IBM Packaging Utility on a Linux x86 64-bit computer. You cannot start Packaging Utility. The version of Packaging Utility that you are using requires 32-bit library support when you install with a 64-bit version of IBM Installation Manager.
- `E3.S3`: SYMPTOM
Different symptoms occur depending on the version of Linux and shells that you use.
- `E3.S4`: * No feedback when you start Packaging Utility.
- `E3.S5`: You start Packaging Utility from a Terminal window running a shell, and change the directory to the installation location of the IBMPU executable. You execute IBMPU. The command returns without providing feedback: 
$ cd /opt/IBM/PackgingUtility
$ ./IBMPU
$
- `E3.S6`: * You receive the message: "no such file or directory"
- `E3.S7`: $ ./IBMPU
bash ./IBMPU no such file or directory
$
- `E3.S8`: * You receive the message: "bad ELF interpreter"
- `E3.S9`: $./IBMPU
./IBMPU bash: ./install: /lib/ld-linux.so.2: bad ELF interpreter: No such file or directory
- `E3.S10`: * Check if Packaging Utility is 32-bit
- `E3.S11`: Use the file command to identify a 32-bit executable:
- `E3.S12`: $ file ./IBMPU
./IBMPU: ELF 32-bit LSB executable, Intel 80386, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked (uses shared libs), for GNU/Linux 2.2.5, not stripped
- `E3.S13`: * Test the 32-bit Java Runtime Environment (JRE)
- `E3.S14`: The IBMPU executable invokes a program written in Java. Verify that the 32-bit JRE does not run by changing to the jre folder and executing the java command with the -version parameter. Similar results as executing the ./IBMPU are shown: 
$ cd /opt/IBM/PackgingUtility/jre/bin
$ ./java
bash: ./java no such file or directory
$ file ./java
./java: ELF 32-bit LSB executable, Intel 80386, version 1 (SYSV), dynamically linked (uses shared libs), for GNU/Linux 2.2.5, not stripped
- `E3.S15`: CAUSE
The required 32-bit libraries are not installed on the computer.
- `E3.S16`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
To work around this issue, take one of the following actions:
- `E3.S17`: * Install a new instance of Packaging Utility version 1.6 and select the 64-bit package group.
- `E3.S18`: * Install the 32-bit libraries that are required to support a 32-bit program
- `E3.S19`: The same techniques for resolving the Installation Manager issues also apply to the Packaging Utility, see Technote #1438776 Issues starting or running Installation Manager [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438776]. 
RELATED INFORMATION
#Issues starting or running Installation Manager [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg21438776]

- `E1.S27`: The installer package for Packaging Utility is pu.offering.disk.platform_version.zip where platform indicates the operating system and version indicates the version of Packaging Utility. The installer package contains files for only one platform. Using this package, you can install Packaging Utility and Installation Manager by running the install command. You can also add this package as a repository in Installation Manager and use the package to update Packaging Utility.

- `E1.S46`: DEFINITIONS
Regression: An error in the Maintenance Delivery Vehicle [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg27008656] (MDV) that produces incorrect or unexpected behavior causing a supported feature to stop functioning as designed. 
This includes:
- `E1.S47`: * Coding errors that cause a regression
 * Documentation or packaging problems that cause a regression
 * Errors reported in a new function delivered in a MDV that cause a regression
- `E1.S48`: Incomplete: An error in the MDV has not regressed, but does not work as designed. 
This includes:
- `E1.S49`: * Fixed APARs which did not solve the original problem but did not break anything new
 * APARs reporting documentation errors, such as readme errors, that cause problems applying an MDV but do not lead to a regression
- `E1.S50`: Notes:  * Regression and incomplete APARs are considered fix-in-error or MDV-in-error
 * Definitions above apply only to valid APARs that result in product fixes (APARs returned as working-as-designed are not assessed for being fix-in-error)
 * Issues in major releases due to new functionality do not apply in this definition
- `E1.S51`: There are no known regressions to report.

   This issue affects users of the GSKit included with MQ 8.0.0.0
   and MQ 8.0.0.4.
   This issue does not affect users of the GSKit included with MQ
   8.0.0.1 through MQ 8.0.0.3.

   MultiPlatform

You can track all active APARs for this component.
- `E5.S3`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E5.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Customers using runmqckm or amqtcert on Windows systems may
   find that they are unable to migrate or import some SSL
   certificates when WMQ 6.0.2.1 is installed.
- `E5.S5`: The most likely error message is "the specified database has
   been corrupted", for a certificate which can be imported
   using a version of WMQ prior to 6.0.2.1.
- `E5.S6`: LOCAL FIX
- `E5.S7`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   Customers using WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows who need to import or
   migrate certificates using keys over a certain size.
- `E5.S8`: Platforms affected:
   Windows
- `E5.S9`: ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows uses a Java runtime environment to run
   the GSkit SSL certificate administration commands (amqtcert,
   runmqckm/gsk7cmd). The Java runtime has some JCE policy files
   which control what strength of cryptography is permitted for use
   with GSkit administration commands.
- `E5.S10`: 6.0.2.1 erroneously shipped an incorrect set of JCE policy
   files. Instead of shipping the unlimited strength files (as with
   previous fixpacks), only the standard files were shipped. This
   prevents certain certificates with large keys from being
   imported or migrated.
- `E5.S11`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  WMQ for Windows has been changed such that the correct policy
   files will be shipped in future fixpacks. Meanwhile, 6.0.2.1
   users affected by this issue may use the following work-around:
- `E5.S12`: 1. Download the unrestricted Java policy files (or obtain
   them from a WMQ 6 version before 6.0.2.1). The relevant files
   are local_policy.jar and US_export_policy.jar and they are
   installed by default in C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere
   MQ\gskit\jre\lib\security
- `E5.S13`: 2. Replace the two 6.0.2.1 gskit\jre\lib\security policy
   files with the unrestricted ones obtained in step 1.
- `E5.S14`: The certificate administration command will then work the same
   as in previous versions.
- `E5.S15`: ---------------------------------------------------------------
   The fix is targeted for delivery in the following PTFs:
- `E5.S16`: v6.0
   Platform           Fix Pack 6.0.2.2
   --------           --------------------
   Windows            U200270

Status: `ANSWER_STATE_VALID`; visible: `True`

Visible answer:
WebSphere MQ V7.0 included Java 5.0 Service Refresh 16 Fix Pack 8 (SR16-FP8). The corresponding maintenance level was V7.0.1.13. [E2.S5] [E2.S11] [E2.S12] [E2.S16]

A later update for WebSphere MQ V7.1 and V7.5 specified platform-dependent Java levels: Java 6.0 SR16-FP26 (6.0.16.26) on AIX, Linux x86-32/x86-64, Linux PPC64, zLinux, and Windows; SR16-FP22 (6.0.16.22) on HP-UX IA32/IA64; and SR16-FP25 (6.0.16.25) on Solaris x86-64/SPARC. [E3.S11] [E3.S12]

WebSphere MQ V8.0 included platform-dependent Java levels: Java 7.1 SR3-FP40 (7.1.3.40) on AIX, Linux x86-32/x86-64, Linux PPC64LE, zLinux, and Windows 32-/64-bit; Java 7.0 SR9-FP32 (7.0.9.32) on HP-UX IA32/IA64; and Java 7.0 SR9-FP40 (7.0.9.40) on Solaris x86-64/SPARC. [E3.S13] [E3.S14]

The supplied JRE was used by Java components including the GSKit graphical interface and WebSphere MQ Explorer; in some releases it also supported Managed File Transfer and the MQXR service. [E1.S8] [E1.S9] [E3.S7] [E3.S8] [E2.S8] [E2.S9]

You can track all active APARs for this component.
- `E4.S3`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  Customers using runmqckm or amqtcert on Windows systems may
   find that they are unable to migrate or import some SSL
   certificates when WMQ 6.0.2.1 is installed.
- `E4.S5`: The most likely error message is "the specified database has
   been corrupted", for a certificate which can be imported
   using a version of WMQ prior to 6.0.2.1.
- `E4.S6`: LOCAL FIX
- `E4.S7`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   USERS AFFECTED:
   Customers using WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows who need to import or
   migrate certificates using keys over a certain size.
- `E4.S8`: Platforms affected:
   Windows
- `E4.S9`: ****************************************************************
   PROBLEM SUMMARY:
   WMQ 6.0.2.1 for Windows uses a Java runtime environment to run
   the GSkit SSL certificate administration commands (amqtcert,
   runmqckm/gsk7cmd). The Java runtime has some JCE policy files
   which control what strength of cryptography is permitted for use
   with GSkit administration commands.
- `E4.S10`: 6.0.2.1 erroneously shipped an incorrect set of JCE policy
   files. Instead of shipping the unlimited strength files (as with
   previous fixpacks), only the standard files were shipped. This
   prevents certain certificates with large keys from being
   imported or migrated.
- `E4.S11`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  WMQ for Windows has been changed such that the correct policy
   files will be shipped in future fixpacks. Meanwhile, 6.0.2.1
   users affected by this issue may use the following work-around:
- `E4.S12`: 1. Download the unrestricted Java policy files (or obtain
   them from a WMQ 6 version before 6.0.2.1). The relevant files
   are local_policy.jar and US_export_policy.jar and they are
   installed by default in C:\Program Files\IBM\WebSphere
   MQ\gskit\jre\lib\security
- `E4.S13`: 2. Replace the two 6.0.2.1 gskit\jre\lib\security policy
   files with the unrestricted ones obtained in step 1.
- `E4.S14`: The certificate administration command will then work the same
   as in previous versions.
- `E4.S15`: ---------------------------------------------------------------
   The fix is targeted for delivery in the following PTFs:
- `E4.S16`: v6.0
   Platform           Fix Pack 6.0.2.2
   --------           --------------------
   Windows            U200270

### techqa_DEV_Q278#row-0115

Question: Can I change the UUID value on the Messaging Engine? After dropping the SIB object, a new UUID value was generated for the new SIB object. However, the messaging application points to the old UUID value.
Is it possible to change the new UUID value back to the old value?

Reference / gold answer:
No, it is not possible to change the UUID value on the Messaging Engine. Once a new UUID is generated for an object, it cannot be changed back to an old value. In this case, the messaging application would need to be updated to point to the new UUID value for the new SIB object.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `1b`:  The messaging engine XXXXYYYYZZZ cannot be started as there is no runtime
- `1c`: initialized for it yet, retry the operation once it has initialized. CAUSE
- `1d`: By looking at the systemout.log, we have something like: .
- `1e`: [6/24/14 15:05:32:488 EDT] 0000001e SibMessage E [XXXXYYYYZZZ] CWSIS1561E: The messaging engine's unique id does not match that found in the file store. ME_UUID=BPE98764B8E93CB4, ME_UUID(FS)=4587F87990047458 .
- `1f`: These are the messaging engine UUID mismatch scenarios: . .
- `1g`: 1) When the data store or file store of different messaging engine is pointed to the current one. .
- `1h`: 2) A backup of the data store or file store taken at an earlier time was restored. .
- `1i`: 3) You have deleted the messaging engine and recreated the Messaging Engine with the same name and trying to use the previous file store which was associated with the old messaging engine(UUID). ANSWER
- `1j`: To resolve the issue you will have to delete the file store for this Messaging Engine: . XXXXYYYYZZZ .
- `1k`: Delete the existing file stores for this messaging engine and restart the JVM.
- `1l`: This action will create the new file store for the new UUID's.
- `1m`: Note1: You must treat the log file, the temporary store file, and the permanent store file as one unit; that is, delete operation must be performed on all three files.
- `1n`: Note2:By performing the suggested action, all the messages in the filestore will be lost. RELATED INFORMATION

- `E1.S3`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  When a destination is created while an server is active, but the
   messaging engine for that application server is stopped, the
   dynamic reload logic does not add that destination to the
   internal state of the messaging engine.
   When the messaging engine is later started (due to a failover in
   this case), a CWSIP0062E message is outputted, and the
   destination cannot be accessed.
   When the whole application server is restarted, the knowledge
   of all destinations for the messaging engine is reloaded, and
   the destination becomes available again.
- `E1.S4`: LOCAL FIX
 *  Restart the application server where the CWSIP0062E message
   is logged.
- `E1.S5`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: Users of the default messaging provider for  *
   *                 WebSphere Application Server V6.0            *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: If a destination is created while a     *
   *                      messaging engine is stopped, but the    *
   *                      application server that hosts it is     *
   *                      running, then a CWSIP0062E error is     *
   *                      seen in the logs on startup of the      *
   *                      messaging engine, and the destination   *
   *                      cannot be accessed.                     *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   In a failover environment, it is common for a messaging engine
   for a bus not to be running within a particular application
   server, even though the application server itself is active.
- `E1.S6`: If a new destination is created in the bus, and dynamic
   configuration reload is enabled for that bus, the SIBus service
   of all application servers which can host messaging engines are
   informed of the change.
- `E1.S7`: However, in the case where a messaging engine is inactive
   within an application server, this process was working
   incorrectly. Knowledge of bus destinations was not fully
   reloaded for the inactive messaging engine, causing the
   following error during messaging engine startup (for example
   after a failover):
- `E1.S8`: CWSIP0062E: The destination {0} with UUID {1} could not be
   recovered due to a possible WCCM configuration error
- `E1.S9`: After the messaging engine started, the destination could not
   be accessed by applications.
- `E1.S10`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  This APAR fixes the issue.

- `E4.S4`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  This APAR contains a fix to optimize how the workload
   management (WLM) component will compress and decompress data
   being sent betweenprocesses. This is designed to reduce
   compression overhead in large WebSphere Process Server or
   service integration bus (SIBus) topologies, specifically with
   a large number of destinations (more effective at 2,000 or more
   destinations). It addresses scenarios in which many clusters
   have been defined and one or more non-messaging engine (ME)
   clusters are restarted while the messaging engine cluster is
   running. A customer experiencing this may see the following:
- `E4.S5`: ThreadMonitor W   WSVR0605W: Thread
   "server.startup : 0" (00000038) has been active for 686179
   milliseconds and may be hung.  There is/are 1 thread(s) in total
   in the server that may be hung.
   at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method)
   at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:199)
   at
   com.ibm.ws.sib.jfapchannel.impl.ExchangeReceiveListener.waitToCo
   mplete(ExchangeReceiveListener.java:235)
- `E4.S6`: In addition this fixes a rare condition which could result in
   compressed data being lost.  This would only occur if a series
   of bytes to be compressed could not actually be compressed
   (every byte was unique). This would then cause a potential loss
   of data due to how WLM handled the uncompressed bytes.
- `E4.S7`: LOCAL FIX
- `E4.S8`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED:  IBM WebSphere Process Server users or users *
   *                  of IBM WebSphere Application Server with    *
   *                  service integration bus (SIBus)             *
   *                  configurations.                             *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: Workload management (WLM) Compressor    *
   *                      Fix and Enhancements                    *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   In scenarios in which many clusters have been defined
   and one or more non-ME clusters are restarted while the
   messaging engine cluster is running, a customer experiencing
   this may see the following:
- `E4.S9`: ThreadMonitor W   WSVR0605W: Thread
   "server.startup : 0" (00000038) has been active for 686179
   milliseconds and may be hung.  There is/are 1 thread(s) in total
   in the server that may be hung.
   at java.lang.Object.wait(Native Method)
   at java.lang.Object.wait(Object.java:199)
   at
   com.ibm.ws.sib.jfapchannel.impl.ExchangeReceiveListener.waitToCo
   mplete(ExchangeReceiveListener.java:235)
- `E4.S10`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  This APAR contains a fix to optimize how the WLM component
   will compress and decompress data being sent between
   processes. This is designed to reduce compression overhead in
   large WPS/SIB topologies, specifically with a large number of
   destinations (more effective at 2,000 or more destinations).
- `E4.S11`: In addition this fixes a rare condition which could result in
   compressed data being lost.  This would only occur if a series
   of bytes to be compressed could not actually be compressed
   (every byte was unique).
- `E4.S12`: compress and decompress data being sent between
   processes. This is designed to reduce compression overhead in
   large WPS/SIB topologies, specifically with a large number of
   destinations (more effective at 2,000 or more destinations).
- `E4.S13`: In addition this fixes a rare condition which could result in
   compressed data being lost.  This would only occur if a series
   of bytes to be compressed could not actually be compressed
   (every byte was unique). This would then cause a potential loss
   of data due to how WLM handled the uncompressed bytes.
- `E4.S14`: Although it is not recommended, the compression optimizations
   can be removed and the code reverted back to the prior code if
   problems are seen by setting a cell level custom property:
- `E4.S15`: In the administrative console, go to the Custom properties
   page for the cell.
- `E4.S16`: System administration > Cell >  cell_name, and then, under
   Additional Properties, click Custom Properties
- `E4.S17`: Create a new custom property with a name of:
- `E4.S18`: IBM_CLUSTER_USE_LEGACY_COMPRESSOR
- `E4.S19`: and a value of true.  Save, Synchronize the nodes and restart
   all of the processes in the cell to pick up this change.
- `E4.S20`: The fix for this APAR is currently targeted for inclusion in
   fix packs 6.1.0.37 and 7.0.0.17.  Please refer to the
   Recommended Updates page for delivery information:
   http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980 [http://www.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?rs=180&uid=swg27004980]

- `E5.S1`: migrate datastore TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E5.S2`: QUESTION
 You can use ESXi with multiple datastores. How do you migrate the virtual machine template, which is created by the Image Construction and Composition Tool for IBM SmartCloud Orchestrator, from one datastore to another datastore?
- `E5.S3`: ANSWER
You can use one of the following methods to migrate the virtual machine template:
- `E5.S4`: * Move the datastore within the same VMware region
   Do not move, delete, or clone the image. Just change the datastore using VMware. You do not need to register the image again.
- `E5.S5`: * Move datastore 1 (DS1) to datastore 2 (DS2) across VMware region server 1 (RS1) to region server 2 (RS2).  1. Identify the image (IM1) in glance. Look for a property called metadata. The property contains the UUID of the ISO image, which contains the metadata. You can find the ISO file as /var/lib/glance/images/<image-uuid> on region server 1 (RS1).
- `E5.S6`: 2. Clone the image (IM1) from datastore (DS1) on region server 1 (RS1) to datastore (DS2) on region server 1 (RS2). For this example, use IM2 as the name for this second image. You can use both vmotion or the reference repository check in and check out.
- `E5.S7`: 3. Create a new image in glance region server (RS2), pass it the ISO files that were copied from step 1, and take note of the UUID.
- `E5.S8`: 4. Create or update the glance metadata image property for the image (IM2) to the UUID value that was noted in the previous step.
- `E5.S9`: 5. Register the cloned image (IM2) in IBM SmartCloud Orchestrator

Visible answer:
The documented resolution is to delete the existing file stores for the messaging engine and restart the JVM; this creates a new file store for the new UUID. The log file, temporary store file, and permanent store file must be deleted together, and messages in the file store will be lost. [E2.S5] [E2.S6] [E2.S7]

- `E1.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
- `E1.S2`: QUESTION
 The messaging engine XXXXYYYYZZZ cannot be started as there is no runtime
initialized for it yet, retry the operation once it has initialized.
- `E1.S3`: CAUSE
By looking at the systemout.log, we have something like:
.
- `E1.S4`: [6/24/14 15:05:32:488 EDT] 0000001e SibMessage E [XXXXYYYYZZZ] CWSIS1561E: The messaging engine's unique id does not match that found in the file store. ME_UUID=BPE98764B8E93CB4, ME_UUID(FS)=4587F87990047458
.
These are the messaging engine UUID mismatch scenarios: 
. 
. 
1) When the data store or file store of different messaging engine is pointed to the current one. 
. 
2) A backup of the data store or file store taken at an earlier time was restored. 
. 
3) You have deleted the messaging engine and recreated the Messaging Engine with the same name and trying to use the previous file store which was associated with the old messaging engine(UUID).
- `E1.S5`: ANSWER
To resolve the issue you will have to delete the file store for this Messaging Engine: .
- `E1.S6`: XXXXYYYYZZZ 
. 
Delete the existing file stores for this messaging engine and restart the JVM. 
This action will create the new file store for the new UUID's.
- `E1.S7`: Note1: You must treat the log file, the temporary store file, and the permanent store file as one unit; that is, delete operation must be performed on all three files.
Note2:By performing the suggested action, all the messages in the filestore will be lost.
- `E1.S8`: RELATED INFORMATION
 Deleting files following removal of a messaging engine [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/SSAW57_7.0.0/com.ibm.websphere.nd.multiplatform.doc/info/ae/ae/tjm1060_.html]
- `E2.S1`: SUBSCRIBE
You can track all active APARs for this component.
- `E2.S2`: APAR STATUS
 * CLOSED AS PROGRAM ERROR.
- `E2.S3`: ERROR DESCRIPTION
 *  When a destination is created while an server is active, but the
   messaging engine for that application server is stopped, the
   dynamic reload logic does not add that destination to the
   internal state of the messaging engine.
   When the messaging engine is later started (due to a failover in
   this case), a CWSIP0062E message is outputted, and the
   destination cannot be accessed.
   When the whole application server is restarted, the knowledge
   of all destinations for the messaging engine is reloaded, and
   the destination becomes available again.
- `E2.S4`: LOCAL FIX
 *  Restart the application server where the CWSIP0062E message
   is logged.
- `E2.S5`: PROBLEM SUMMARY
 *  ****************************************************************
   * USERS AFFECTED: Users of the default messaging provider for  *
   *                 WebSphere Application Server V6.0            *
   ****************************************************************
   * PROBLEM DESCRIPTION: If a destination is created while a     *
   *                      messaging engine is stopped, but the    *
   *                      application server that hosts it is     *
   *                      running, then a CWSIP0062E error is     *
   *                      seen in the logs on startup of the      *
   *                      messaging engine, and the destination   *
   *                      cannot be accessed.                     *
   ****************************************************************
   * RECOMMENDATION:                                              *
   ****************************************************************
   In a failover environment, it is common for a messaging engine
   for a bus not to be running within a particular application
   server, even though the application server itself is active.
- `E2.S6`: If a new destination is created in the bus, and dynamic
   configuration reload is enabled for that bus, the SIBus service
   of all application servers which can host messaging engines are
   informed of the change.
- `E2.S7`: However, in the case where a messaging engine is inactive
   within an application server, this process was working
   incorrectly. Knowledge of bus destinations was not fully
   reloaded for the inactive messaging engine, causing the
   following error during messaging engine startup (for example
   after a failover):
- `E2.S8`: CWSIP0062E: The destination {0} with UUID {1} could not be
   recovered due to a possible WCCM configuration error
- `E2.S9`: After the messaging engine started, the destination could not
   be accessed by applications.
- `E2.S10`: PROBLEM CONCLUSION
 *  This APAR fixes the issue.
- `E2.S11`: TEMPORARY FIX

- `E4.S2`: Known issues 
Issue 1 Summary :
- `E4.S3`: Customers using IBM WebSphere Transformation Extender(WTX) version 8.4.1.2 who use native schema and choice sequence iterations are unable to access iterations of a particular sequence group.
- `E4.S4`: Resolution :
- `E4.S5`: The fix for this issue (APAR PI31636) is available in WTX v8.4.1.3.
- `E4.S6`: Issue 2
- `E4.S7`: Summary :
- `E4.S8`: Customers using IBM Integration Bus (IIB) version 9.0.0.x may experience the following BIP2930E error when deploying or restarting the broker.
- `E4.S9`: RecoverableException BIP2930E: A function or procedure was called but the value supplied for the ''cAppVer'' parameter was of type ''BOOLEAN'' but the function/procedure expects value of type ''CHARACTER'' Functions and procedures require an exact matching between the data type of values supplied as parameters and the data type in its definition.
- `E4.S10`: Resolution :
- `E4.S11`: The fix for this issue (IIB APAR IT06286) is available in IIB Maintenance Level 9.0.0.4.
- `E4.S12`: Issue 3
- `E4.S13`: Summary :
- `E4.S14`: Customers using IBM Integration Bus (IIB) version 9.0.0.3 may experience the following BIP2503E when executing customer flows if propagating from a node after exiting a FOR loop acting on a shared variable.
- `E4.S15`: RecoverableException BIP2503E: Propagate with a SHARED variable lock held by FOR statement.
- `E4.S16`: Resolution :
- `E4.S17`: The fix for this issue (IIB APAR IT07974) is available in IIB Maintenance Level 9.0.0.4.
- `E4.S18`: Issue 4
- `E4.S19`: Summary :
- `E4.S20`: Customers using IBM Integration Bus (IIB) version 9.0.0.5 may experience the following issue:
- `E4.S21`: If a user has a REFERENCE variable declared at the module or schema level which points at either OutputRoot, OutputLocalEnvironment or OutputExceptionList and performs a PROPAGATE without specifying DELETE NONE in a compute node then it is not defined what the REFERENCE variable will be left pointing at. After the PROPAGATE the Output trees are deleted and the REFERENCE variables should be reset to point at the root of the newly created trees.The module and schema level reference variables are not being reset and are thus left to point at the original syntax element which they were pointing at which will now have been reset leading to unexpected results.

### techqa_DEV_Q292#row-0058

Question: Content Engine System Health Page page doesn't reflect correctly, Fixed Content Advise and Storage Area showing unavailable. Content Engine System Health Page page doesn't reflect correctly, Fixed Content Advise and Storage Area showing unavailable. 

Reference / gold answer:
To resolve the issue of Content Engine Health Page not reflecting correctly and showing Fixed Content Devices and Storage Areas as unavailable, you should follow these steps:

1. Check the Content Engine Bootstrap User has Full Control on the Object Store and associated Storage Areas.
2. Right-click on the Object Store, choose Properties, select the All Properties radio button, view the Storage Area property name, and verify that the Security tab allows the Content Engine Bootstrap User has Full Control. 

Following these steps should correct the issue and ensure that the Content Engine Health Page displays the correct status for Fixed Content Devices and Storage Areas.

Reference relevant evidence:
- `2b`:  The Content Engine Health Page (http://<CEserver>:<port>/P8CE/Health ) provides the status for different areas of the FileNet P8 system.
- `2c`: When viewing the page, both the Fixed Content Devices and the Storage Areas may display red icons instead of checkmark green icons. SYMPTOM
- `2d`: Red icons are displayed next to the Fixed Content Devices and Storage Areas even though users can add and access content.
- `2e`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
- `2f`: The p8_server_error log may contain the following E_ACCESS_DENIED error:
- `2g`: yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss nnnnnn ENG FNRCE0241E - ERROR method name: postLoadSecurity principal name: <username> Global Transaction: false User Transaction: false Exception Info: The requester has insufficient access rights to perform the requested operation.
- `2h`: com.filenet.api.exception.EngineRuntimeException: E_ACCESS_DENIED: The requester has insufficient access rights to perform the requested operation. at com.filenet.engine.retrieve.IndependentClassRetriever.postLoadSecurity(IndependentClassRetriever.java:1390) at com.filenet.engine.retrieve.RetrieverClassBase.loadNonScalarProperties(RetrieverClassBase.java:633) at com.filenet.engine.retrieve.IndependentClassRetriever.loadNonScalarProperties(IndependentClassRetriever.java:1298) at com.filenet.engine.retrieve.IndependentClassRetriever.loadObject(IndependentClassRetriever.java:1119) ...
- `2i`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM  1.
- `2j`: Verify the Content Engine Bootstrap User has Full Control on the Object Store and all associated Storage Areas.  2.
- `2k`: Inspect Storage Area security by right-clicking on the Object Store  3. Choose Properties  4.
- `2l`: Select the All Properties radio button and view the Storage Area property name  5.
- `2m`: Click on the drop down list to select the Storage Area.  6.
- `2n`: The Storage Area properties screen will appear.  7.
- `2o`: Verify the Security tab allows the Content Engine Bootstrap User has Full Control.

- `E4.S1`: CLOSE_WAIT; CORBA.NO_RESPONSE; iiop connection refused; ce client connection failed TECHNOTE (TROUBLESHOOTING)
- `E4.S2`: PROBLEM(ABSTRACT)
 Attempts to connect to a P8 Content Engine from any CE client (e.g. ICN, ICM, Workplace, WorkplaceXT) or custom client application, result in connection failures.
- `E4.S3`: SYMPTOM
There may be a number of different errors depending on the client application. For example:
- `E4.S4`: The Repository is not available.
- `E4.S5`: failed to establish connection using iiop://<server>:port/FileNet/Engine
- `E4.S6`: CORBA.NO_RESPONSE
- `E4.S7`: WebSphere may report ORB thread starvation or multiple ORB hung threads, for example:-
- `E4.S8`: WSVR0606W: Thread "ORB.thread.pool : 90" (000000e0) was previously reported to be hung but has completed. It was active for approximately 1626228 milliseconds. There is/are 4 thread(s) in total in the server that still may be hung.
- `E4.S9`: CAUSE
Excessive load balancer health monitor calls against the default WebSphere EJB port may use all available ORB threads and may leave TCP connections in the CLOSE_WAIT state, resulting in connection failures from other clients.
- `E4.S10`: ENVIRONMENT
High availability IBM FileNet P8 Content Engine load balanced farm.
- `E4.S11`: DIAGNOSING THE PROBLEM
Check the WebSphere systemout.log for messages relating to hung threads or thread starvation.
Use netstat to collect information about port usage and remote connections.
Collect the load balancer health monitor configurations for all target P8 CE ports.
- `E4.S12`: RESOLVING THE PROBLEM
Review the following points in order to prevent this problem from occurring:
- `E4.S13`: * Avoid using a health monitor against the EJB/bootstrap port. 
 * The preferred load balancer health monitor for P8 Content Engine is to use the CE start-up context page, also known as the CE ping page. This should be configured against the HTTP port: 
   http://<<server>>:<<port>>/FileNet/Engine 
 * A typical load balancer HTTP health monitor configuration will only require the context path string:
   /FileNet/Engine 
 * The monitor interval should be set to the largest practical time interval, typically greater than 5 seconds. and a time-out value of not less than 15 seconds. 
 * The Content Engine application server instance will need to be re-started to close the accumulated open connections.
- `E4.S14`: Cross reference information Segment Product Component Platform Version Edition Application Servers WebSphere Application Server
- `E5.S1`: TECHNOTE (FAQ)
